yayā samohitaṃ sarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ pañcamo yuddhakhaṇḍe
2.5.d:
महाप्रभोश्च लीलेयं शङ्करस्य परात्मनः ।
यया समोहितं सर्वं सदेवासुरमानुषम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां पञ्चमो युद्धखण्डे

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
tadā devagaṇāḥ sarve dānavaiśca parājitāḥ |
dudruvurbhayabhītāśca śastrāstrakṣatavigrahāḥ ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
तदा देवगणाः सर्वे दानवैश्च पराजिताः ।
दुद्रुवुर्भयभीताश्च शस्त्रास्त्रक्षतविग्रहाः ॥
2.5.m:
Sanatkumāra said: / Thus and in many other words, based on the Śruti and Smṛti, / Śaṅkara spoke to him, imparting supreme knowledge.

Sanatkumāra said:
Then all the hosts of gods, defeated by the Dānavas,
fled in terror, their bodies wounded by weapons and missiles.

2.5.s:
te parāvṛtya viśveśaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ |
trāhi trāhīti sarveśetyūcurvihvalayā girā ||
2.5.d:
ते परावृत्य विश्वेशं शङ्करं शरणं ययुः ।
त्राहि त्राहीति सर्वेशेत्यूचुर्विह्वलया गिरा ॥
2.5.m:
Turning back, they took refuge with Śaṅkara, the lord of the universe,
and said in agitated voices: "Save us! Save us, O Lord of All!"

2.5.s:
dṛṣṭvā parājayaṃ teṣāṃ devādīnāṃ sa śaṅkaraḥ |
sabhayaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā kopamuccaiścakāra ha ||
2.5.d:
दृष्ट्वा पराजयं तेषां देवादीनां स शङ्करः ।
सभयं वचनं श्रुत्वा कोपमुच्चैश्चकार ह ॥
2.5.m:
Seeing the defeat of the gods and the others,
and hearing their fearful words, Śaṅkara displayed intense anger.

2.5.s:
nirīkṣya sa kṛpādṛṣṭyā devebhyaścābhayaṃ dadau |
balaṃ ca svagaṇānāṃ vai varddhayāmāsa tejasā ||
2.5.d:
निरीक्ष्य स कृपादृष्ट्या देवेभ्यश्चाभयं ददौ ।
बलं च स्वगणानां वै वर्द्धयामास तेजसा ॥
2.5.m:
Gazing with an eye of compassion, he granted fearlessness to the gods,
and by his splendor increased the strength of his own attendants.

2.5.s:
śivājñaptastadā skando dānavānāṃ gaṇaiḥ saha |
yuyudhe nirbhayaḥ saṅkhye mahāvīro harātmajaḥ ||
2.5.d:
शिवाज्ञप्तस्तदा स्कन्दो दानवानां गणैः सह ।
युयुधे निर्भयः सङ्ख्ये महावीरो हरात्मजः ॥
2.5.m:
Then Skanda, commanded by Śiva, fearlessly fought in battle
with the hosts of Dānavas—the great hero, the son of Hara.

2.5.s:
kṛtvā krodhaṃ vīraśabdaṃ devo yastārakāntakaḥ |
akṣauhiṇīnāṃ śatakaṃ samare sa jaghāna ha ||
2.5.d:
कृत्वा क्रोधं वीरशब्दं देवो यस्तारकान्तकः ।
अक्षौहिणीनां शतकं समरे स जघान ह ॥
2.5.m:
Displaying anger and uttering a hero's roar, the god who is the slayer of Tāraka
slew a hundred akṣauhiṇīs in the battle.

2.5.s:
rudhiraṃ pātayāmāsa kālī kamalalocanā |
teṣāṃ śirāṃsi sañchidya babhakṣa sahasā ca sā ||
2.5.d:
रुधिरं पातयामास काली कमललोचना ।
तेषां शिरांसि सञ्छिद्य बभक्ष सहसा च सा ॥
2.5.m:
Lotus-eyed Kālī shed their blood;
severing their heads, she devoured them suddenly.

2.5.s:
papau raktāni teṣāṃ ca dānavānāṃ samantataḥ |
yuddhaṃ cakāra vividhaṃ suradānavabhīṣaṇam ||
2.5.d:
पपौ रक्तानि तेषां च दानवानां समन्ततः ।
युद्धं चकार विविधं सुरदानवभीषणम् ॥
2.5.m:
She drank the blood of those Dānavas all around,
and fought a varied battle, terrifying to gods and Dānavas.

2.5.s:
śatalakṣaṃ gajendrāṇāṃ dānavānāṃ tathā raṇe |
samādāyaikahastena mukhe cikṣepa līlayā ||
2.5.d:
शतलक्षं गजेन्द्राणां दानवानां तथा रणे ।
समादायैकहस्तेन मुखे चिक्षेप लीलया ॥
2.5.m:
Gathering up ten million lordly elephants and Dānavas in the fight
with a single hand, she tossed them into her mouth in sport.

2.5.s:
kabandhānāṃ sahasraṃ ca sannanarta raṇe bahu |
mahān kolāhalo jātaḥ klībānāṃ ca bhayaṅkaraḥ ||
2.5.d:
कबन्धानां सहस्रं च सन्ननर्त रणे बहु ।
महान् कोलाहलो जातः क्लीबानां च भयङ्करः ॥
2.5.m: And thousands of headless trunks danced profusely in the battle; / a great uproar arose, terrifying to cowards.

2.5.s:
punaḥ skandaḥ prakupyoccaiḥ śaravarṣāṃ cakāra ha |
pātayāmāsa kṣaṇataḥ koṭiśo'suranāyakān ||
2.5.d:
पुनः स्कन्दः प्रकुप्योच्चैः शरवर्षां चकार ह ।
पातयामास क्षणतः कोटिशोऽसुरनायकान् ॥
2.5.m: Then Skanda, becoming intensely enraged, sent down a shower of arrows; / in an instant he brought down asura leaders by the millions.

2.5.s:
dānavāḥ śarajālena skandasya kṣatavigrahāḥ |
bhītāḥ pradudruvuḥ sarve śeṣā maraṇatastadā ||
2.5.d:
दानवाः शरजालेन स्कन्दस्य क्षतविग्रहाः ।
भीताः प्रदुद्रुवुः सर्वे शेषा मरणतस्तदा ॥
2.5.m: Their bodies wounded by Skanda's net of arrows, / all the remaining Dānavas, terrified of death, fled.

2.5.s:
vṛṣaparvā vipracittirdaṇḍaścāpi vikampanaḥ |
skandena yuyudhuḥ sārddhaṃ tena sarve krameṇa ca ||
2.5.d:
वृषपर्वा विप्रचित्तिर्दण्डश्चापि विकम्पनः ।
स्कन्देन युयुधुः सार्द्धं तेन सर्वे क्रमेण च ॥
2.5.m: Vṛṣaparvan, Vipracitti, Daṇḍa, and Vikampana— / all of them fought in turn with that Skanda.

2.5.s:
mahāmārī ca yuyudhe na babhūva parāṅmukhī |
babhūvuste kṣatāṅgāśca skandaśaktiprapīḍitāḥ ||
2.5.d:
महामारी च युयुधे न बभूव पराङ्मुखी ।
बभूवुस्ते क्षताङ्गाश्च स्कन्दशक्तिप्रपीडिताः ॥
2.5.m: And Mahāmārī fought and did not turn back; / afflicted by Skanda's spear, their limbs were battered.

2.5.s:
mahāmārīskandayośca vijayo'bhūttadā mune |
nedurdundubhayaḥ svarge puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ papāta ha ||
2.5.d:
महामारीस्कन्दयोश्च विजयोऽभूत्तदा मुने ।
नेदुर्दुन्दुभयः स्वर्गे पुष्पवृष्टिः पपात ह ॥
2.5.m: Then, O sage, victory belonged to Mahāmārī and Skanda; / kettledrums sounded in heaven, and a shower of flowers fell.

2.5.s:
skandasya samaraṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāraudraṃ tamadbhutam |
dānavānāṃ kṣayakaraṃ yathā prakṛtikalpakam ||
2.5.d:
स्कन्दस्य समरं दृष्ट्वा महारौद्रं तमद्भुतम् ।
दानवानां क्षयकरं यथा प्रकृतिकल्पकम् ॥
2.5.m: Seeing Skanda's extremely dreadful and wondrous fight, / which caused the destruction of the Dānavas like the natural dissolution of an age,

2.5.s:
mahāmārīkṛtaṃ taccopadravaṃ kṣayahetukam |
cukopātīva sahasā sanaddho'bhūtsvayaṃ tadā ||
2.5.d:
महामारीकृतं तच्चोपद्रवं क्षयहेतुकम् ।
चुकोपातीव सहसा सनद्धोऽभूत्स्वयं तदा ॥
2.5.m: and that havoc wrought by Mahāmārī, which caused their ruin, / he suddenly grew exceedingly angry and equipped himself [for battle].

2.5.s:
varaṃ vimānamāruhya nānāśastrāstrasaṃyutam |
abhayaṃ sarvavīrāṇāṃ nānāratnaparicchadam ||
2.5.d:
वरं विमानमारुह्य नानाशस्त्रास्त्रसंयुतम् ।
अभयं सर्ववीराणां नानारत्नपरिच्छदम् ॥
2.5.m: Mounting an excellent aerial car furnished with various weapons and missiles, / which offered security to all warriors and was adorned with various jewels,

2.5.s:
mahāvīraiḥ śaṅkhacūḍo jagāma rathamadhyataḥ |
dhanurvikṛṣya karṇāntaṃ cakāra śaravarṣaṇam ||
2.5.d:
महावीरैः शङ्खचूडो जगाम रथमध्यतः ।
धनुर्विकृष्य कर्णान्तं चकार शरवर्षणम् ॥
2.5.m: Śaṅkhacūḍa went into the midst of the chariots accompanied by great heroes; / drawing his bow to his ear, he loosed a shower of arrows.

2.5.s:
tasya sā śaravṛṣṭiśca durnivāryā bhayaṅkarī |
mahāghorāndhakāraśca vadhasthāne babhūva ha ||
2.5.d:
तस्य सा शरवृष्टिश्च दुर्निवार्या भयङ्करी ।
महाघोरान्धकारश्च वधस्थाने बभूव ह ॥
2.5.m: Irresistible and terrifying was that shower of arrows of his; / and a deep, dreadful darkness arose over the killing ground.

2.5.s:
devāḥ pradudruvuḥ sarve ye'nye nandīśvarādayaḥ |
eka eva kārttikeyastasthau samaramūrddhani ||
2.5.d:
देवाः प्रदुद्रुवुः सर्वे येऽन्ये नन्दीश्वरादयः ।
एक एव कार्त्तिकेयस्तस्थौ समरमूर्द्धनि ॥
2.5.m: All the gods, along with Nandīśvara and the others, fled; / only Kārttikeya stood alone at the front of the battle.

2.5.s:
parvatānāṃ ca sarpāṇāṃ nāgānāṃ śākhināṃ tathā |
rājā cakāra vṛṣṭiṃ ca durnivāryāṃ bhayaṅkarīm ||
2.5.d:
पर्वतानां च सर्पाणां नागानां शाखिनां तथा ।
राजा चकार वृष्टिं च दुर्निवार्यां भयङ्करीम् ॥
2.5.m: A shower of mountains, serpents, elephants, and trees / the king released—irresistible and terrifying.

2.5.s:
taddṛṣṭyā prahataḥ skando babhūva śivanandanaḥ |
nīhāreṇa ca sāndreṇa saṃvṛto bhāskaro yathā ||
2.5.d:
तद्दृष्ट्या प्रहतः स्कन्दो बभूव शिवनन्दनः ।
नीहारेण च सान्द्रेण संवृतो भास्करो यथा ॥
2.5.m: Struck by his glance, Skanda, the son of Śiva, / became obscured like the sun enveloped in dense fog.

2.5.s:
nānāvidhāṃ svamāyāṃ ca cakāra mayadarśitām |
tāṃ nāvidan surāḥ ke'pi gaṇāśca munisattama ||
2.5.d:
नानाविधां स्वमायां च चकार मयदर्शिताम् ।
तां नाविदन् सुराः केऽपि गणाश्च मुनिसत्तम ॥
2.5.m: He displayed various kinds of illusory powers shown to him by Maya; / no gods nor attendants could comprehend them, O best of sages.

2.5.s:
tadaiva śaṅkhacūḍaśca mahāmāyī mahābalaḥ |
śareṇaikena divyena dhanuściccheda tasya vai ||
2.5.d:
तदैव शङ्खचूडश्च महामायी महाबलः ।
शरेणैकेन दिव्येन धनुश्चिच्छेद तस्य वै ॥
2.5.m: Just then, the mighty Śaṅkhacūḍa, a master of great illusions, / severed his bow with a single divine arrow.

2.5.s:
babhañja tadrathaṃ divyaṃ ciccheda ratharakṣakān |
mayūraṃ jarjarībhūtaṃ divyāstreṇa cakāra saḥ ||
2.5.d:
बभञ्ज तद्रथं दिव्यं चिच्छेद रथरक्षकान् ।
मयूरं जर्जरीभूतं दिव्यास्त्रेण चकार सः ॥
2.5.m: He shattered his divine chariot, slew the chariot guards, / and with a divine missile reduced his peacock to a mangled state.

2.5.s:
śaktiṃ cikṣepa sūryābhāṃ tasya vakṣasi ghātinīm |
mūrcchāmavāpa sahasā tatprahāreṇa sa kṣaṇam ||
2.5.d:
शक्तिं चिक्षेप सूर्याभां तस्य वक्षसि घातिनीम् ।
मूर्च्छामवाप सहसा तत्प्रहारेण स क्षणम् ॥
2.5.m: He hurled a deadly spear, radiant like the sun, at his chest; / struck by it, he suddenly fell into a swoon for a moment.

2.5.s:
punaśca cetanāṃ prāpya kārtikaḥ paravīrahā |
ratnendrasāranirmāṇamāruroha svavāhanam ||
2.5.d:
पुनश्च चेतनां प्राप्य कार्तिकः परवीरहा ।
रत्नेन्द्रसारनिर्माणमारुरोह स्ववाहनम् ॥
2.5.m: Regaining consciousness once more, Kārttikeya, the slayer of enemy warriors, / mounted his vehicle fashioned from the essence of the finest gems.

2.5.s:
smṛtvā pādau maheśasya sāmbikasya ca ṣaṇmukhaḥ |
śastrāstrāṇi gṛhītvaiva cakāra raṇamulbaṇam ||
2.5.d:
स्मृत्वा पादौ महेशस्य साम्बिकस्य च षण्मुखः ।
शस्त्रास्त्राणि गृहीत्वैव चकार रणमुल्बणम् ॥
2.5.m: Remembering the feet of the great lord accompanied by Ambikā, the six-faced god, / taking up weapons and missiles, waged a fierce battle.

2.5.s:
sarpāṃśca parvatāṃścaiva vṛkṣāṃśca prastarāṃstathā |
sarvāṃściccheda kopena divyāstreṇa śivātmajaḥ ||
2.5.d:
सर्पांश्च पर्वतांश्चैव वृक्षांश्च प्रस्तरांस्तथा ।
सर्वांश्चिच्छेद कोपेन दिव्यास्त्रेण शिवात्मजः ॥
2.5.m: The serpents, the mountains, the trees, and the rocks— / the son of Śiva angrily severed them all with a divine missile.

2.5.s:
vahniṃ nivārayāmāsa pārjanyena śareṇa ha |
rathaṃ dhanuśca ciccheda śaṅkhacūḍasya līlayā ||
2.5.d:
वह्निं निवारयामास पार्जन्येन शरेण ह ।
रथं धनुश्च चिच्छेद शङ्खचूडस्य लीलया ॥
2.5.m: He repelled the fire with a rain-cloud arrow, / and effortlessly shattered Śaṅkhacūḍa's chariot and bow,

2.5.s:
sannāhaṃ sarvavāhāṃśca kirīṭaṃ mukuṭojjvalam |
vīraśabdaṃ cakārāsau jagarja ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
2.5.d:
सन्नाहं सर्ववाहांश्च किरीटं मुकुटोज्ज्वलम् ।
वीरशब्दं चकारासौ जगर्ज च पुनः पुनः ॥
2.5.m: his armor, all his mounts, and his diadem radiant with a crest-jewel; / he raised a heroic shout and roared again and again.

2.5.s:
cikṣepa śaktiṃ sūryābhāṃ dānavendrasya vakṣasi |
tatprahāreṇa samprāpa mūrcchāṃ dīrghatamena ca ||
2.5.d:
चिक्षेप शक्तिं सूर्याभां दानवेन्द्रस्य वक्षसि ।
तत्प्रहारेण सम्प्राप मूर्च्छां दीर्घतमेन च ॥
2.5.m: He hurled a spear, radiant like the sun, at the chest of the lord of the Dānavas; / struck by it, he fell into a prolonged swoon.

2.5.s:
muhūrtamātraṃ tatkleśaṃ vinīya sa mahābalaḥ |
cetanāṃ prāpya cottasthau jagarja harivarcasaḥ ||
2.5.d:
मुहूर्तमात्रं तत्क्लेशं विनीय स महाबलः ।
चेतनां प्राप्य चोत्तस्थौ जगर्ज हरिवर्चसः ॥
2.5.m: Dispelling that distress within mere moments, that mighty [king], / possessing the brilliance of Viṣṇu, regained consciousness, stood up, and roared.

2.5.s:
śaktyā jaghāna taṃ cāpi kārtikeyaṃ mahābalam |
sa papāta mahīpṛṣṭhe'moghāṃ kurvan vidhipradām ||
2.5.d:
शक्त्या जघान तं चापि कार्तिकेयं महाबलम् ।
स पपात महीपृष्ठेऽमोघां कुर्वन् विधिप्रदाम् ॥
2.5.m: With his spear he struck mighty Kārttikeya in return; / he fell to the surface of the earth, fulfilling [the spear] bestowed by Brahmā as unerring.

2.5.s:
kālī gṛhītvā taṃ kroḍe nināya śivasannidhau |
jñānena taṃ śivaścāpi jīvayāmāsa līlayā ||
2.5.d:
काली गृहीत्वा तं क्रोडे निनाय शिवसन्निधौ ।
ज्ञानेन तं शिवश्चापि जीवयामास लीलया ॥
2.5.m: Kālī took him in her lap and brought him to Śiva's presence; / and Śiva, through his knowledge, revived him with ease.

2.5.s:
dadau balamanantaṃ ca samuttasthau pratāpavān |
gamanāya matiṃ cakre punastatra śivātmajaḥ ||
2.5.d:
ददौ बलमनन्तं च समुत्तस्थौ प्रतापवान् ।
गमनाय मतिं चक्रे पुनस्तत्र शिवात्मजः ॥
2.5.m: He gave him infinite strength, and the glorious son of Śiva stood up; / he resolved once more to go back there.

2.5.s:
etasminnantare vīro vīrabhadro mahābalaḥ |
śaṅkhacūḍena yuyudhe samare balaśālinā ||
2.5.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरो वीरभद्रो महाबलः ।
शङ्खचूडेन युयुधे समरे बलशालिना ॥
2.5.m: In the meantime, the heroic and mighty Vīrabhadra / fought in battle with the powerful Śaṅkhacūḍa.

2.5.s:
vavarṣa samare'strāṇi yāni yāni ca dānavaḥ |
ciccheda līlayā vīrastāni tāni nijaiḥ śaraiḥ ||
2.5.d:
ववर्ष समरेऽस्त्राणि यानि यानि च दानवः ।
चिच्छेद लीलया वीरस्तानि तानि निजैः शरैः ॥
2.5.m: Whatever missiles the Dānava rained down in battle, / the hero effortlessly severed each one with his own arrows.

2.5.s:
divyānyastrāṇi śataśo mumuce dānaveśvaraḥ |
tāni ciccheda taṃ bāṇairvīrabhadraḥ pratāpavān ||
2.5.d:
दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि शतशो मुमुचे दानवेश्वरः ।
तानि चिच्छेद तं बाणैर्वीरभद्रः प्रतापवान् ॥
2.5.m: The lord of the Dānavas released divine missiles by the hundreds; / glorious Vīrabhadra severed them and [struck] him with arrows.

2.5.s:
athātīva cukopoccaiḥ śaṅkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān |
śaktyā jaghānorasi taṃ sa cakampe papāta kau ||
2.5.d:
अथातीव चुकोपोच्चैः शङ्खचूडः प्रतापवान् ।
शक्त्या जघानोरसि तं स चकम्पे पपात कौ ॥
2.5.m: Then the glorious Śaṅkhacūḍa became exceedingly enraged; / he struck him on the chest with a spear, and [Vīrabhadra] trembled and fell to the earth.

2.5.s:
kṣaṇena cetanāṃ prāpya samuttasthau gaṇeśvaraḥ |
jagrāha ca dhanurbhūyo vīrabhadro gaṇāgraṇīḥ ||
2.5.d:
क्षणेन चेतनां प्राप्य समुत्तस्थौ गणेश्वरः ।
जग्राह च धनुर्भूयो वीरभद्रो गणाग्रणीः ॥
2.5.m: Regaining consciousness in a moment, the lord of the attendants stood up; / Vīrabhadra, the foremost among the attendants, took up his bow once more.

2.5.s:
etasminnantare kālī jagāma samaraṃ punaḥ |
bhakṣituṃ dānavān svāṃśca rakṣituṃ kārtikecchayā ||
2.5.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे काली जगाम समरं पुनः ।
भक्षितुं दानवान् स्वांश्च रक्षितुं कार्तिकेच्छया ॥
2.5.m: In the meantime, Kālī went back to the battle / to devour the Dānavas and protect her own, in accordance with Kārttikeya's wish.

2.5.s:
vīrāstāmanujagmuśca te ca nandīśvarādayaḥ |
sarve devāśca gandharvā yakṣā rakṣāṃsi pannagāḥ ||
2.5.d:
वीरास्तामनुजग्मुश्च ते च नन्दीश्वरादयः ।
सर्वे देवाश्च गन्धर्वा यक्षा रक्षांसि पन्नगाः ॥
2.5.m: The heroes followed her, including Nandīśvara and the others, / and all the gods, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Pannagas.

2.5.s:
madyabhāṇḍāśca bahuśaḥ śataśo vādyavāhakāḥ |
punaḥ samudyatāścāsan vīrā ubhayato'khilāḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ pañcamo yuddhakhaṇḍe
2.5.d:
मद्यभाण्डाश्च बहुशः शतशो वाद्यवाहकाः ।
पुनः समुद्यताश्चासन् वीरा उभयतोऽखिलाः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां पञ्चमो युद्धखण्डे
2.5.m:
With numerous jars of liquor and hundreds of instrumental musicians, / all the heroes on both sides became engaged once more.

Obeisance to the glorious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

In the fifth [section], the Yuddhakhaṇḍa, of the second [book], the Rudrasaṃhitā.

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
sā ca gatvā hi saṅgrāmaṃ siṃhanādaṃ cakāra ha |
devyāśca tena nādena mūrcchāmāpuśca dānavāḥ ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
सा च गत्वा हि सङ्ग्रामं सिंहनादं चकार ह ।
देव्याश्च तेन नादेन मूर्च्छामापुश्च दानवाः ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Having reached the battlefield, she let out a lion's roar; / and at that roar of the goddess, the Dānavas swooned.

2.5.s:
aṭṭāṭṭahāsamaśivaṃ cakāra ca punaḥ punaḥ |
tadā papau ca mādhvīkaṃ nanarta raṇamūrddhani ||
2.5.d:
अट्टाट्टहासमशिवं चकार च पुनः पुनः ।
तदा पपौ च माध्वीकं ननर्त रणमूर्द्धनि ॥
2.5.m: She uttered an inauspicious, boisterous burst of loud laughter again and again; / then she drank liquor and danced at the front of the battle.

2.5.s:
ugradaṃṣṭrā cogradaṇḍā koṭavī ca papau madhu |
anyāśca devyastatrājau nanṛturmadhu sampapuḥ ||
2.5.d:
उग्रदंष्ट्रा चोग्रदण्डा कोटवी च पपौ मधु ।
अन्याश्च देव्यस्तत्राजौ ननृतुर्मधु सम्पपुः ॥
2.5.m: Ugradaṃṣṭrā, Ugradaṇḍā, and Koṭavī drank wine; / and other goddesses danced there in battle and drank wine.

2.5.s:
mahān kolāhalo jāto gaṇadevadale tadā |
jahṛṣurbahugarjantaḥ sarve suragaṇādayaḥ ||
2.5.d:
महान् कोलाहलो जातो गणदेवदले तदा ।
जहृषुर्बहुगर्जन्तः सर्वे सुरगणादयः ॥
2.5.m: A great uproar arose then in the army of the attendants and gods; / roaring loudly, all the hosts of gods and others rejoiced.

2.5.s:
dṛṣṭvā kālīṃ śaṅkhacūḍaḥ śīghramājau samāyayau |
dānavāśca bhayaṃ prāptā rājā tebhyo'bhayaṃ dadau ||
2.5.d:
दृष्ट्वा कालीं शङ्खचूडः शीघ्रमाजौ समाययौ ।
दानवाश्च भयं प्राप्ता राजा तेभ्योऽभयं ददौ ॥
2.5.m: Seeing Kālī, Śaṅkhacūḍa quickly advanced to the battle; / and to the terrified Dānavas the king granted protection.

2.5.s:
kālī cikṣepa vahniṃ ca pralayāgniśikhopamam |
rājā jaghāna taṃ śīghraṃ vaiṣṇavāṅkitalīlayā ||
2.5.d:
काली चिक्षेप वह्निं च प्रलयाग्निशिखोपमम् ।
राजा जघान तं शीघ्रं वैष्णवाङ्कितलीलया ॥
2.5.m: Kālī hurled fire resembling the flames of the cosmic dissolution; / the king swiftly extinguished it playfully with a Vaiṣṇava [missile].

2.5.s:
nārāyaṇāstraṃ sā devī cikṣepa taduparyaram |
vṛddhiṃ jagāma tacchastraṃ dṛṣṭvā vāmaṃ ca dānavam ||
2.5.d:
नारायणास्त्रं सा देवी चिक्षेप तदुपर्यरम् ।
वृद्धिं जगाम तच्छस्त्रं दृष्ट्वा वामं च दानवम् ॥
2.5.m: The goddess quickly hurled the Nārāyaṇa missile at him; / that weapon expanded upon seeing the Dānava to its left.

2.5.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṅkhacūḍaśca pralayāgniśikhopamam |
papāta daṇḍavadbhūmau praṇanāma punaḥpunaḥ ||
2.5.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा शङ्खचूडश्च प्रलयाग्निशिखोपमम् ।
पपात दण्डवद्भूमौ प्रणनाम पुनःपुनः ॥
2.5.m: Seeing it blazing like the flames of cosmic dissolution, Śaṅkhacūḍa / fell prostrate like a staff upon the ground and bowed down again and again.

2.5.s:
nivṛttiṃ prāpa tacchstraṃ dṛṣṭvā namraṃ ca dānavam |
brahmāstramatha sā devī cikṣepa mantrapūrvakam ||
2.5.d:
निवृत्तिं प्राप तच्छ्स्त्रं दृष्ट्वा नम्रं च दानवम् ।
ब्रह्मास्त्रमथ सा देवी चिक्षेप मन्त्रपूर्वकम् ॥
2.5.m: Seeing the Dānava humble, that weapon ceased; / then the goddess, accompanied by mantras, hurled the Brahmā missile.

2.5.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā prajjvalantaṃ ca praṇamya bhuvi saṃsthitaḥ |
brahmāstreṇa dānavendro vinirvāraṃ cakāra ha ||
2.5.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा प्रज्ज्वलन्तं च प्रणम्य भुवि संस्थितः ।
ब्रह्मास्त्रेण दानवेन्द्रो विनिर्वारं चकार ह ॥
2.5.m:
Seeing it blazing, and having bowed while standing on the earth,
the lord of the Dānavas countered it with the weapon of Brahmā.

2.5.s:
atha kruddho dānavendro dhanurākṛṣya raṃhasā |
cikṣepa divyānyastrāṇi devyai vai mantrapūrvakam ||
2.5.d:
अथ क्रुद्धो दानवेन्द्रो धनुराकृष्य रंहसा ।
चिक्षेप दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि देव्यै वै मन्त्रपूर्वकम् ॥
2.5.m:
Then the lord of the Dānavas, enraged, drew his bow with speed
and hurled divine weapons at the goddess with mantras.

2.5.s:
āhāraṃ samare cakre prasārya mukhamāyatam |
jagarja sāṭṭahāsaṃ ca dānavā bhayamāyayuḥ ||
2.5.d:
आहारं समरे चक्रे प्रसार्य मुखमायतम् ।
जगर्ज साट्टहासं च दानवा भयमाययुः ॥
2.5.m:
She made a meal of them in the battle, opening her wide mouth;
she roared with a loud laugh, and the Dānavas were seized with fear.

2.5.s:
kālyai cikṣepa śaktiṃ sa śatayojanamāyatām |
devī divyāstrajālena śatakhaṇḍaṃ cakāra sā ||
2.5.d:
काल्यै चिक्षेप शक्तिं स शतयोजनमायताम् ।
देवी दिव्यास्त्रजालेन शतखण्डं चकार सा ॥
2.5.m:
He hurled at Kālī a spear a hundred yojanas long;
with a network of divine weapons the goddess cut it into a hundred pieces.

2.5.s:
sa ca vaiṣṇavamastraṃ ca cikṣepa caṇḍikopari |
māheśvareṇa kālī ca vinirvāraṃ cakāra sā ||
2.5.d:
स च वैष्णवमस्त्रं च चिक्षेप चण्डिकोपरि ।
माहेश्वरेण काली च विनिर्वारं चकार सा ॥
2.5.m:
He then hurled the Vaiṣṇava weapon against Caṇḍikā;
and Kālī countered it with the Māheśvara weapon.

2.5.s:
evaṃ cirataraṃ yuddhamanyo'nyaṃ sambabhūva ha |
prekṣakā abhavan sarve devāśca dānavā api ||
2.5.d:
एवं चिरतरं युद्धमन्योऽन्यं सम्बभूव ह ।
प्रेक्षका अभवन् सर्वे देवाश्च दानवा अपि ॥
2.5.m:
Thus a battle between them went on for a very long time;
all the gods and the Dānavas as well became onlookers.

2.5.s:
atha kuddhā mahādevī kālī kālasamā raṇe |
jagrāha mantrapūtaṃ ca śaraṃ pāśupataṃ ruṣā ||
2.5.d:
अथ कुद्धा महादेवी काली कालसमा रणे ।
जग्राह मन्त्रपूतं च शरं पाशुपतं रुषा ॥
2.5.m:
Then the great goddess Kālī, enraged, resembling Death in battle,
grasped in fury the Pāśupata arrow purified by mantra.

2.5.s:
kṣepātpūrvaṃ tanniṣeddhuṃ vāgbabhūvāśarīriṇī |
na kṣipāstramidaṃ devi śaṅkhacūḍāya vai ruṣā ||
2.5.d:
क्षेपात्पूर्वं तन्निषेद्धुं वाग्बभूवाशरीरिणी ।
न क्षिपास्त्रमिदं देवि शङ्खचूडाय वै रुषा ॥
2.5.m:
Before she hurled it, an incorporeal voice arose to stop it:
‘Do not hurl this weapon, O goddess, in fury at Śaṅkhacūḍa!

2.5.s:
mṛtyuḥ pāśupatānnāstyamoghādapi ca caṇḍike |
śaṅkhacūḍasya vīrasyopāyamanyaṃ vicāraya ||
2.5.d:
मृत्युः पाशुपतान्नास्त्यमोघादपि च चण्डिके ।
शङ्खचूडस्य वीरस्योपायमन्यं विचारय ॥
2.5.m:
There is no death for the heroic Śaṅkhacūḍa, O Caṇḍikā, even from the unerring Pāśupata [weapon];
consider another means!’

2.5.s:
ityākarṇya bhadrakālī na cikṣepa tadastrakam |
śatalakṣaṃ dānavānāṃ jaghāsa līlayā kṣudhā ||
2.5.d:
इत्याकर्ण्य भद्रकाली न चिक्षेप तदस्त्रकम् ।
शतलक्षं दानवानां जघास लीलया क्षुधा ॥
2.5.m:
Hearing this, Bhadrakālī did not hurl that weapon;
with hunger, she sportively devoured ten million Dānavas.

2.5.s:
attuṃ jagāma vegena śaṅkhacūḍaṃ bhayaṅkarī |
divyāstreṇa ca raudreṇa vārayāmāsa dānavaḥ ||
2.5.d:
अत्तुं जगाम वेगेन शङ्खचूडं भयङ्करी ।
दिव्यास्त्रेण च रौद्रेण वारयामास दानवः ॥
2.5.m:
The terrifying goddess swiftly went to devour Śaṅkhacūḍa;
and the Dānava warded her off with a divine, terrible weapon.

2.5.s:
atha kruddho dānavendraḥ khaḍgaṃ cikṣepa satvaram |
grīṣmasūryopamaṃ tīkṣṇadhāramatyantabhīkaram ||
2.5.d:
अथ क्रुद्धो दानवेन्द्रः खड्गं चिक्षेप सत्वरम् ।
ग्रीष्मसूर्योपमं तीक्ष्णधारमत्यन्तभीकरम् ॥
2.5.m:
Then the lord of the Dānavas, enraged, swiftly hurled a sword,
sharp-edged, resembling the summer sun, exceedingly terrifying.

2.5.s:
sā kālī taṃ samālokyāyāntaṃ prajvalitaṃ ruṣā |
prasārya mukhamāhāraṃ cakre tasya ca paśyataḥ ||
2.5.d:
सा काली तं समालोक्यायान्तं प्रज्वलितं रुषा ।
प्रसार्य मुखमाहारं चक्रे तस्य च पश्यतः ॥
2.5.m:
Seeing it coming blazing in fury, Kālī
opened her mouth and devoured it as he watched.

2.5.s:
divyānyastrāṇi cānyāni ciccheda dānaveśvaraḥ |
prāptāni pūrvataścakre śatakhaṇḍāni tāni ca ||
2.5.d:
दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि चान्यानि चिच्छेद दानवेश्वरः ।
प्राप्तानि पूर्वतश्चक्रे शतखण्डानि तानि च ॥
2.5.m:
And the lord of the Dānavas cut down other divine weapons [of hers];
as they arrived from before, he cut them into a hundred pieces.

2.5.s:
punarattuṃ mahādevī vegatastaṃ jagāma ha |
sarvasiddheśvaraḥ śrīmānantardhānaṃ cakāra saḥ ||
2.5.d:
पुनरत्तुं महादेवी वेगतस्तं जगाम ह ।
सर्वसिद्धेश्वरः श्रीमानन्तर्धानं चकार सः ॥
2.5.m:
Again the great goddess swiftly went to devour him;
he, the glorious lord of all perfected beings, vanished.

2.5.s:
vegena muṣṭinā kālī tamadṛṣṭvā ca dānavam |
babhañja ca rathaṃ tasya jaghāna kila sārathim ||
2.5.d:
वेगेन मुष्टिना काली तमदृष्ट्वा च दानवम् ।
बभञ्ज च रथं तस्य जघान किल सारथिम् ॥
2.5.m:
Not seeing the Dānava, Kālī, with the swift blow of her fist,
smashed his chariot and killed his charioteer.

2.5.s:
athāgatya drutaṃ māyī cakraṃ cikṣepa vegataḥ |
bhadrakālyai śaṅkhacūḍaḥ pralayāgniśikhopamam ||
2.5.d:
अथागत्य द्रुतं मायी चक्रं चिक्षेप वेगतः ।
भद्रकाल्यै शङ्खचूडः प्रलयाग्निशिखोपमम् ॥
2.5.m:
Then the illusionist Śaṅkhacūḍa swiftly came and hurled with speed
a discus resembling the crest of the fire of dissolution at Bhadrakālī.

2.5.s:
sā devī taṃ tadā cakraṃ vāmahastena līlayā |
jagrāha svamukhenaivāhāraṃ cakre ruṣā drutam ||
2.5.d:
सा देवी तं तदा चक्रं वामहस्तेन लीलया ।
जग्राह स्वमुखेनैवाहारं चक्रे रुषा द्रुतम् ॥
2.5.m:
Then the goddess sportively caught that discus with her left hand
and swiftly swallowed it with her own mouth in fury.

2.5.s:
muṣṭyā jaghāna taṃ devī mahākopena vegataḥ |
babhrāma dānavendro'pi kṣaṇaṃ mūrcchāmavāpa saḥ ||
2.5.d:
मुष्ट्या जघान तं देवी महाकोपेन वेगतः ।
बभ्राम दानवेन्द्रोऽपि क्षणं मूर्च्छामवाप सः ॥
2.5.m:
With immense rage the goddess struck him swiftly with her fist;
the lord of the Dānavas reeled, and fell unconscious for a moment.

2.5.s:
kṣaṇena cetanāṃ prāpya sa cottasthau pratāpavān |
na cakre bāhu yuddhaṃ ca mātṛbuddhyā tayā saha ||
2.5.d:
क्षणेन चेतनां प्राप्य स चोत्तस्थौ प्रतापवान् ।
न चक्रे बाहु युद्धं च मातृबुद्ध्या तया सह ॥
2.5.m:
Regaining consciousness in a moment, the powerful one stood up;
he did not engage in hand-to-hand combat with her, regarding her as a mother.

2.5.s:
gṛhītvā dānavaṃ devī bhrāmayitvā punaḥ punaḥ |
ūrdhvaṃ ca prāpayāmāsa mahākopena vegataḥ ||
2.5.d:
गृहीत्वा दानवं देवी भ्रामयित्वा पुनः पुनः ।
ऊर्ध्वं च प्रापयामास महाकोपेन वेगतः ॥
2.5.m:
Seizing the Dānava and whirling him around again and again,
the goddess hurled him upward with great anger and speed.

2.5.s:
utpapāta ca vegena śaṅkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān |
nipatya ca samuttastho praṇamya bhadrakālikām ||
2.5.d:
उत्पपात च वेगेन शङ्खचूडः प्रतापवान् ।
निपत्य च समुत्तस्थो प्रणम्य भद्रकालिकाम् ॥
2.5.m:
The powerful Śaṅkhacūḍa sprang up swiftly;
falling down, he stood up and bowed to Bhadrakālikā.

2.5.s:
ratnendrasāranirmāṇavimānaṃ sumanoharam |
āruroha sa hṛṣṭātmā na bhrānto'pi mahāraṇe ||
2.5.d:
रत्नेन्द्रसारनिर्माणविमानं सुमनोहरम् ।
आरुरोह स हृष्टात्मा न भ्रान्तोऽपि महारणे ॥
2.5.m:
He mounted his magnificent celestial chariot made of the essence of the best of gems;
his heart was glad, and he was not confused even in that great battle.

2.5.s:
dānavānāṃ hi kṣatajaṃ sā papau kālikā kṣudhā |
etasminnantare tatra vāgbabhūvāśarīriṇī ||
2.5.d:
दानवानां हि क्षतजं सा पपौ कालिका क्षुधा ।
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र वाग्बभूवाशरीरिणी ॥
2.5.m:
Then Kālikā drank the blood of the Dānavas in her hunger;
in the meantime, an incorporeal voice arose there:

2.5.s:
lakṣaṃ ca dānavendrāṇāmavaśiṣṭaṃ raṇe'dhunā |
uddhataṃ guñjatāṃ sārddhaṃ tatastvaṃ bhuṅkṣva ceśvari ||
2.5.d:
लक्षं च दानवेन्द्राणामवशिष्टं रणेऽधुना ।
उद्धतं गुञ्जतां सार्द्धं ततस्त्वं भुङ्क्ष्व चेश्वरि ॥
2.5.m:
‘One hundred thousand lords of the Dānavas now remain in the battle;
consume them together with their haughty clamour, O sovereign goddess!

2.5.s:
saṅgrāme dānavendraṃ ca hantuṃ na kuru mānasam |
avadhyo'yaṃ śaṅkhacūḍastava devīti niścayam ||
2.5.d:
सङ्ग्रामे दानवेन्द्रं च हन्तुं न कुरु मानसम् ।
अवध्योऽयं शङ्खचूडस्तव देवीति निश्चयम् ॥
2.5.m:
Do not set your mind on killing the lord of the Dānavas in battle;
this Śaṅkhacūḍa cannot be killed by you, O goddess, this is certain.’

2.5.s:
tacchutvā vacanaṃ devī niḥsṛtaṃ vyomamaṇḍalāt |
dānavānāṃ bahūnāṃ ca māṃsaṃ ca rudhiraṃ tathā ||
2.5.d:
तच्छुत्वा वचनं देवी निःसृतं व्योममण्डलात् ।
दानवानां बहूनां च मांसं च रुधिरं तथा ॥
2.5.m:
Having heard that voice issue from the vault of heaven,
and having eaten the flesh and drunk the blood of many Dānavas,

2.5.s:
bhuktvā pītvā bhadrakālī śaṅkarāntikamāyayau |
uvāca raṇavṛttāntaṃ paurvāparyeṇa sakramam ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ pañcamo yuddhakhaṇḍe
2.5.d:
भुक्त्वा पीत्वा भद्रकाली शङ्करान्तिकमाययौ ।
उवाच रणवृत्तान्तं पौर्वापर्येण सक्रमम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां पञ्चमो युद्धखण्डे
2.5.m:
Bhadrakālī came to the presence of Śaṅkara
and recounted the events of the battle in succession from beginning to end.

Homage to the glorious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

In the Yuddhakhaṇḍa, the fifth [section] of the second [part], the Rudrasaṃhitā.

2.5.s:
vyāsa uvāca |
śrutvā kālyuktamīśāno kiṃ cakāra kimuktavān |
tattvaṃ vada mahāprājña paraṃ kautūhalaṃ mama ||
2.5.d:
व्यास उवाच ।
श्रुत्वा काल्युक्तमीशानो किं चकार किमुक्तवान् ।
तत्त्वं वद महाप्राज्ञ परं कौतूहलं मम ॥
2.5.m:
Vyāsa said:
Having heard what Kālī said, what did the Lord do, and what did he say?
Tell me the truth, O exceedingly wise one; my curiosity is supreme.

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
kālyuktaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā śaṅkaraḥ parameśvaraḥ |
mahālīlākaraḥ śambhurjahāsāśvāsayañca tām ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
काल्युक्तं वचनं श्रुत्वा शङ्करः परमेश्वरः ।
महालीलाकरः शम्भुर्जहासाश्वासयञ्च ताम् ॥
2.5.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Having heard the words spoken by Kālī, Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord,
Śambhu, who performs great divine play, laughed and comforted her.

2.5.s:
vyomavāṇīṃ samākarṇya tattvajñānaviśāradaḥ |
yayau svayaṃ ca samare svagaṇaiḥ saha śaṅkaraḥ ||
2.5.d:
व्योमवाणीं समाकर्ण्य तत्त्वज्ञानविशारदः ।
ययौ स्वयं च समरे स्वगणैः सह शङ्करः ॥
2.5.m:
Having heard the voice from the sky, Śaṅkara, skilled in the knowledge of truth,
went himself to the battle accompanied by his own attendants.

2.5.s:
mahāvṛṣabhamārūḍho vīrabhadrādisaṃyutaḥ |
bhairavaiḥ kṣetrapālaiśca svasamānaiḥ samanvitaḥ ||
2.5.d:
महावृषभमारूढो वीरभद्रादिसंयुतः ।
भैरवैः क्षेत्रपालैश्च स्वसमानैः समन्वितः ॥
2.5.m:
Mounted on his great bull, accompanied by Vīrabhadra and others,
attended by the Bhairavas and the Kṣetrapālas who were his equals,

2.5.s:
raṇaṃ prāpto maheśaśca vīrarūpaṃ vidhāya ca |
virarājādhikaṃ tatra rudro mūrta ivāntakaḥ ||
2.5.d:
रणं प्राप्तो महेशश्च वीररूपं विधाय च ।
विरराजाधिकं तत्र रुद्रो मूर्त इवान्तकः ॥
2.5.m:
Maheśa reached the battle; having assumed a heroic form,
Rudra shone there exceedingly, like the god of death embodied.

2.5.s:
śaṅkhacūḍaḥ śivaṃ dṛṣṭvā vimānādavaruhya saḥ |
nanāma parayā bhaktyā śirasā daṇḍavadbhuvi ||
2.5.d:
शङ्खचूडः शिवं दृष्ट्वा विमानादवरुह्य सः ।
ननाम परया भक्त्या शिरसा दण्डवद्भुवि ॥
2.5.m:
Seeing Śiva, Śaṅkhacūḍa descended from his celestial chariot
and bowed with supreme devotion, prostrating with his head on the ground like a staff.

2.5.s:
taṃ praṇamya tu yogena vimānamāruroha saḥ |
tūrṇaṃ cakāra sannāhaṃ dhanurjagrāha seṣukam ||
2.5.d:
तं प्रणम्य तु योगेन विमानमारुरोह सः ।
तूर्णं चकार सन्नाहं धनुर्जग्राह सेषुकम् ॥
2.5.m:
Having bowed to him through yoga, he mounted his celestial chariot,
quickly put on his armour, and seized his bow along with arrows.

2.5.s:
śivadānavayoryuddhaṃ śatamabdaṃ babhūva ha |
bāṇavarṣamivograṃ tadvarṣatormoghayostadā ||
2.5.d:
शिवदानवयोर्युद्धं शतमब्दं बभूव ह ।
बाणवर्षमिवोग्रं तद्वर्षतोर्मोघयोस्तदा ॥
2.5.m:
The battle between Śiva and the Dānava lasted for a hundred years,
as the two unerring ones showered a fierce rain of arrows.

2.5.s:
śaṅkhacūḍo mahāvīraḥ śarāṃścikṣepa dāruṇān |
ciccheda śaṅkarastānvai līlayā svaśarotkaraiḥ ||
2.5.d:
शङ्खचूडो महावीरः शरांश्चिक्षेप दारुणान् ।
चिच्छेद शङ्करस्तान्वै लीलया स्वशरोत्करैः ॥
2.5.m:
The great hero Śaṅkhacūḍa hurled dreadful arrows;
Śaṅkara cut them down sportively with volleys of his own arrows.

2.5.s:
tadaṅgeṣu ca śastraughaistāḍayāmāsa kopataḥ |
mahārudro virūpākṣo duṣṭadaṇḍaḥ satāṃ gatiḥ ||
2.5.d:
तदङ्गेषु च शस्त्रौघैस्ताडयामास कोपतः ।
महारुद्रो विरूपाक्षो दुष्टदण्डः सतां गतिः ॥
2.5.m:
And with showers of weapons he angrily struck his limbs—
Mahārudra, the three-eyed, who punishes the wicked, the refuge of the virtuous.

2.5.s:
dānavo niśitaṃ khaḍgaṃ carma cādāya vegavān |
vṛṣaṃ jaghāna śirasi śivasya varavāhanam ||
2.5.d:
दानवो निशितं खड्गं चर्म चादाय वेगवान् ।
वृषं जघान शिरसि शिवस्य वरवाहनम् ॥
2.5.m:
Taking a sharp sword and shield, the swift Dānava
struck the bull, Śiva’s excellent mount, on the head.

2.5.s:
tāḍite vāhane rudrastaṃ kṣurapreṇa līlayā |
khaḍgaṃ ciccheda tasyāśu carma cāpi mahojjvalam ||
2.5.d:
ताडिते वाहने रुद्रस्तं क्षुरप्रेण लीलया ।
खड्गं चिच्छेद तस्याशु चर्म चापि महोज्ज्वलम् ॥
2.5.m:
When his mount was struck, Rudra sportively, with a crescent-tipped arrow,
swiftly cut down his sword and also his blazing shield.

2.5.s:
chinne'sau carmaṇi tadā śaktiṃ cikṣepa so'suraḥ |
dvidhā cakre svabāṇena harastāṃ sammukhāgatām ||
2.5.d:
छिन्नेऽसौ चर्मणि तदा शक्तिं चिक्षेप सोऽसुरः ।
द्विधा चक्रे स्वबाणेन हरस्तां सम्मुखागताम् ॥
2.5.m:
When that shield was cut, the Asura hurled a spear;
Hara cut it into two pieces with his own arrow as it came straight forward.

2.5.s:
kopādhmātaḥ śaṅkhacūḍaḥ cakraṃ cikṣepa dānavaḥ |
muṣṭipātena taccāpyacūrṇayatsahasā haraḥ ||
2.5.d:
कोपाध्मातः शङ्खचूडः चक्रं चिक्षेप दानवः ।
मुष्टिपातेन तच्चाप्यचूर्णयत्सहसा हरः ॥
2.5.m:
Swollen with wrath, the Dānava Śaṅkhacūḍa hurled a discus;
Hara suddenly shattered that too with the blow of his fist.

2.5.s:
gadāmāvidhya tarasā sañcikṣepa haraṃ prati |
śambhunā sāpi sahasā bhinnā bhasmatvamāgatā ||
2.5.d:
गदामाविध्य तरसा सञ्चिक्षेप हरं प्रति ।
शम्भुना सापि सहसा भिन्ना भस्मत्वमागता ॥
2.5.m:
Whirling a club, he hurled it with force toward Hara;
that too was suddenly smashed by Śambhu and turned to ashes.

2.5.s:
tataḥ paraśumādāya hastena dānaveśvaraḥ |
dhāvati sma haraṃ vegācchaṅkhacūḍaḥ krudhākulaḥ ||
2.5.d:
ततः परशुमादाय हस्तेन दानवेश्वरः ।
धावति स्म हरं वेगाच्छङ्खचूडः क्रुधाकुलः ॥
2.5.m:
Then the lord of the Dānavas, seizing an axe with his hand,
ran with speed toward Hara, Śaṅkhacūḍa overcome with rage.

2.5.s:
samāhṛtya svabāṇaughairapātayata śaṅkaraḥ |
drutaṃ paraśuhastaṃ taṃ bhūtale līlayāsuram ||
2.5.d:
समाहृत्य स्वबाणौघैरपातयत शङ्करः ।
द्रुतं परशुहस्तं तं भूतले लीलयासुरम् ॥
2.5.m:
Gathering [force], Śaṅkara quickly knocked the Asura with the axe in hand
down to the surface of the earth sportively with volleys of his arrows.

2.5.s:
tataḥ kṣaṇena samprāpya saṃjñāmāruhya sadratham |
dhṛtadivyāyudhaśaro babhau vyāpyākhilaṃ nabhaḥ ||
2.5.d:
ततः क्षणेन सम्प्राप्य संज्ञामारुह्य सद्रथम् ।
धृतदिव्यायुधशरो बभौ व्याप्याखिलं नभः ॥
2.5.m:
Then, recovering consciousness in a moment, mounting an excellent chariot,
bearing divine weapons and arrows, he shone, pervading the entire sky.

2.5.s:
āyāntaṃ taṃ nirīkṣyaiva ḍamarudhvanimādarāt |
cakāra jyāravaṃ cāpi dhanuṣo duḥsahaṃ haraḥ ||
2.5.d:
आयान्तं तं निरीक्ष्यैव डमरुध्वनिमादरात् ।
चकार ज्यारवं चापि धनुषो दुःसहं हरः ॥
2.5.m:
Seeing him advancing, Hara with zeal produced
the sound of the ḍamaru, and also the unbearable twang of his bowstring.

2.5.s:
pūrayāmāsa kakubhaḥ śṛṅganādena ca prabhuḥ |
svayaṃ jagarja giriśastrāsayannasurāṃstadā ||
2.5.d:
पूरयामास ककुभः शृङ्गनादेन च प्रभुः ।
स्वयं जगर्ज गिरिशस्त्रासयन्नसुरांस्तदा ॥
2.5.m:
The Lord filled the quarters with the sound of a horn;
then Giriśa himself roared, terrifying the asuras.

2.5.s:
tyājitebhamahāgarvairmahānādairvṛṣeśvaraḥ |
pūrayāmāsa sahasā khaṃ gāṃ vasudiśastathā ||
2.5.d:
त्याजितेभमहागर्वैर्महानादैर्वृषेश्वरः ।
पूरयामास सहसा खं गां वसुदिशस्तथा ॥
2.5.m:
The Lord of Bulls, with great roars that stripped the great pride of elephants,
suddenly filled the sky, the earth, and the eight directions.

2.5.s:
mahākālaḥ samutpatya tāḍayad gāṃ tathā nabhaḥ |
karābhyāṃ tanninādena kṣiptā āsanpurā ravāḥ ||
2.5.d:
महाकालः समुत्पत्य ताडयद् गां तथा नभः ।
कराभ्यां तन्निनादेन क्षिप्ता आसन्पुरा रवाः ॥
2.5.m:
Mahākāla leaped up and struck the earth and the sky
with both hands; by that roar, previous sounds were eclipsed.

2.5.s:
aṭṭāṭṭahāsamaśivaṃ kṣetrapālaścakāra ha |
bhairavo'pi mahānādaṃ sa cakāra mahāhave ||
2.5.d:
अट्टाट्टहासमशिवं क्षेत्रपालश्चकार ह ।
भैरवोऽपि महानादं स चकार महाहवे ॥
2.5.m:
Kṣetrapāla gave an inauspicious, violent boisterous laugh;
Bhairava too uttered a great cry in that great battle.

2.5.s:
mahākolāhalo jāto raṇamadhye bhayaṅkaraḥ |
vīraśabdo babhūvātha gaṇamadhye samantataḥ ||
2.5.d:
महाकोलाहलो जातो रणमध्ये भयङ्करः ।
वीरशब्दो बभूवाथ गणमध्ये समन्ततः ॥
2.5.m:
A terrifying, immense tumult arose in the midst of the battle;
then the battle-cry of heroes resounded on every side among the attendants.

2.5.s:
santresurdānavāḥsarve taiḥ śabdairbhayadaiḥ kharaiḥ |
cukopātīva tacchrutvā dānavendro mahābalaḥ ||
2.5.d:
सन्त्रेसुर्दानवाःसर्वे तैः शब्दैर्भयदैः खरैः ।
चुकोपातीव तच्छ्रुत्वा दानवेन्द्रो महाबलः ॥
2.5.m:
All the dānavas were terrified by those harsh, frightening sounds;
hearing that, the mighty lord of the dānavas grew exceedingly enraged.

2.5.s:
tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti duṣṭātman vyājahāra yadā haraḥ |
devairgaṇaiśca taiḥ śīghramuktaṃ jaya jayeti ca ||
2.5.d:
तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति दुष्टात्मन् व्याजहार यदा हरः ।
देवैर्गणैश्च तैः शीघ्रमुक्तं जय जयेति च ॥
2.5.m:
When Hara proclaimed, "Halt! Halt, evil-minded one!"
the gods and the attendants quickly shouted, "Victory! Victory!"

2.5.s:
athāgatya sa dambhasya tanayaḥ supratāpavān |
śaktiṃ cikṣepa rudrāya jvālāmālātibhīṣaṇām ||
2.5.d:
अथागत्य स दम्भस्य तनयः सुप्रतापवान् ।
शक्तिं चिक्षेप रुद्राय ज्वालामालातिभीषणाम् ॥
2.5.m:
Then advancing, the son of Dambha, endowed with immense prowess,
hurled a spear at Rudra, terrifying with a garland of flames.

2.5.s:
vahnikūṭaprabhāyāntī kṣetrapālena satvaram |
nirastāgatya sājau vai mukhotpannamaholkayā ||
2.5.d:
वह्निकूटप्रभायान्ती क्षेत्रपालेन सत्वरम् ।
निरस्तागत्य साजौ वै मुखोत्पन्नमहोल्कया ॥
2.5.m:
As it arrived blazing like a mass of fire, it was quickly repelled in battle
by Kṣetrapāla, who struck it with a great meteor born from his mouth.

2.5.s:
punaḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ śivadānavayormahat |
cakampe dharaṇī dyauśca sanagābdhijalāśayā ||
2.5.d:
पुनः प्रववृते युद्धं शिवदानवयोर्महत् ।
चकम्पे धरणी द्यौश्च सनगाब्धिजलाशया ॥
2.5.m:
Again a great battle ensued between Śiva and the dānava;
the earth and the heavens trembled, along with the mountains, oceans, and bodies of water.

2.5.s:
dāmbhimuktān śarān śambhuḥ śarāṃstatprahitānsa ca |
sahasraśaḥ śarairugraiściccheda śataśastadā ||
2.5.d:
दाम्भिमुक्तान् शरान् शम्भुः शरांस्तत्प्रहितान्स च ।
सहस्रशः शरैरुग्रैश्चिच्छेद शतशस्तदा ॥
2.5.m:
Śambhu cut off the arrows released by Dambha's son, and he cut off the arrows dispatched by him,
with hundreds of fierce arrows, by the thousands.

2.5.s:
tataḥ śambhustriśūlena saṅkruddhastaṃ jaghāna ha |
tatprahāramasahyāśu kau papāta sa mūrcchitaḥ ||
2.5.d:
ततः शम्भुस्त्रिशूलेन सङ्क्रुद्धस्तं जघान ह ।
तत्प्रहारमसह्याशु कौ पपात स मूर्च्छितः ॥
2.5.m:
Then Śambhu, enraged, struck him with his trident;
unable to bear that blow, he immediately fell swooning to the earth.

2.5.s:
tataḥ kṣaṇena samprāpa saṃjñāṃ sa ca tadāsuraḥ |
ājaghāna śarai rudraṃ tānsarvānāttakārmukaḥ ||
2.5.d:
ततः क्षणेन सम्प्राप संज्ञां स च तदासुरः ।
आजघान शरै रुद्रं तान्सर्वानात्तकार्मुकः ॥
2.5.m:
Then, recovering consciousness in a moment, that asura
grasped his bow and struck Rudra with arrows, with all of them.

2.5.s:
bāhūnāmayutaṃ kṛtvā chādayāmāsa śaṅkaram |
cakrāyutena sahasā śaṅkhacūḍaḥ pratāpavān ||
2.5.d:
बाहूनामयुतं कृत्वा छादयामास शङ्करम् ।
चक्रायुतेन सहसा शङ्खचूडः प्रतापवान् ॥
2.5.m:
Creating ten thousand arms, Śaṅkhacūḍa, full of prowess,
suddenly covered Śaṅkara with ten thousand discs.

2.5.s:
tato durgāpatiḥ kruddho rudro durgārtināśanaḥ |
tāni cakrāṇi ciccheda svaśarairuttamairdrutam ||
2.5.d:
ततो दुर्गापतिः क्रुद्धो रुद्रो दुर्गार्तिनाशनः ।
तानि चक्राणि चिच्छेद स्वशरैरुत्तमैर्द्रुतम् ॥
2.5.m:
Then Durgā's lord, Rudra, the destroyer of the distress of the impassable,
swiftly cut to pieces those discs with his own excellent arrows.

2.5.s:
tato vegena sahasā gadāmādāya dānavaḥ |
abhyadhāvata vai hantuṃ bahusenāvṛto haram ||
2.5.d:
ततो वेगेन सहसा गदामादाय दानवः ।
अभ्यधावत वै हन्तुं बहुसेनावृतो हरम् ॥
2.5.m:
Then, seizing a mace in haste, the dānava,
surrounded by a vast army, rushed forward to slay Hara.

2.5.s:
gadāṃ ciccheda tasyāśvāpatataḥ so'sinā haraḥ |
śitadhāreṇa saṅkruddho duṣṭagarvāpahārakaḥ ||
2.5.d:
गदां चिच्छेद तस्याश्वापततः सोऽसिना हरः ।
शितधारेण सङ्क्रुद्धो दुष्टगर्वापहारकः ॥
2.5.m:
As he rushed forward, Hara, enraged, who removes the pride of the wicked,
swiftly severed his mace with a sharp-edged sword.

2.5.s:
chinnāyāṃ svagadāyāṃ ca cukopātīva dānavaḥ |
śūlaṃ jagrāha tejasvī pareṣāṃ duḥsahaṃ jvalat ||
2.5.d:
छिन्नायां स्वगदायां च चुकोपातीव दानवः ।
शूलं जग्राह तेजस्वी परेषां दुःसहं ज्वलत् ॥
2.5.m:
When his mace was shattered, the radiant dānava became exceedingly enraged;
he grasped a flaming trident, unbearable to his adversaries.

2.5.s:
sudarśanaṃ śūlahastamāyāntaṃ dānaveśvaram |
svatriśūlena vivyādha hṛdi taṃ vegato haraḥ ||
2.5.d:
सुदर्शनं शूलहस्तमायान्तं दानवेश्वरम् ।
स्वत्रिशूलेन विव्याध हृदि तं वेगतो हरः ॥
2.5.m:
As the lord of the dānavas approached, lovely to behold, spear in hand,
Hara swiftly pierced his heart with his own trident.

2.5.s:
triśūlabhinnahṛdayānniṣkrāntaḥ puruṣaḥ paraḥ |
tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti covāca śaṅkhacūḍasya vīryavān ||
2.5.d:
त्रिशूलभिन्नहृदयान्निष्क्रान्तः पुरुषः परः ।
तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चोवाच शङ्खचूडस्य वीर्यवान् ॥
2.5.m:
From the heart pierced by the trident, another heroic person emerged
from Śaṅkhacūḍa, saying, "Halt, halt!"

2.5.s:
niṣkrāmato hi tasyāśu prahasya svanavattataḥ |
ciccheda ca śiro bhīmamasinā so'patadbhuvi ||
2.5.d:
निष्क्रामतो हि तस्याशु प्रहस्य स्वनवत्ततः ।
चिच्छेद च शिरो भीममसिना सोऽपतद्भुवि ॥
2.5.m:
As he was emerging, [Hara], laughing loudly, immediately
severed his dreadful head with a sword; he fell to the earth.

2.5.s:
tataḥ kālīṃ cakhādograṃ daṃṣṭrākṣuṇṇaśirodharān |
asurāṃstān bahūn krodhāt prasārya svamukhaṃ tadā ||
2.5.d:
ततः कालीं चखादोग्रं दंष्ट्राक्षुण्णशिरोधरान् ।
असुरांस्तान् बहून् क्रोधात् प्रसार्य स्वमुखं तदा ॥
2.5.m:
Then Kālī fiercely devoured many asuras in anger,
widening her mouth, their necks crushed by her fangs.

2.5.s:
kṣetrapālaścakhādānyānbahūndaityānkrudhākulaḥ |
kecinneśurbhairavāstracchinnā bhinnāstathāpare ||
2.5.d:
क्षेत्रपालश्चखादान्यान्बहून्दैत्यान्क्रुधाकुलः ।
केचिन्नेशुर्भैरवास्त्रच्छिन्ना भिन्नास्तथापरे ॥
2.5.m:
Filled with wrath, Kṣetrapāla devoured many other daityas;
some perished, severed by Bhairava's weapons, and others were pierced.

2.5.s:
vīrabhadro'parān vīrān bahūn krodhādanāśayat |
nandīśvaro jaghānānyān bahūnamaramardakān ||
2.5.d:
वीरभद्रोऽपरान् वीरान् बहून् क्रोधादनाशयत् ।
नन्दीश्वरो जघानान्यान् बहूनमरमर्दकान् ॥
2.5.m:
Vīrabhadra angrily destroyed many other warriors;
Nandīśvara slew many others, crushers of the gods.

2.5.s:
evaṃ bahugaṇā vīrāstadā sannahya kopataḥ |
vyanāśayanbahūndaityānasurān devamardakān ||
2.5.d:
एवं बहुगणा वीरास्तदा सन्नह्य कोपतः ।
व्यनाशयन्बहून्दैत्यानसुरान् देवमर्दकान् ॥
2.5.m:
Thus the heroic attendants, having armed themselves in fury,
destroyed many daityas and asuras, crushers of the gods.

2.5.s:
itthaṃ bahutaraṃ tatra tasya sainyaṃ nanāśa tat |
vidrutāścāpare vīrā bahavo bhayakātarāḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ pañcamo yuddhakhaṇḍe
2.5.d:
इत्थं बहुतरं तत्र तस्य सैन्यं ननाश तत् ।
विद्रुताश्चापरे वीरा बहवो भयकातराः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां पञ्चमो युद्धखण्डे
2.5.m:
In this manner, a great part of his army was destroyed there,
and many other warriors fled, distraught with fear.

Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, entitled "Description of the Destruction of Śaṅkhacūḍa's Army," in the Yuddhakhaṇḍa, the fifth [section] of the second [book], the Rudrasaṃhitā, in the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
svabalaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā mukhyaṃ bahutaraṃ tataḥ |
tathā vīrān prāṇasamān cukopātīva dānavaḥ ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
स्वबलं निहतं दृष्ट्वा मुख्यं बहुतरं ततः ।
तथा वीरान् प्राणसमान् चुकोपातीव दानवः ॥
2.5.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Seeing that most of his chief forces had been slain,
as well as the warriors who were as dear to him as life, the dānava grew exceedingly enraged.

2.5.s:
uvāca vacanaṃ śambhuṃ tiṣṭhāmyājau sthiro bhava |
kimetairnihatairme'dya sammukhe samaraṃ kuru ||
2.5.d:
उवाच वचनं शम्भुं तिष्ठाम्याजौ स्थिरो भव ।
किमेतैर्निहतैर्मेऽद्य सम्मुखे समरं कुरु ॥
2.5.m:
He spoke these words to Śambhu: "I stand ready; stand firm in battle!
What is the use of slaying these? Fight me face to face today!"

2.5.s:
ityuktvā dānavendro'sau sannaddhaḥ samare mune |
agacchanniścayaṃ kṛtvā'bhimukhaṃ śaṅkarasya ca ||
2.5.d:
इत्युक्त्वा दानवेन्द्रोऽसौ सन्नद्धः समरे मुने ।
अगच्छन्निश्चयं कृत्वाऽभिमुखं शङ्करस्य च ॥
2.5.m:
Having spoken thus, O sage, that lord of the dānavas, armed in battle,
made a resolve and advanced against Śaṅkara.

2.5.s:
divyānyastrāṇi cikṣepa mahārudrāya dānavaḥ |
cakāra śaravṛṣṭiṃ ca toyavṛṣṭiṃ yathā ghanaḥ ||
2.5.d:
दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि चिक्षेप महारुद्राय दानवः ।
चकार शरवृष्टिं च तोयवृष्टिं यथा घनः ॥
2.5.m:
The dānava hurled divine missiles at Mahārudra
and unleashed a shower of arrows, like a cloud [releasing] a shower of water.

2.5.s:
māyāścakāra vividhā adṛśyā bhayadarśitāḥ |
apratarkyāḥ suragaṇairnikhilairapiḥ sattamaiḥ ||
2.5.d:
मायाश्चकार विविधा अदृश्या भयदर्शिताः ।
अप्रतर्क्याः सुरगणैर्निखिलैरपिः सत्तमैः ॥
2.5.m:
He created various illusory powers that were invisible, frightening to behold,
and inconceivable even to all the gods, the best of beings.

2.5.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṅkarastatra cikṣepāstraṃ ca līlayā |
māheśvaraṃ mahādivyaṃ sarvamāyāvināśanam ||
2.5.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा शङ्करस्तत्र चिक्षेपास्त्रं च लीलया ।
माहेश्वरं महादिव्यं सर्वमायाविनाशनम् ॥
2.5.m:
Seeing that, Śaṅkara then effortlessly hurled the Māheśvara missile,
greatly divine, which destroys all illusory powers.

2.5.s:
tejasā tasya tanmāyā naṣṭāścāsan drutaṃ tadā |
divyānyastrāṇi tānyeva nistejāṃsyabhavannapi ||
2.5.d:
तेजसा तस्य तन्माया नष्टाश्चासन् द्रुतं तदा ।
दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि तान्येव निस्तेजांस्यभवन्नपि ॥
2.5.m:
By its splendor, his illusions were immediately destroyed,
and even those divine missiles of his became devoid of splendor.

2.5.s:
atha yuddhe maheśānastadvadhāya mahābalaḥ |
śūlaṃ jagrāha sahasā durnivāryaṃ sutejasām ||
2.5.d:
अथ युद्धे महेशानस्तद्वधाय महाबलः ।
शूलं जग्राह सहसा दुर्निवार्यं सुतेजसाम् ॥
2.5.m:
Then, in the battle, the mighty Maheśāna, in order to slay him,
suddenly grasped his trident, irresistible and of great brilliance.

2.5.s:
tadaiva tanniṣeddhuṃ ca vāgbabhūvāśarīriṇī |
kṣipa śūlaṃ na cedānīṃ prārthanāṃ śṛṇu śaṅkara ||
2.5.d:
तदैव तन्निषेद्धुं च वाग्बभूवाशरीरिणी ।
क्षिप शूलं न चेदानीं प्रार्थनां शृणु शङ्कर ॥
2.5.m:
At that very moment, an unembodied voice arose to restrain it:
"Do not cast the trident now, Śaṅkara; listen to my request!

2.5.s:
sarvathā tvaṃ samartho hi kṣaṇād brahmāṇḍanāśane |
kimekadānavasyeśa śaṅkhacūḍasya sāmpratam ||
2.5.d:
सर्वथा त्वं समर्थो हि क्षणाद् ब्रह्माण्डनाशने ।
किमेकदानवस्येश शङ्खचूडस्य साम्प्रतम् ॥
2.5.m:
Indeed, you are entirely capable of destroying the universe in a single moment;
what is one dānava, Śaṅkhacūḍa, to you now, O Lord?

2.5.s:
tathāpi vedamaryādā na nāśyā svāminā tvayā |
tāṃ śṛṇuṣva mahādeva saphalaṃ kuru satyataḥ ||
2.5.d:
तथापि वेदमर्यादा न नाश्या स्वामिना त्वया ।
तां शृणुष्व महादेव सफलं कुरु सत्यतः ॥
2.5.m:
Even so, the ordinance of the Veda must not be broken by you, the master;
listen to it, Mahādeva, and make it truly fulfilled.

2.5.s:
yāvadasya kare'tyugraṃ kavacaṃ paramaṃ hareḥ |
yāvatsatītvamastyeva satyā asyasya yoṣitaḥ ||
2.5.d:
यावदस्य करेऽत्युग्रं कवचं परमं हरेः ।
यावत्सतीत्वमस्त्येव सत्या अस्यस्य योषितः ॥
2.5.m:
As long as the supreme, most formidable armor of Hari is in his hand,
and as long as the chastity of his devoted wife remains intact,

2.5.s:
tāvadasya jarāmṛtyuḥ śaṅkhacūḍasya śaṅkara |
nāstītyavitathaṃ nātha vidhehi brahmaṇo vacaḥ ||
2.5.d:
तावदस्य जरामृत्युः शङ्खचूडस्य शङ्कर ।
नास्तीत्यवितथं नाथ विधेहि ब्रह्मणो वचः ॥
2.5.m:
so long does Śaṅkhacūḍa have neither old age nor death, O Śaṅkara;
make Brahmā's word true, O Lord!"

2.5.s:
ityākarṇya nabhovāṇīṃ tathetyukte hare tadā |
harecchayāgato viṣṇustaṃ dideśa satāṃ gatiḥ ||
2.5.d:
इत्याकर्ण्य नभोवाणीं तथेत्युक्ते हरे तदा ।
हरेच्छयागतो विष्णुस्तं दिदेश सतां गतिः ॥
2.5.m:
Hearing that heavenly voice, when Hara said, "So be it,"
Viṣṇu, the refuge of the virtuous, arrived by Hara's will and gave instructions to him.

2.5.s:
vṛddhabrāhmaṇaveṣeṇa viṣṇurmāyāvināṃ varaḥ |
śaṅkhacūḍopakaṇṭhaṃ ca gatvovāca sa taṃ tadā ||
2.5.d:
वृद्धब्राह्मणवेषेण विष्णुर्मायाविनां वरः ।
शङ्खचूडोपकण्ठं च गत्वोवाच स तं तदा ॥
2.5.m:
Assuming the guise of an old brahmin, Viṣṇu, the foremost of magicians,
approached Śaṅkhacūḍa and spoke to him at that time.

2.5.s:
vṛddhabrāhmaṇa uvāca |
dehi bhikṣāṃ dānavendra mahyaṃ prāptāya sāmpratam ||
2.5.d:
वृद्धब्राह्मण उवाच ।
देहि भिक्षां दानवेन्द्र मह्यं प्राप्ताय साम्प्रतम् ॥
2.5.m:
The old brahmin said:
"O lord of the dānavas, give alms to me who have just arrived.

2.5.s:
nedānīṃ kathayiṣyāmi prakaṭaṃ dīnavatsalam |
paścāttvāṃ kathayiṣyāmi punaḥ satyaṃ kariṣyasi ||
2.5.d:
नेदानीं कथयिष्यामि प्रकटं दीनवत्सलम् ।
पश्चात्त्वां कथयिष्यामि पुनः सत्यं करिष्यसि ॥
2.5.m:
I shall not speak [my request] openly now, O you who are kind to the wretched;
I will tell you later, and then you shall fulfill your promise."

2.5.s:
omityuvāca rājendraḥ prasannavadanekṣaṇaḥ |
kavacārthī janaścāhamityuvāceti sacchalāt ||
2.5.d:
ओमित्युवाच राजेन्द्रः प्रसन्नवदनेक्षणः ।
कवचार्थी जनश्चाहमित्युवाचेति सच्छलात् ॥
2.5.m: "Om," said the king of kings with a cheerful face and eyes. / "I am a man who seeks [your] armor," he said deceptively.

2.5.s:
tacchrutvā dānavendro'sau brahmaṇyaḥ satyavāgvibhuḥ |
tad dadau kavacaṃ divyaṃ viprāya prāṇasammatam ||
2.5.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा दानवेन्द्रोऽसौ ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यवाग्विभुः ।
तद् ददौ कवचं दिव्यं विप्राय प्राणसम्मतम् ॥
2.5.m: Hearing that, the lord of the Dānavas, devoted to brahmins, truthful in speech, and mighty, / gave that divine armor, which was dear to him as his own life, to the brahmin.

2.5.s:
māyayetthaṃ tu kavacaṃ tasmājjagrāha vai hariḥ |
śaṅkhacūḍasya rūpeṇa jagāma tulasīṃ prati ||
2.5.d:
माययेत्थं तु कवचं तस्माज्जग्राह वै हरिः ।
शङ्खचूडस्य रूपेण जगाम तुलसीं प्रति ॥
2.5.m: Through illusion Hari thus took the armor from him; / assuming the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa, he went toward Tulasī.

2.5.s:
gatvā tatra haristasyā yonau māyāviśāradaḥ |
vīryādhānaṃ cakārāśu devakāryārthamīśvaraḥ ||
2.5.d:
गत्वा तत्र हरिस्तस्या योनौ मायाविशारदः ।
वीर्याधानं चकाराशु देवकार्यार्थमीश्वरः ॥
2.5.m: Having gone there, Hari, skilled in illusion, the Lord, / quickly placed his seed into her womb for the sake of the gods' mission.

2.5.s:
etasminnantare śambhumīrayan svavacaḥ prabhuḥ |
śaṅkhacūḍavadhārthāya śūlaṃ jagrāha prajvalat ||
2.5.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शम्भुमीरयन् स्ववचः प्रभुः ।
शङ्खचूडवधार्थाय शूलं जग्राह प्रज्वलत् ॥
2.5.m: Meanwhile the lord Śambhu, uttering his own word, / seized his blazing trident in order to slay Śaṅkhacūḍa.

2.5.s:
tacchūlaṃ vijayaṃ nāma śaṅkarasya parātmanaḥ |
sañcakāśe diśaḥ sarvā rodasīṃ samprakāśayan ||
2.5.d:
तच्छूलं विजयं नाम शङ्करस्य परात्मनः ।
सञ्चकाशे दिशः सर्वा रोदसीं सम्प्रकाशयन् ॥
2.5.m: That trident named Vijaya, belonging to Śaṅkara, the supreme Self, / shone forth, illuminating all the quarters and heaven and earth,

2.5.s:
koṭimadhyāhnamārtaṇḍapralayāgniśikhopamam |
durnivāryaṃ ca durddharṣamavyarthaṃ vairighātakam ||
2.5.d:
कोटिमध्याह्नमार्तण्डप्रलयाग्निशिखोपमम् ।
दुर्निवार्यं च दुर्द्धर्षमव्यर्थं वैरिघातकम् ॥
2.5.m: resembling ten million midday suns and flames of the fire of cosmic dissolution, / irresistible and unassailable, unfailing, the slayer of enemies,

2.5.s:
tejasāṃ cakramatyugraṃ sarvaśastrāstranāyakam |
surāsurāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ duḥsahaṃ ca bhayaṅkaram ||
2.5.d:
तेजसां चक्रमत्युग्रं सर्वशस्त्रास्त्रनायकम् ।
सुरासुराणां सर्वेषां दुःसहं च भयङ्करम् ॥
2.5.m: an exceedingly fierce wheel of splendors, the chief of all weapons and missiles, / unbearable and terrifying to all the gods and Asuras,

2.5.s:
saṃhartuṃ sarvabrahmāḍamavalambya ca līlayā |
saṃsthitaṃ paramaṃ tatra ekatrībhūya vijvalat ||
2.5.d:
संहर्तुं सर्वब्रह्माडमवलम्ब्य च लीलया ।
संस्थितं परमं तत्र एकत्रीभूय विज्वलत् ॥
2.5.m: standing there supreme, blazing united in one mass / as if effortlessly leaning to destroy the entire universe,

2.5.s:
dhanuḥ sahasraṃ dīrgheṇa prasthena śatahastakam |
jīvabrahmasvarūpaṃ ca nityarūpamanirmitam ||
2.5.d:
धनुः सहस्रं दीर्घेण प्रस्थेन शतहस्तकम् ।
जीवब्रह्मस्वरूपं च नित्यरूपमनिर्मितम् ॥
2.5.m: a thousand bows in length and a hundred cubits in breadth, / identical in nature to the individual soul and Brahman, eternal in form, uncreated.

2.5.s:
vibhramad vyomni tacchūlaṃ śaṅkhacūḍopari kṣaṇāt |
cakāra bhasma tacchīghraṃ nipatya śivaśāsanāt ||
2.5.d:
विभ्रमद् व्योम्नि तच्छूलं शङ्खचूडोपरि क्षणात् ।
चकार भस्म तच्छीघ्रं निपत्य शिवशासनात् ॥
2.5.m: Whirling in the sky, that trident instantly came over Śaṅkhacūḍa / and, falling by Śiva's command, swiftly reduced him to ashes.

2.5.s:
atha śūlaṃ maheśasya drutamāvṛtya śaṅkaram |
yayau vihāyasā vipra manoyāyi svakāryakṛt ||
2.5.d:
अथ शूलं महेशस्य द्रुतमावृत्य शङ्करम् ।
ययौ विहायसा विप्र मनोयायि स्वकार्यकृत् ॥
2.5.m: Then, having swiftly returned around Śaṅkara, the trident of the great Lord, / having accomplished its task, departed through the air, traveling as fast as thought, O brahmin.

2.5.s:
nedurdundubhayaḥ svarge jagurgandharvakinnarāḥ |
tuṣṭuvurmunayo devā nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ ||
2.5.d:
नेदुर्दुन्दुभयः स्वर्गे जगुर्गन्धर्वकिन्नराः ।
तुष्टुवुर्मुनयो देवा ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः ॥
2.5.m: Kettledrums sounded in heaven, Gandharvas and Kinnaras sang, / sages and gods offered praise, and hosts of Apsarases danced.

2.5.s:
babhūva puṣpavṛṣṭiśca śivasyopari santatam |
praśaśaṃsa harirbrahmā śakrādyā munayastathā ||
2.5.d:
बभूव पुष्पवृष्टिश्च शिवस्योपरि सन्ततम् ।
प्रशशंस हरिर्ब्रह्मा शक्राद्या मुनयस्तथा ॥
2.5.m: A continuous shower of flowers fell upon Śiva; / Hari, Brahmā, Śakra and others, as well as the sages, praised [him].

2.5.s:
śaṅkhacūḍo dānavendraḥ śivasya kṛpayā tadā |
śāpamukto babhūvātha pūrvarūpamavāpa ha ||
2.5.d:
शङ्खचूडो दानवेन्द्रः शिवस्य कृपया तदा ।
शापमुक्तो बभूवाथ पूर्वरूपमवाप ह ॥
2.5.m: Then the lord of the Dānavas, Śaṅkhacūḍa, by the grace of Śiva, / was freed from his curse and attained his former form.

2.5.s:
asthibhiḥ śaṅkhacūḍasya śaṅkhajātirbabhūva ha |
praśastaṃ śaṅkhatoyaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śaṅkaraṃ vinā ||
2.5.d:
अस्थिभिः शङ्खचूडस्य शङ्खजातिर्बभूव ह ।
प्रशस्तं शङ्खतोयं च सर्वेषां शङ्करं विना ॥
2.5.m: From the bones of Śaṅkhacūḍa the conch species arose; / water from a conch is praiseworthy for all, except for Śaṅkara.

2.5.s:
viśeṣeṇa harerlakṣmyāḥ śaṅkhatoyaṃ mahāpriyam |
sambandhināṃ ca tasyāpi na harasya mahāmune ||
2.5.d:
विशेषेण हरेर्लक्ष्म्याः शङ्खतोयं महाप्रियम् ।
सम्बन्धिनां च तस्यापि न हरस्य महामुने ॥
2.5.m: Water from a conch is especially very dear to Hari, to Lakṣmī, / and to his associates, but never to Hara, O great sage.

2.5.s:
tamitthaṃ śaṅkaro hatvā śivalokaṃ jagāma saḥ |
suprahṛṣṭo vṛṣārūḍhaḥ somaskandagaṇairvṛtaḥ ||
2.5.d:
तमित्थं शङ्करो हत्वा शिवलोकं जगाम सः ।
सुप्रहृष्टो वृषारूढः सोमस्कन्दगणैर्वृतः ॥
2.5.m: Having thus slain him, Śaṅkara went to the world of Śiva, / exceedingly delighted, mounted on his bull, accompanied by Umā, Skanda, and his attendants.

2.5.s:
harirjagāma vaikuṇṭhaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ svastho babhūva ha |
surāḥ svaviṣayaṃ prāpuḥ paramānandasaṃyutāḥ ||
2.5.d:
हरिर्जगाम वैकुण्ठं कृष्णः स्वस्थो बभूव ह ।
सुराः स्वविषयं प्रापुः परमानन्दसंयुताः ॥
2.5.m: Hari went to Vaikuṇṭha, Kṛṣṇa was at ease, / and the gods reached their own realms filled with supreme bliss.

2.5.s:
jagatsvāsthyamatīvāpa sarvaṃ nirvighnamāpa kam |
nirmalaṃ cābhavadvyoma kṣitiḥ sarvā sumaṅgalā ||
2.5.d:
जगत्स्वास्थ्यमतीवाप सर्वं निर्विघ्नमाप कम् ।
निर्मलं चाभवद्व्योम क्षितिः सर्वा सुमङ्गला ॥
2.5.m: The world attained great peace, everything attained freedom from obstacles; / the sky became spotless, and the entire earth was most auspicious.

2.5.s:
iti proktaṃ maheśasya caritaṃ pramudāvaham |
sarvaduḥkhaharaṃ śrīdaṃ sarvakāmaprapūrakam ||
2.5.d:
इति प्रोक्तं महेशस्य चरितं प्रमुदावहम् ।
सर्वदुःखहरं श्रीदं सर्वकामप्रपूरकम् ॥
2.5.m: Thus the narrative of the great Lord, which brings delight, / removes all sorrow, bestows fortune, and fulfills all desires, has been told.

2.5.s:
dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ sarvavighnanivāraṇam |
bhuktidaṃ muktidaṃ caiva sarvakāmaphalapradam ||
2.5.d:
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं सर्वविघ्ननिवारणम् ।
भुक्तिदं मुक्तिदं चैव सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ॥
2.5.m: It brings prosperity, fame, long life, and wards off all obstacles; / it bestows enjoyment and liberation, and grants the fruit of all desires.

2.5.s:
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ |
śrāvayedvā paṭhedvāpi pāṭhayedvā sudhīrnaraḥ ||
2.5.d:
य इदं शृणुयान्नित्यं चरितं शशिमौलिनः ।
श्रावयेद्वा पठेद्वापि पाठयेद्वा सुधीर्नरः ॥
2.5.m: A wise man who constantly hears this deed of the moon-crested [Lord], / or recites it, or reads it, or causes it to be read,

2.5.s:
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ sutaṃ saukhyaṃ labhetātra na saṃśayaḥ |
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti śivabhaktiṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
2.5.d:
धनं धान्यं सुतं सौख्यं लभेतात्र न संशयः ।
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति शिवभक्तिं विशेषतः ॥
2.5.m: shall obtain wealth, grain, a son, and happiness—of this there is no doubt; / he attains all desires, especially devotion to Śiva.

2.5.s:
idamākhyānamatulaṃ sarvopadravanāśanam |
paramajñānajananaṃ śivabhaktivivarddhanam ||
2.5.d:
इदमाख्यानमतुलं सर्वोपद्रवनाशनम् ।
परमज्ञानजननं शिवभक्तिविवर्द्धनम् ॥
2.5.m: This peerless story destroys all calamities, / engenders supreme knowledge, and fosters devotion to Śiva.

2.5.s:
brāhmaṇo brahmavarcasvī kṣatriyo vijayī bhavet |
dhanāḍhyo vaiśyajaḥ śūdraḥ śṛṇvan sattamatāmiyāt ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ pañcamo yuddhakhaṇḍe
2.5.d:
ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मवर्चस्वी क्षत्रियो विजयी भवेत् ।
धनाढ्यो वैश्यजः शूद्रः शृण्वन् सत्तमतामियात् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां पञ्चमो युद्धखण्डे
2.5.m:
By hearing it, a brāhmaṇa becomes endowed with holy radiance, a kṣatriya victorious, / a vaiśya rich in wealth, and a śūdra attains excellence.

Thus ends the fortieth chapter, titled "The Slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa," in the Yuddhakhaṇḍa, the fifth [section] of the second Rudrasaṃhitā, in the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.5.s:
vyāsa uvāca |
nārāyaṇaśca bhagavān vīryādhānaṃ cakāra ha |
tulasyāḥ kena yatnena yonau tadvaktumarhasi ||
2.5.d:
व्यास उवाच ।
नारायणश्च भगवान् वीर्याधानं चकार ह ।
तुलस्याः केन यत्नेन योनौ तद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
2.5.m: Vyāsa said: / The blessed Nārāyaṇa placed his seed / into the womb of Tulasī: with what effort [did he do so]? Please tell that.

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
nārāyaṇo hi devānāṃ kāryakartā satāṃ gatiḥ |
śaṅkhacūḍasya rūpeṇa reme tadrāmayā saha ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
नारायणो हि देवानां कार्यकर्ता सतां गतिः ।
शङ्खचूडस्य रूपेण रेमे तद्रामया सह ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Nārāyaṇa, the accomplisher of the work of the gods and the refuge of the virtuous, / sportively enjoyed that beautiful woman in the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa.

2.5.s:
tadeva śṛṇu viṣṇośca caritaṃ pramudāvaham |
śivaśāsanakartuśca mātuśca jagatāṃ hareḥ ||
2.5.d:
तदेव शृणु विष्णोश्च चरितं प्रमुदावहम् ।
शिवशासनकर्तुश्च मातुश्च जगतां हरेः ॥
2.5.m: Hear that delightful story of Viṣṇu, / the mother of the worlds, Hari, who executed Śiva's command.

2.5.s:
raṇamadhye vyomavacaḥ śrutvā devena śambhunā |
preritaḥ śaṅkhacūḍasya gṛhītvā kavacaṃ param ||
2.5.d:
रणमध्ये व्योमवचः श्रुत्वा देवेन शम्भुना ।
प्रेरितः शङ्खचूडस्य गृहीत्वा कवचं परम् ॥
2.5.m: Hearing the voice from the sky in the midst of the battle, / prompted by the divine lord Śambhu, Hari took the supreme armor of Śaṅkhacūḍa,

2.5.s:
viprarūpeṇa tvaritaṃ māyayā nijayā hariḥ |
jagāma śaṅkhacūḍasya rūpeṇa tulasīgṛham ||
2.5.d:
विप्ररूपेण त्वरितं मायया निजया हरिः ।
जगाम शङ्खचूडस्य रूपेण तुलसीगृहम् ॥
2.5.m: and swiftly, having assumed the form of a brahmin, Hari, through his own illusion, / went to the house of Tulasī in the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa.

2.5.s:
dundubhiṃ vādayāmāsa tulasīdvārasannidhau |
jayaśabdaṃ ca tatraiva bodhayāmāsa sundarīm ||
2.5.d:
दुन्दुभिं वादयामास तुलसीद्वारसन्निधौ ।
जयशब्दं च तत्रैव बोधयामास सुन्दरीम् ॥
2.5.m: He caused the kettledrum to be sounded near the door of Tulasī / and raised a cry of victory right there, waking that beautiful woman.

2.5.s:
tacchrutvā caiva sā sādhvī paramānandasaṃyutā |
rājamārgaṃ gavākṣeṇa dadarśa paramādarāt ||
2.5.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा चैव सा साध्वी परमानन्दसंयुता ।
राजमार्गं गवाक्षेण ददर्श परमादरात् ॥
2.5.m: Hearing that, the chaste woman was filled with supreme joy / and looked out onto the royal highway through the latticed window with great reverence.

2.5.s:
brāhmaṇebhyo dhanaṃ dattvā kārayāmāsa maṅgalam |
drutaṃ cakāra śṛṅgāraṃ jñātvā''yātaṃ nijaṃ patim ||
2.5.d:
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनं दत्त्वा कारयामास मङ्गलम् ।
द्रुतं चकार शृङ्गारं ज्ञात्वा'ऽयातं निजं पतिम् ॥
2.5.m: Giving wealth to the brahmins, she had auspicious ceremonies performed; / she quickly adorned herself, knowing that her own husband had arrived.

2.5.s:
avaruhya rathādviṣṇustaddevyā bhavanaṃ yayau |
śaṅkhacūḍasvarūpaḥ sa māyāvī devakāryakṛt ||
2.5.d:
अवरुह्य रथाद्विष्णुस्तद्देव्या भवनं ययौ ।
शङ्खचूडस्वरूपः स मायावी देवकार्यकृत् ॥
2.5.m: Descending from his chariot, Viṣṇu went to that lady's mansion, / having the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa, full of illusion, accomplishing the gods' mission.

2.5.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ ca puraḥ prāptaṃ svakāntaṃ sā mudānvitā |
tatpādau kṣālayāmāsa nanāma ca ruroda ca ||
2.5.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं च पुरः प्राप्तं स्वकान्तं सा मुदान्विता ।
तत्पादौ क्षालयामास ननाम च रुरोद च ॥
2.5.m: Seeing her own beloved arrived before her, filled with joy, / she washed his feet, bowed down, and wept.

2.5.s:
ratnasiṃhāsane ramye vāsayāmāsa maṅgalam |
tāmbūlaṃ ca dadau tasmai karpūrādisuvāsitam ||
2.5.d:
रत्नसिंहासने रम्ये वासयामास मङ्गलम् ।
ताम्बूलं च ददौ तस्मै कर्पूरादिसुवासितम् ॥
2.5.m: She seated the auspicious [guest] on a charming jewel-throne / and gave him betel seasoned with camphor and other spices.

2.5.s:
adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvanaṃ sambabhūva ha |
raṇe gataṃ ca prāṇeśaṃ paśyantyāśca punargṛhe ||
2.5.d:
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म जीवनं सम्बभूव ह ।
रणे गतं च प्राणेशं पश्यन्त्याश्च पुनर्गृहे ॥
2.5.m: "Today my birth and my life have become fruitful, / as I see the lord of my life, who had gone to battle, back home again."

2.5.s:
ityuktvā sakaṭākṣaṃ sā nirīkṣya sasmitaṃ mudā |
papraccha raṇavṛttāntaṃ kāntaṃ madhurayā girā ||
2.5.d:
इत्युक्त्वा सकटाक्षं सा निरीक्ष्य सस्मितं मुदा ।
पप्रच्छ रणवृत्तान्तं कान्तं मधुरया गिरा ॥
2.5.m: Having said this, looking at him with side-glances and smiling with joy, / she inquired about the events of the battle from her beloved with a sweet voice.

2.5.s:
tulasyuvāca |
asaṅkhyaviśvasaṃhartā sa devapravaraḥ prabhuḥ |
yasyājñāvarttino devā viṣṇubrahmādayaḥ sadā ||
2.5.d:
तुलस्युवाच ।
असङ्ख्यविश्वसंहर्ता स देवप्रवरः प्रभुः ।
यस्याज्ञावर्त्तिनो देवा विष्णुब्रह्मादयः सदा ॥
2.5.m: Tulasī said: / That foremost of gods, the Lord, is the destroyer of countless universes; / Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and the other gods always obey his command.

2.5.s:
tridevajanakaḥ so'tra triguṇātmā ca nirguṇaḥ |
bhaktecchayā ca saguṇo haribrahmāpravartakaḥ ||
2.5.d:
त्रिदेवजनकः सोऽत्र त्रिगुणात्मा च निर्गुणः ।
भक्तेच्छया च सगुणो हरिब्रह्माप्रवर्तकः ॥
2.5.m: He is the progenitor of the three gods here, consisting of the three qualities and free from qualities; / endowed with qualities by the desire of his devotees, he is the activator of Hari and Brahmā.

2.5.s:
kuberasya prārthanayā guṇarūpadharo haraḥ |
kailāsavāsī gaṇapaḥ parabrahma satāṃ gatiḥ ||
2.5.d:
कुबेरस्य प्रार्थनया गुणरूपधरो हरः ।
कैलासवासी गणपः परब्रह्म सतां गतिः ॥
2.5.m: At the request of Kubera, Hara assumed a form with qualities; / he resides on Kailāsa, is the lord of the attendants, the supreme Brahman, and the refuge of the virtuous.

2.5.s:
yasyaikapalamātreṇa koṭibrahmāṇḍasaṅkṣayaḥ |
viṣṇubrahmādayo'tītā bahavaḥ kṣaṇamātrataḥ ||
2.5.d:
यस्यैकपलमात्रेण कोटिब्रह्माण्डसङ्क्षयः ।
विष्णुब्रह्मादयोऽतीता बहवः क्षणमात्रतः ॥
2.5.m: In a mere moment of his time, ten million universes perish; / many like Viṣṇu and Brahmā pass away in a single instant.

2.5.s:
kartuṃ sārddhaṃ ca tenaiva samaraṃ tvaṃ gataḥ prabho |
kathaṃ babhūva saṅgrāmastena devasahāyinā ||
2.5.d:
कर्तुं सार्द्धं च तेनैव समरं त्वं गतः प्रभो ।
कथं बभूव सङ्ग्रामस्तेन देवसहायिना ॥
2.5.m: You went to wage war with him, O Lord; / how was the battle with him, who is aided by the gods?

2.5.s:
kuśalī tvamihāyātastaṃ jitvā parameśvaram |
kathaṃ babhūva vijayastava brūhi tadeva me ||
2.5.d:
कुशली त्वमिहायातस्तं जित्वा परमेश्वरम् ।
कथं बभूव विजयस्तव ब्रूहि तदेव मे ॥
2.5.m: You have returned here safe, having conquered that Parameśvara; / tell me just that: how did your victory come to be?

2.5.s:
śrutvetthaṃ tulasīvākyaṃ sa vihasya ramāpatiḥ |
śaṅkhacūḍarūpadharastāmuvācāmṛtaṃ vacaḥ ||
2.5.d:
श्रुत्वेत्थं तुलसीवाक्यं स विहस्य रमापतिः ।
शङ्खचूडरूपधरस्तामुवाचामृतं वचः ॥
2.5.m: Hearing these words of Tulasī, the husband of Ramā, / smiling and wearing the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa, spoke sweet nectar-like words to her:

2.5.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yadāhaṃ raṇabhūmau ca jagāma samarapriyaḥ |
kolāhalo mahān jātaḥ pravṛtto'bhūnmahāraṇaḥ ||
2.5.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
यदाहं रणभूमौ च जगाम समरप्रियः ।
कोलाहलो महान् जातः प्रवृत्तोऽभून्महारणः ॥
2.5.m: The Blessed Lord said: / 'When I, fond of battle, went to the battlefield, / a great uproar arose, and a mighty battle began.

2.5.s:
devadānavayoryuddhaṃ sambabhūva jayaiṣiṇoḥ |
daityāḥ parājitāstatra nirjarairbalagarvitaiḥ ||
2.5.d:
देवदानवयोर्युद्धं सम्बभूव जयैषिणोः ।
दैत्याः पराजितास्तत्र निर्जरैर्बलगर्वितैः ॥
2.5.m: A battle took place between the gods and the dānavas, both desirous of victory; / there the daityas were defeated by the gods, proud of their strength.

2.5.s:
tadāhaṃ samaraṃ tatrākārṣaṃ devairbalotkaṭaiḥ |
parājitāśca te devāḥ śaṅkaraṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ ||
2.5.d:
तदाहं समरं तत्राकार्षं देवैर्बलोत्कटैः ।
पराजिताश्च ते देवाः शङ्करं शरणं ययुः ॥
2.5.m: Then I fought a battle there against the gods of immense strength; / and those gods, being defeated, went to Śaṅkara for refuge.

2.5.s:
rudro'pi tatsahāyārthamājagāma raṇaṃ prati |
tenāhaṃ vai ciraṃ kālamayautsaṃ baladarpitaḥ ||
2.5.d:
रुद्रोऽपि तत्सहायार्थमाजगाम रणं प्रति ।
तेनाहं वै चिरं कालमयौत्सं बलदर्पितः ॥
2.5.m: Rudra also came to the battle to assist them; / with him I, arrogant with strength, fought for a long time.

2.5.s:
āvayoḥ samaraḥ kānte pūrṇamabdaṃ babhūva ha |
nāśo babhūva sarveṣāmasurāṇāṃ ca kāmini ||
2.5.d:
आवयोः समरः कान्ते पूर्णमब्दं बभूव ह ।
नाशो बभूव सर्वेषामसुराणां च कामिनि ॥
2.5.m: The battle between the two of us lasted for a full year, O beloved; / and all the asuras were destroyed, O lovely woman!

2.5.s:
prītiṃ ca kārayāmāsa brahmā ca svayamāvayoḥ |
devānāmadhikārāśca pradattā brahmaśāsanāt ||
2.5.d:
प्रीतिं च कारयामास ब्रह्मा च स्वयमावयोः ।
देवानामधिकाराश्च प्रदत्ता ब्रह्मशासनात् ॥
2.5.m: Brahmā himself brought about peace between the two of us, / and the dominions of the gods were restored by the command of Brahmā.

2.5.s:
mayāgataṃ svabhavanaṃ śivalokaṃ śivo gataḥ |
sarvasvāsthyamatīvāpa dūrībhūto hyupadravaḥ ||
2.5.d:
मयागतं स्वभवनं शिवलोकं शिवो गतः ।
सर्वस्वास्थ्यमतीवाप दूरीभूतो ह्युपद्रवः ॥
2.5.m: I came to my own abode, and Śiva went to the world of Śiva; / complete well-being was restored, and all disturbance was removed.'

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
ityuktvā jagatāṃ nāthaḥ śayanaṃ ca cakāra ha |
reme ramāpatistatra ramayā sa tayā mudā ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा जगतां नाथः शयनं च चकार ह ।
रेमे रमापतिस्तत्र रमया स तया मुदा ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Having spoken thus, the lord of the worlds went to bed; / there the husband of Ramā joyfully took delight with her as with Ramā.

2.5.s:
sā sādhvī sukhasambhāvākarṣaṇasya vyatikramāt |
sarvaṃ vitarkayāmāsa kastvamevetyuvāca sā ||
2.5.d:
सा साध्वी सुखसम्भावाकर्षणस्य व्यतिक्रमात् ।
सर्वं वितर्कयामास कस्त्वमेवेत्युवाच सा ॥
2.5.m: Because of a deviation in the manner of sexual enjoyment, that chaste woman / suspected everything, and she said, 'Who are you, indeed?'

2.5.s:
tulasyuvāca |
ko vā tvaṃ vada māmāśu bhuktāhaṃ māyayā tvayā |
dūrīkṛtaṃ matsatītvamatha tvāṃ vai śapāmyaham ||
2.5.d:
तुलस्युवाच ।
को वा त्वं वद मामाशु भुक्ताहं मायया त्वया ।
दूरीकृतं मत्सतीत्वमथ त्वां वै शपाम्यहम् ॥
2.5.m: Tulasī said: / 'Tell me at once, who are you? I have been enjoyed by you through illusion! / My chastity has been destroyed; therefore, I surely curse you!'

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
tulasīvacanaṃ śrutvā hariḥ śāpabhayena ca |
dadhāra līlayā brahmansvamūrtiṃ sumanoharām ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
तुलसीवचनं श्रुत्वा हरिः शापभयेन च ।
दधार लीलया ब्रह्मन्स्वमूर्तिं सुमनोहराम् ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Hearing Tulasī's words and fearing a curse, / Hari sportively assumed his own very charming form, O sage.

2.5.s:
tad dṛṣṭvā tulasī rūpaṃ jñātvā viṣṇuṃ tu cihnataḥ |
pātivratyaparityāgāt kruddhā sā tamuvāca ha ||
2.5.d:
तद् दृष्ट्वा तुलसी रूपं ज्ञात्वा विष्णुं तु चिह्नतः ।
पातिव्रत्यपरित्यागात् क्रुद्धा सा तमुवाच ह ॥
2.5.m: Seeing that form and recognizing Viṣṇu by his marks, / she, enraged by the violation of her wifely fidelity, spoke to him:

2.5.s:
tulasyuvāca |
he viṣṇo te dayā nāsti pāṣāṇasadṛśaṃ manaḥ |
patidharmasya bhaṅgena mama svāmī hataḥ khalu ||
2.5.d:
तुलस्युवाच ।
हे विष्णो ते दया नास्ति पाषाणसदृशं मनः ।
पतिधर्मस्य भङ्गेन मम स्वामी हतः खलु ॥
2.5.m: Tulasī said: / 'O Viṣṇu, you have no compassion; your mind is like a stone! / Truly, my husband has been slain through the destruction of wifely virtue.

2.5.s:
pāṣāṇasadṛśastvaṃ ca dayāhīno yataḥ khalaḥ |
tasmātpāṣāṇarūpastvaṃ macchāpena bhavādhunā ||
2.5.d:
पाषाणसदृशस्त्वं च दयाहीनो यतः खलः ।
तस्मात्पाषाणरूपस्त्वं मच्छापेन भवाधुना ॥
2.5.m: Since you are like a stone, void of compassion and wicked, / therefore, by my curse, become a stone right now!

2.5.s:
ye vadanti dayāsindhuṃ tvāṃ bhrāntāste na saṃśayaḥ |
bhakto vināparādhena parārthe ca kathaṃ hataḥ ||
2.5.d:
ये वदन्ति दयासिन्धुं त्वां भ्रान्तास्ते न संशयः ।
भक्तो विनापराधेन परार्थे च कथं हतः ॥
2.5.m: Those who call you an ocean of compassion are deluded, without doubt; / how could a devotee be slain without fault for the sake of another?'

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
ityuktvā tulasī sā vai śaṅkhacūḍapriyā satī |
bhṛśaṃ ruroda śokārtā vilalāpa bhṛśaṃ muhuḥ ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा तुलसी सा वै शङ्खचूडप्रिया सती ।
भृशं रुरोद शोकार्ता विललाप भृशं मुहुः ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Having spoken thus, Tulasī, that chaste woman dear to Śaṅkhacūḍa, / wept bitterly, afflicted with grief, and lamented repeatedly.

2.5.s:
tatastāṃ rudatīṃ dṛṣṭvā sa viṣṇuḥ parameśvaraḥ |
sasmāra śaṅkaraṃ devaṃ yena sammohitaṃ jagat ||
2.5.d:
ततस्तां रुदतीं दृष्ट्वा स विष्णुः परमेश्वरः ।
सस्मार शङ्करं देवं येन सम्मोहितं जगत् ॥
2.5.m: Then, seeing her weeping, Viṣṇu, the supreme lord, / remembered god Śaṅkara, by whom the world is enchanted.

2.5.s:
tataḥ prādurbabhūvātha śaṅkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ |
hariṇā praṇataścāsītsannuto vinayena saḥ ||
2.5.d:
ततः प्रादुर्बभूवाथ शङ्करो भक्तवत्सलः ।
हरिणा प्रणतश्चासीत्सन्नुतो विनयेन सः ॥
2.5.m: Thereupon Śaṅkara, affectionate toward devotees, appeared; / he was saluted by Hari and praised with humility.

2.5.s:
śokākulaṃ hariṃ dṛṣṭvā vilapantīṃ ca tatpriyām |
nayena bodhayāmāsa taṃ tāṃ kṛpaṇavatsalām ||
2.5.d:
शोकाकुलं हरिं दृष्ट्वा विलपन्तीं च तत्प्रियाम् ।
नयेन बोधयामास तं तां कृपणवत्सलाम् ॥
2.5.m: Seeing Hari agitated by grief and his beloved lamenting, / he, compassionate to the miserable, instructed him and her with wisdom:

2.5.s:
śaṅkara uvāca |
mā rodīstulasi tvaṃ hi bhuṅkte karmaphalaṃ janaḥ |
sukhaduḥkhado na ko'pyasti saṃsāre karmasāgare ||
2.5.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ।
मा रोदीस्तुलसि त्वं हि भुङ्क्ते कर्मफलं जनः ।
सुखदुःखदो न कोऽप्यस्ति संसारे कर्मसागरे ॥
2.5.m: Śaṅkara said: / 'Do not weep, Tulasī! A person enjoys the fruit of their own actions; / there is no one who gives pleasure or pain in this world, which is an ocean of action.

2.5.s:
prastutaṃ śṛṇu nirduḥkhaṃ śṛṇoti sumanā hariḥ |
dvayoḥ sukhakaraṃ yattad bravīmi sukhahetave ||
2.5.d:
प्रस्तुतं शृणु निर्दुःखं शृणोति सुमना हरिः ।
द्वयोः सुखकरं यत्तद् ब्रवीमि सुखहेतवे ॥
2.5.m: Listen without sorrow to what is at hand; Hari is listening with an attentive mind; / I shall speak what brings happiness to both of you, for the sake of your joy.

2.5.s:
tapastvayā kṛtaṃ bhadre tasyaiva tapasaḥ phalam |
tadanyathā kathaṃ syādvai jātaṃ tvayi tathā ca tat ||
2.5.d:
तपस्त्वया कृतं भद्रे तस्यैव तपसः फलम् ।
तदन्यथा कथं स्याद्वै जातं त्वयि तथा च तत् ॥
2.5.m: Austerity was performed by you, O auspicious one, and this is the fruit of that very austerity; / how could that be otherwise? It has indeed happened to you thus.

2.5.s:
idaṃ śarīraṃ tyaktvā ca divyadehaṃ vidhāya ca |
ramasva hariṇā nityaṃ ramayā sadṛśī bhava ||
2.5.d:
इदं शरीरं त्यक्त्वा च दिव्यदेहं विधाय च ।
रमस्व हरिणा नित्यं रमया सदृशी भव ॥
2.5.m: Casting off this body and assuming a divine form, / take delight perpetually with Hari and become equal to Ramā.

2.5.s:
taveyaṃ tanurutsṛṣṭā nadīrūpā bhavediha |
bhārate puṇyarūpā sā gaṇḍakīti ca viśrutā ||
2.5.d:
तवेयं तनुरुत्सृष्टा नदीरूपा भवेदिह ।
भारते पुण्यरूपा सा गण्डकीति च विश्रुता ॥
2.5.m: This discarded body of yours shall become a river in this world, / in the land of Bhārata, meritorious and renowned as the Gaṇḍakī.

2.5.s:
kiyatkālaṃ mahādevi devapūjanasādhane |
pradhānarūpā tulasī bhaviṣyati vareṇa me ||
2.5.d:
कियत्कालं महादेवि देवपूजनसाधने ।
प्रधानरूपा तुलसी भविष्यति वरेण मे ॥
2.5.m: For some time, O great goddess, by my boon, / Tulasī shall become the principal medium in the worship of the gods.

2.5.s:
svarge martye ca pātāle tiṣṭha tvaṃ harisannidhau |
bhava tvaṃ tulasīvṛkṣo varā puṣpeṣu sundari ||
2.5.d:
स्वर्गे मर्त्ये च पाताले तिष्ठ त्वं हरिसन्निधौ ।
भव त्वं तुलसीवृक्षो वरा पुष्पेषु सुन्दरि ॥
2.5.m: In heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld, stay in the presence of Hari; / become the Tulasī plant, best among blossoms, O beautiful woman!

2.5.s:
vṛkṣādhiṣṭhātṛdevī tvaṃ vaikuṇṭhe divyarūpiṇī |
sārdhaṃ rahasi hariṇā nityaṃ krīḍāṃ kariṣyasi ||
2.5.d:
वृक्षाधिष्ठातृदेवी त्वं वैकुण्ठे दिव्यरूपिणी ।
सार्धं रहसि हरिणा नित्यं क्रीडां करिष्यसि ॥
2.5.m: As the presiding deity of the plant with a divine form in Vaikuṇṭha, / you will constantly engage in secret sport with Hari.

2.5.s:
nadyadhiṣṭhātṛdevī yā bhārate bahupuṇyadā |
lavaṇodasya patnī sā haryaṃśasya bhaviṣyasi ||
2.5.d:
नद्यधिष्ठातृदेवी या भारते बहुपुण्यदा ।
लवणोदस्य पत्नी सा हर्यंशस्य भविष्यसि ॥
2.5.m: As the presiding deity of the river in Bhārata, bestowing great merit, / you shall become the wife of the salt ocean, a portion of Hari.

2.5.s:
harirvai śailarūpī ca gaṇḍakī tīrasannidhau |
saṅkariṣyatyadhiṣṭhānaṃ bhārate tava śāpataḥ ||
2.5.d:
हरिर्वै शैलरूपी च गण्डकी तीरसन्निधौ ।
सङ्करिष्यत्यधिष्ठानं भारते तव शापतः ॥
2.5.m: Hari, in the form of a mountain on the bank of the Gaṇḍakī, / will make his abode in Bhārata because of your curse.

2.5.s:
tatra koṭyaśca kīṭāśca tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrā bhayaṅkarāḥ |
tacchittvā kuhare cakraṃ kariṣyanti tadīyakam ||
2.5.d:
तत्र कोट्यश्च कीटाश्च तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रा भयङ्कराः ।
तच्छित्त्वा कुहरे चक्रं करिष्यन्ति तदीयकम् ॥
2.5.m: There, millions of worms with sharp and dreadful teeth / will pierce it and create his discus inside its cavity.

2.5.s:
śālagrāmaśilā sā hi tadbhedādatipuṇyadā |
lakṣmīnārāyaṇākhyādiścakrabhedādbhaviṣyati ||
2.5.d:
शालग्रामशिला सा हि तद्भेदादतिपुण्यदा ।
लक्ष्मीनारायणाख्यादिश्चक्रभेदाद्भविष्यति ॥
2.5.m: That śālagrāma stone is indeed extremely meritorious through those varieties; / it will be known as Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa and so forth, based on the varieties of discuses.

2.5.s:
śālagrāmaśilā viṣṇostulasyāstava saṅgamaḥ |
sadā sādṛśyarūpā yā bahupuṇyavivarddhinī ||
2.5.d:
शालग्रामशिला विष्णोस्तुलस्यास्तव सङ्गमः ।
सदा सादृश्यरूपा या बहुपुण्यविवर्द्धिनी ॥
2.5.m: The union of the śālagrāma stone of Viṣṇu and you, Tulasī, / is an eternal companionship that increases abundant merit.

2.5.s:
tulasīpatravicchedaṃ śālagrāme karoti yaḥ |
tasya janmāntare bhadre strīvicchedo bhaviṣyati ||
2.5.d:
तुलसीपत्रविच्छेदं शालग्रामे करोति यः ।
तस्य जन्मान्तरे भद्रे स्त्रीविच्छेदो भविष्यति ॥
2.5.m: Whoever separates a Tulasī leaf from a śālagrāma stone / will suffer separation from his wife in another birth, O auspicious one.

2.5.s:
tulasīpatravicchedaṃ śaṅkhaṃ hitvā karoti yaḥ |
bhāryāhīno bhavetso'pi rogī syātsaptajanmasu ||
2.5.d:
तुलसीपत्रविच्छेदं शङ्खं हित्वा करोति यः ।
भार्याहीनो भवेत्सोऽपि रोगी स्यात्सप्तजन्मसु ॥
2.5.m: Whoever separates a Tulasī leaf while abandoning the conch, / he too will become deprived of a wife and be diseased for seven births.

2.5.s:
śālagrāmaśca tulasī śaṅkhaṃ caikatra eva hi |
yo rakṣati mahājñānī sa bhavecchrīharipriyaḥ ||
2.5.d:
शालग्रामश्च तुलसी शङ्खं चैकत्र एव हि ।
यो रक्षति महाज्ञानी स भवेच्छ्रीहरिप्रियः ॥
2.5.m: The great wise one who keeps the śālagrāma, / the Tulasī, and the conch together in one place becomes dear to Śrī Hari.

2.5.s:
tvaṃ priyāḥ śaṅkhacūḍasya caikamanvantarāvadhi |
śaṅkhena sārdhaṃ tvadbhedaḥ kevalaṃ duḥkhadastava ||
2.5.d:
त्वं प्रियाः शङ्खचूडस्य चैकमन्वन्तरावधि ।
शङ्खेन सार्धं त्वद्भेदः केवलं दुःखदस्तव ॥
2.5.m: You were the beloved of Śaṅkhacūḍa for the span of one manvantara; / your separation from the conch will cause you only sorrow.'

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
ityuktvā śaṅkarastatra māhātmyamūcivāṃstadā |
śālagrāmaśilāyāśca tulasyā bahupuṇyadam ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा शङ्करस्तत्र माहात्म्यमूचिवांस्तदा ।
शालग्रामशिलायाश्च तुलस्या बहुपुण्यदम् ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Having spoken thus, Śaṅkara then recited the eulogy / of the śālagrāma stone and Tulasī, which yields great merit.

2.5.s:
tataścāntarhito bhūtvā modayitvā hariṃ ca tām |
jagāma svālayaṃ śambhuḥ śarmado hi sadā satām ||
2.5.d:
ततश्चान्तर्हितो भूत्वा मोदयित्वा हरिं च ताम् ।
जगाम स्वालयं शम्भुः शर्मदो हि सदा सताम् ॥
2.5.m: Then, having gladdened Hari and her, Śambhu vanished / and went to his own abode, for he always bestows happiness on the virtuous.

2.5.s:
iti śrutvā vacaḥ śambhoḥ prasannā tu tulasyabhūt |
taddehaṃ ca parityajya divyarūpā babhūva ha ||
2.5.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचः शम्भोः प्रसन्ना तु तुलस्यभूत् ।
तद्देहं च परित्यज्य दिव्यरूपा बभूव ह ॥
2.5.m: Hearing these words of Śambhu, Tulasī became pleased; / abandoning that body, she assumed a divine form.

2.5.s:
prajagāma tayā sārddhaṃ vaikuṇṭhaṃ kamalāpatiḥ |
sadyastaddehajātā ca babhūva gaṇḍakī nadī ||
2.5.d:
प्रजगाम तया सार्द्धं वैकुण्ठं कमलापतिः ।
सद्यस्तद्देहजाता च बभूव गण्डकी नदी ॥
2.5.m: The husband of Kamalā went with her to Vaikuṇṭha; / and from her body immediately arose the Gaṇḍakī River.

2.5.s:
śailo'bhūdacyutaḥ so'pi tattīre puṇyado nṛṇām |
kurvanti tatra kīṭāśca chidraṃ bahuvidhaṃ mune ||
2.5.d:
शैलोऽभूदच्युतः सोऽपि तत्तीरे पुण्यदो नृणाम् ।
कुर्वन्ति तत्र कीटाश्च छिद्रं बहुविधं मुने ॥
2.5.m: Acyuta also became a mountain on its bank, bestowing merit on mortals; / there, O sage, the worms bore various kinds of cavities.

2.5.s:
jale patanti yāstatra śilāstāstvatipuṇyadāḥ |
sthalasthā piṅgalā jñeyāścopatāpāya caiva hi ||
2.5.d:
जले पतन्ति यास्तत्र शिलास्तास्त्वतिपुण्यदाः ।
स्थलस्था पिङ्गला ज्ञेयाश्चोपतापाय चैव हि ॥
2.5.m: Those stones that fall into the water are extremely meritorious; / those remaining on land are known to be tawny and lead to torment.

2.5.s:
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ tava praśnānusārataḥ |
caritaṃ puṇyadaṃ śambhoḥ sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām ||
2.5.d:
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं तव प्रश्नानुसारतः ।
चरितं पुण्यदं शम्भोः सर्वकामप्रदं नृणाम् ॥
2.5.m: Thus, all has been told according to your question: / the meritorious life of Śambhu, which grants all desires to mortals.

2.5.s:
ākhyānamidamākhyātaṃ viṣṇumāhātmyamiśritam |
bhuktimuktipradaṃ puṇyaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ pañcamo yuddhakhaṇḍe
2.5.d:
आख्यानमिदमाख्यातं विष्णुमाहात्म्यमिश्रितम् ।
भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं पुण्यं किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां पञ्चमो युद्धखण्डे
2.5.m:
This sacred narrative, combined with the eulogy of Viṣṇu, / which grants enjoyment and liberation, has been told. What more do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the forty-first chapter, entitled 'Description of the Curse of Tulasī' in the narrative of the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, in the fifth section, the Yuddhakhaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudrasaṃhitā, in the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.5.s:
nārada uvāca |
śaṅkhacūḍavadhaṃ śrutvā caritaṃ śaśimaulinaḥ |
ayaṃ tṛpto'smi no tvatto'mṛtaṃ pītvā yathā janaḥ ||
2.5.d:
नारद उवाच ।
शङ्खचूडवधं श्रुत्वा चरितं शशिमौलिनः ।
अयं तृप्तोऽस्मि नो त्वत्तोऽमृतं पीत्वा यथा जनः ॥
2.5.m: Nārada said: / Having heard the slaying of Śaṅkhacūḍa, the deed of the moon-crested god, / I am not sated, hearing it from you, just as a man [is never sated] drinking nectar.

2.5.s:
brahmanyaccaritaṃ tasya maheśasya mahātmanaḥ |
