2.5.m: The messenger said: / "I have been sent [and] enter the cave; this Andhaka spoke this word to you: / 'You have no need for a woman; release the woman, young and beautiful!

2.5.s:
prāyo bhavāṃstāpasastajjuṣasva kṣāntaṃ mayā yatkamanīyamantaḥ |
munirvirodhavya iti pracintya na tvaṃ munistāpasa kiṃ tu śatruḥ ||
2.5.d:
प्रायो भवांस्तापसस्तज्जुषस्व क्षान्तं मया यत्कमनीयमन्तः ।
मुनिर्विरोधव्य इति प्रचिन्त्य न त्वं मुनिस्तापस किं तु शत्रुः ॥
2.5.m: You are mostly an ascetic; practice that! What is desirable within has been endured by me, / thinking, "An ascetic should not be opposed." But you are not an ascetic, O ascetic—you are an enemy!

2.5.s:
atīva daityeṣu mahāvirodhī yudhyasva vegena mayā pramathya |
nayāmi pātālatalānurūpaṃ yamakṣayaṃ tāpasa dhūrtta hi tvām ||
2.5.d:
अतीव दैत्येषु महाविरोधी युध्यस्व वेगेन मया प्रमथ्य ।
नयामि पातालतलानुरूपं यमक्षयं तापस धूर्त्त हि त्वाम् ॥
2.5.m: You are a great adversary among the Daityas! Fight swiftly! Having crushed you with my [might], / I shall send you, O rogue ascetic, to the abode of Yama, suited to the realm of the netherworld!'"

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
etadvaco dūtamukhānniśamya kapālamālī tamuvāca kopāt |
jvalanviṣādena mahāṃstrinetraḥ satāṃ gatirduṣṭamadaprahartā ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
एतद्वचो दूतमुखान्निशम्य कपालमाली तमुवाच कोपात् ।
ज्वलन्विषादेन महांस्त्रिनेत्रः सतां गतिर्दुष्टमदप्रहर्ता ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Hearing these words from the mouth of the messenger, the wearer of the garland of skulls, the great three-eyed one, the refuge of the virtuous, the destroyer of the pride of the wicked, / blazing with indignance, spoke to him in anger.

2.5.s:
śiva uvāca |
vyaktaṃ vacaste tadatīva cograṃ proktaṃ hi tattvaṃ tvaritaṃ prayāhi |
kuruṣva yuddhaṃ hi mayā prasahya yadi praśakto'si balena hi tvam ||
2.5.d:
शिव उवाच ।
व्यक्तं वचस्ते तदतीव चोग्रं प्रोक्तं हि तत्त्वं त्वरितं प्रयाहि ।
कुरुष्व युद्धं हि मया प्रसह्य यदि प्रशक्तोऽसि बलेन हि त्वम् ॥
2.5.m: Śiva said: / "Your word is clear, exceedingly harsh; truth indeed has been spoken; depart quickly! / Wage war by force with me, if indeed you are capable with your might!

2.5.s:
yaḥ syādaśakto bhuvi tasya ko'rtho dārairdhanairvā sumanoharaiśca |
āyāntu daityāśca balena mattā vicāryamevaṃ tu kṛtaṃ mayaitat ||
2.5.d:
यः स्यादशक्तो भुवि तस्य कोऽर्थो दारैर्धनैर्वा सुमनोहरैश्च ।
आयान्तु दैत्याश्च बलेन मत्ता विचार्यमेवं तु कृतं मयैतत् ॥
2.5.m: If one is powerless on earth, what use has he for wives or exquisite wealth? / Let the Daityas, intoxicated with power, come; this has been decided by me.

2.5.s:
śarīrayātrāpi kutastvaśakteḥ kurvantu yadyadvihitaṃ tu teṣām |
mamāpi yadyatkaraṇīyamasti tattatkariṣyāmi na saṃśayo'tra ||
2.5.d:
शरीरयात्रापि कुतस्त्वशक्तेः कुर्वन्तु यद्यद्विहितं तु तेषाम् ।
ममापि यद्यत्करणीयमस्ति तत्तत्करिष्यामि न संशयोऽत्र ॥
2.5.m: From where can even bodily maintenance come for the powerless? Let them do whatever is prescribed for them! / Whatever is to be done by me, that I shall do; there is no doubt about this."

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
etadvacastadvidhaso'pi tasmā-cchrutvā harānnirgata eva hṛṣṭaḥ |
prāgāttato garjitahuṅkṛtāni kurvaṃstato daityapateḥ sakāśam ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ pañcamo yuddhakhaṇḍe
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
एतद्वचस्तद्विधसोऽपि तस्मा-च्छ्रुत्वा हरान्निर्गत एव हृष्टः ।
प्रागात्ततो गर्जितहुङ्कृतानि कुर्वंस्ततो दैत्यपतेः सकाशम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां पञ्चमो युद्धखण्डे
2.5.m:
Sanatkumāra said: / Hearing that speech of his from Hara, that Vidhasa went forth delighted, / and went roaring and shouting fiercely into the presence of the Daitya lord.

Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter, titled "Description of the Beginning of the Battle and the Messenger's Discourse," in the fifth section, the Yuddhakhaṇḍa, of the second Rudrasaṃhitā in the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
tasyeṅgitajñaśca sa daityarājo gadāṃ gṛhītvā tvaritaḥ sasainyaḥ |
kṛtvātha sā'gre gilanāmadheyaṃ sudāruṇaṃ devavarairabhedyam ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
तस्येङ्गितज्ञश्च स दैत्यराजो गदां गृहीत्वा त्वरितः ससैन्यः ।
कृत्वाथ साऽग्रे गिलनामधेयं सुदारुणं देववरैरभेद्यम् ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Understanding his intention, the king of the Daityas quickly took his club together with his army, / having placed in front the dreadful [array] named Gilana, impenetrable to the best of gods.

2.5.s:
guhāmukhaṃ prāpya maheśvarasya bibheda śastrairaśaniprakāśaiḥ |
anye tato vīrakameva śastrai-ravākiran śailasutāṃ tathānye ||
2.5.d:
गुहामुखं प्राप्य महेश्वरस्य बिभेद शस्त्रैरशनिप्रकाशैः ।
अन्ये ततो वीरकमेव शस्त्रै-रवाकिरन् शैलसुतां तथान्ये ॥
2.5.m: Reaching the mouth of Maheśvara's cave, he pierced it with weapons flashing like thunderbolts; / then others showered Vīraka with weapons, and others the daughter of the mountain.

2.5.s:
dvāraṃ hi kecidruciraṃ babhañjuḥ puṣpāṇi patrāṇi vināśayeyuḥ |
phalāni mūlāni jalaṃ ca hṛdya-mudyānamārgānapi khaṇḍayeyuḥ ||
2.5.d:
द्वारं हि केचिद्रुचिरं बभञ्जुः पुष्पाणि पत्राणि विनाशयेयुः ।
फलानि मूलानि जलं च हृद्य-मुद्यानमार्गानपि खण्डयेयुः ॥
2.5.m: Some indeed smashed the charming entrance, destroyed the flowers and leaves, / the fruits, roots, and pleasant water, and tore up the pathways of the garden.

2.5.s:
viloḍayeyurmuditāśca keci-cchṛṅgāṇi śailasya ca bhānumanti |
tato haraḥ sasmṛtavān svasainyaṃ samāhvayan kupitaḥ śūlapāṇiḥ ||
2.5.d:
विलोडयेयुर्मुदिताश्च केचि-च्छृङ्गाणि शैलस्य च भानुमन्ति ।
ततो हरः सस्मृतवान् स्वसैन्यं समाह्वयन् कुपितः शूलपाणिः ॥
2.5.m: Delighted, some broke down the radiant peaks of the mountain. / Then Hara remembered his own army and, angry, the trident-handed [Lord] called out.

2.5.s:
bhūtāni cānyāni sudāruṇāni devānsasainyānsaha viṣṇumukhyān |
āhūtamātrānugaṇāḥsasainyā rathairgajairvājivṛṣaiśca gobhiḥ ||
2.5.d:
भूतानि चान्यानि सुदारुणानि देवान्ससैन्यान्सह विष्णुमुख्यान् ।
आहूतमात्रानुगणाःससैन्या रथैर्गजैर्वाजिवृषैश्च गोभिः ॥
2.5.m: The dreadful Bhūtas and the others, the gods with their armies led by Viṣṇu, / as soon as they were summoned, the retinues with their armies came with chariots, elephants, horses, bulls, and cattle,

2.5.s:
uṣṭraiḥ kharaiḥ pakṣivaraiśca siṃhaiḥ te sarvadevāḥ sahabhūtasaṅghaiḥ |
vyāghrairmṛgaiḥ sūkarasārasaiśca samīnamatsyaiḥ śiśumāramukhyaiḥ ||
2.5.d:
उष्ट्रैः खरैः पक्षिवरैश्च सिंहैः ते सर्वदेवाः सहभूतसङ्घैः ।
व्याघ्रैर्मृगैः सूकरसारसैश्च समीनमत्स्यैः शिशुमारमुख्यैः ॥
2.5.m: with camels, donkeys, noble birds, and lions, all those gods along with hosts of Bhūtas, / with tigers, deer, boars, cranes, various fish, and dolphins at their head,

2.5.s:
anyaiśca nānā vidhajīvasaṅghai-rviśīrṇadaṃśaiḥ sphuṭitaiḥ śmaśānaiḥ |
bhujaṅgamaiḥ pretaśataiḥ piśācai-rdivyairvimānaiḥ kamalākaraiśca ||
2.5.d:
अन्यैश्च नाना विधजीवसङ्घै-र्विशीर्णदंशैः स्फुटितैः श्मशानैः ।
भुजङ्गमैः प्रेतशतैः पिशाचै-र्दिव्यैर्विमानैः कमलाकरैश्च ॥
2.5.m: and with other hosts of various living beings, with ragged bites, from burst cremation grounds, / with serpents, hundreds of Pretas, Piśācas, divine aerial chariots, lotus pools,

2.5.s:
nadīnadaiḥ parvatavāhanaiśca samāgatāḥ prāñjalayaḥ praṇamya |
kapardinaṃ tasthuradīnasattvāḥ senāpatiṃ vīrakameva kṛtvā ||
2.5.d:
नदीनदैः पर्वतवाहनैश्च समागताः प्राञ्जलयः प्रणम्य ।
कपर्दिनं तस्थुरदीनसत्त्वाः सेनापतिं वीरकमेव कृत्वा ॥
2.5.m: rivers, streams, and mountain vehicles; having arrived, bowing with joined palms, / of indomitable courage, they stood before the Kapardin, having made Vīraka their general.

2.5.s:
visarjayāmāsa raṇāya devān viśrāntavāhānatha tatpinākī |
yuddhe sthiraṃ labdhajayaṃ pradhānaṃ sampreṣitāste tu maheśvareṇa ||
2.5.d:
विसर्जयामास रणाय देवान् विश्रान्तवाहानथ तत्पिनाकी ।
युद्धे स्थिरं लब्धजयं प्रधानं सम्प्रेषितास्ते तु महेश्वरेण ॥
2.5.m: Then the wielder of the Pināka sent forth the gods, whose mounts were rested, to the battle; / steadfast in battle, victorious, excellent, they were dispatched by Maheśvara.

2.5.s:
cakruryugāntapratimaṃ ca yuddhaṃ maryādahīnaṃ sagilena sarve |
daityendrasainyena sadaiva ghoraṃ krodhānnigīrṇāstridaśāstu saṅkhye ||
2.5.d:
चक्रुर्युगान्तप्रतिमं च युद्धं मर्यादहीनं सगिलेन सर्वे ।
दैत्येन्द्रसैन्येन सदैव घोरं क्रोधान्निगीर्णास्त्रिदशास्तु सङ्ख्ये ॥
2.5.m: Together with Gilana, all of them fought a battle resembling the end of the cosmic age, devoid of bounds, / ever dreadful against the army of the lord of Daityas; but the gods were swallowed up in fury in the fight.

2.5.s:
tasminkṣaṇe yudhyamānāśca sarve brahmendraviṣṇvarkaśaśāṅkamukhyāḥ |
āsannigīrṇā vidhasena tena sainye nigīrṇe'sti tu vīrako hi ||
2.5.d:
तस्मिन्क्षणे युध्यमानाश्च सर्वे ब्रह्मेन्द्रविष्ण्वर्कशशाङ्कमुख्याः ।
आसन्निगीर्णा विधसेन तेन सैन्ये निगीर्णेऽस्ति तु वीरको हि ॥
2.5.m: At that moment, all those fighting—headed by Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu, the Sun, and the Moon— / were swallowed up by that Vidhasa; yet when the army was swallowed, Vīraka remained.

2.5.s:
vihāya saṅgrāmaśiroguhāṃ tāṃ praviśya śarvaṃ praṇipatya mūrdhnā |
provāca duḥkhābhihataḥ smarāriṃ suvīrako vāgmivaro'tha vṛttam ||
2.5.d:
विहाय सङ्ग्रामशिरोगुहां तां प्रविश्य शर्वं प्रणिपत्य मूर्ध्ना ।
प्रोवाच दुःखाभिहतः स्मरारिं सुवीरको वाग्मिवरोऽथ वृत्तम् ॥
2.5.m: Leaving the forefront of the battle and entering that cave, bowing his head to Śarva, / the noble Vīraka, best of eloquent speakers, stricken with grief, reported the event to the enemy of Smara:

2.5.s:
nigīrṇaṃ te sainyaṃ vighasaditijenādya bhagava-nnigīrṇo'sau viṣṇustribhuvanagururdaityadalanaḥ |
nigīrṇau candrārkau druhiṇamaghavānau ca varadau nigīrṇāste sarve yamavaruṇavātāśca dhanadaḥ ||
2.5.d:
निगीर्णं ते सैन्यं विघसदितिजेनाद्य भगव-न्निगीर्णोऽसौ विष्णुस्त्रिभुवनगुरुर्दैत्यदलनः ।
निगीर्णौ चन्द्रार्कौ द्रुहिणमघवानौ च वरदौ निगीर्णास्ते सर्वे यमवरुणवाताश्च धनदः ॥
2.5.m: "Your army has been swallowed today by the Daitya Vidhasa, O Lord! / Viṣṇu, the teacher of the three worlds and crusher of Daityas, has been swallowed! / Swallowed are the Moon and Sun, Druhiṇa and Maghavan, granters of boons; / swallowed are all of them: Yama, Varuṇa, Vāyu, and Dhanada!

2.5.s: sthito'smyekaḥ prahvaḥ kimiha karaṇīyaṃ bhavatu me ajeyo daityendraḥ pramuditamanā daityasahitaḥ ||
2.5.d: स्थितोऽस्म्येकः प्रह्वः किमिह करणीयं भवतु मे अजेयो दैत्येन्द्रः प्रमुदितमना दैत्यसहितः ॥
2.5.m: I stand alone, bowed low; what should I do here? / The lord of Daityas is unconquerable, joyful in mind along with the Daityas.

2.5.s:
ajeyaṃ tvāṃ prāptaḥ pratibhayamanā mārutagatiḥ svayaṃ viṣṇurdevaḥ kanakakaśipuṃ kaśyapasutam |
nakhaistīkṣṇairbhaktyā tadapi bhagavān śiṣṭavaśagaḥ pravṛttastrailokyaṃ vidhamatu malaṃ vyāttavadanaḥ ||
2.5.d:
अजेयं त्वां प्राप्तः प्रतिभयमना मारुतगतिः स्वयं विष्णुर्देवः कनककशिपुं कश्यपसुतम् ।
नखैस्तीक्ष्णैर्भक्त्या तदपि भगवान् शिष्टवशगः प्रवृत्तस्त्रैलोक्यं विधमतु मलं व्यात्तवदनः ॥
2.5.m: Frightened in mind, swift as the wind, I have approached you who are unconquerable. / The Lord God Viṣṇu himself [tore] the son of Kaśyapa, Hiraṇyakaśipu, / with sharp claws out of devotion; yet the Lord, obedient to his devotees, / is active; let him with gaping mouth completely blast the three worlds!

2.5.s: vasiṣṭhādyaiḥ śapto bhuvanapatibhiḥ saptamunibhiḥ tathābhūte bhūyastvamiti suciraṃ daityasahitaḥ ||
2.5.d: वसिष्ठाद्यैः शप्तो भुवनपतिभिः सप्तमुनिभिः तथाभूते भूयस्त्वमिति सुचिरं दैत्यसहितः ॥
2.5.m: Cursed by Vasiṣṭha and the other seven sages, the lords of the world, / you have been thus for a very long time, along with the Daityas!"

2.5.s:
tatastenoktāste praṇayavacanairātmani hitaiḥ kadāsmādvai ghorādbhavati mama mokṣo munivarāḥ |
yataḥ kruddhairukto vighasaharaṇādyuddhasamaye tato ghorairbāṇairvidalitamukhe muṣṭibhiralam ||
2.5.d:
ततस्तेनोक्तास्ते प्रणयवचनैरात्मनि हितैः कदास्माद्वै घोराद्भवति मम मोक्षो मुनिवराः ।
यतः क्रुद्धैरुक्तो विघसहरणाद्युद्धसमये ततो घोरैर्बाणैर्विदलितमुखे मुष्टिभिरलम् ॥
2.5.m: Then they were spoken to by him with affectionate words beneficial to himself: / 'When indeed, O best of sages, will my release from this dreadful [state] take place?' / Wherefore he was told by the angered [sages]: 'From the swallowing of Vighasa at the time of battle, / and from having your mouth shattered with terrible arrows and thoroughly with fists,

2.5.s:
badaryākhyāraṇye nanu harigṛhe puṇyavasatau nisaṃstabhyātmānaṃ vigatakaluṣo yāsyasi param |
tatasteṣāṃ vākyātpratidinamasau daityagilanaḥ kṣudhārtaḥ saṅgrāmād bhramati punarāmodamuditaḥ ||
2.5.d:
बदर्याख्यारण्ये ननु हरिगृहे पुण्यवसतौ निसंस्तभ्यात्मानं विगतकलुषो यास्यसि परम् ।
ततस्तेषां वाक्यात्प्रतिदिनमसौ दैत्यगिलनः क्षुधार्तः सङ्ग्रामाद् भ्रमति पुनरामोदमुदितः ॥
2.5.m: firmly steadying yourself in the forest named Badarī, Hari’s abode, an auspicious dwelling, / you shall go to the supreme [state], freed of defilement.' / Then, by their word, that swallower of Daityas wanders daily / afflicted with hunger away from the battlefield, again joyful with delight.

2.5.s:
tamaścedaṃ ghoraṃ jagaduditayoḥ sūryaśaśino-ryathāśukrastubhyaṃ paramaripuratyantavikaraḥ |
hatāndevairdaityānpunaramṛtavidyāstutipadaiḥ savīryānsanhṛṣṭānvraṇaśataviyuktānprakurute ||
2.5.d:
तमश्चेदं घोरं जगदुदितयोः सूर्यशशिनो-र्यथाशुक्रस्तुभ्यं परमरिपुरत्यन्तविकरः ।
हतान्देवैर्दैत्यान्पुनरमृतविद्यास्तुतिपदैः सवीर्यान्सन्हृष्टान्व्रणशतवियुक्तान्प्रकुरुते ॥
2.5.m: And [he said]: 'This terrible darkness has arisen upon the world, [obscuring] the sun and moon, / while Śukra, your supreme enemy, is causing immense destruction. / By the verses of praise of the nectar-lore (sañjīvinīvidyā), he again restores the Daityas slain by the gods, / making them vigorous, delighted, and free of their hundreds of wounds.

2.5.s: varaṃ prāṇāstyājyāstava mama tu saṅgrāmasamaye bhavānsākṣībhūtaḥ kṣaṇamapi vṛtaḥ kāryakaraṇe ||
2.5.d: वरं प्राणास्त्याज्यास्तव मम तु सङ्ग्रामसमये भवान्साक्षीभूतः क्षणमपि वृतः कार्यकरणे ॥
2.5.m: Better that life be abandoned at the time of your battle and mine; / you, being a witness, have been chosen even for a moment for the performance of the task.'

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
itīdaṃ satputrātpramathapatirākarṇya kupita-ściraṃ dhyātvā cakre tribhuvanapatiḥ prāganupamam |
pragāyatsāmākhyaṃ dinakarakarākāravapuṣā prahāsāttannāmnā tadanu nihataṃ tena ca tamaḥ ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
इतीदं सत्पुत्रात्प्रमथपतिराकर्ण्य कुपित-श्चिरं ध्यात्वा चक्रे त्रिभुवनपतिः प्रागनुपमम् ।
प्रगायत्सामाख्यं दिनकरकराकारवपुषा प्रहासात्तन्नाम्ना तदनु निहतं तेन च तमः ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Hearing this from his noble son, the angered lord of the Pramathas, the lord of the three worlds, / meditated for a long time and first produced an incomparable [hymn] / singing the Sāman, in a form shaped like the sun’s rays; / and by his laughter, by its utterance, the darkness was thereupon destroyed by him.

2.5.s:
prakāśe'smim̐lloke punarapi mahāyuddhamakarod raṇe daityaiḥ sārddhaṃ vikṛtavadanairvīrakamuniḥ |
śilācūrṇaṃ bhuktvā pravaramuninā yastu janitaḥ sa kṛtvā saṇgrāmaṃ puramapi purā yaśca jitavān ||
2.5.d:
प्रकाशेऽस्मिम्̐ल्लोके पुनरपि महायुद्धमकरोद् रणे दैत्यैः सार्द्धं विकृतवदनैर्वीरकमुनिः ।
शिलाचूर्णं भुक्त्वा प्रवरमुनिना यस्तु जनितः स कृत्वा सण्ग्रामं पुरमपि पुरा यश्च जितवान् ॥
2.5.m: When this world was illuminated, sage Vīraka once more waged great war / in battle alongside the Daityas of disfigured faces; / he who was begotten by the excellent sage after eating powdered stone, / and who, having waged war, had formerly conquered even the city.

2.5.s:
mahārudraḥ sadyaḥ sa khalu ditijenātigilitaḥ tataścāsau nandī niśitaśaraśūlāsisahitaḥ |
pradhāno yodhānāṃ munivaraśatānāmapi mahān nivāso vidyānāṃ śamadamamahādhairyasahitaḥ ||
2.5.d:
महारुद्रः सद्यः स खलु दितिजेनातिगिलितः ततश्चासौ नन्दी निशितशरशूलासिसहितः ।
प्रधानो योधानां मुनिवरशतानामपि महान् निवासो विद्यानां शमदममहाधैर्यसहितः ॥
2.5.m: Indeed, that great Rudra was swallowed on the spot by the son of Diti; / and then Nandin, equipped with sharp arrows, trident, and sword, / foremost among warriors, great even among hundreds of excellent sages, / the abode of sciences, endowed with tranquility, self-control, and great fortitude—

2.5.s:
nirīkṣyaivaṃ paścād vṛṣabhavaramāruhya bhagavān kapardī yuddhārthī vighasaditijaṃ sammukhamukhaḥ |
japandivyaṃ mantraṃ nigalanavidhānodgilanakaṃ sthitaḥ sajjaṃ kṛtvā dhanuraśanikalpānapi śarān ||
2.5.d:
निरीक्ष्यैवं पश्चाद् वृषभवरमारुह्य भगवान् कपर्दी युद्धार्थी विघसदितिजं सम्मुखमुखः ।
जपन्दिव्यं मन्त्रं निगलनविधानोद्गिलनकं स्थितः सज्जं कृत्वा धनुरशनिकल्पानपि शरान् ॥
2.5.m: seeing this, the venerable Kapardin, desiring battle, / mounted his excellent bull and faced the Daitya Vighasa head-on; / chanting a divine mantra that effects swallowing and disgorging, / he stood with bow strung and arrows like thunderbolts.

2.5.s:
tatau niṣkānto'sau vighasavadanādvīrakamuni-rgṛhītvā tatsarve svabalamatulaṃ viṣṇusahitāḥ |
samudgīrṇāḥ sarve kamalajabalārīndudinapāḥ prahṛṣṭaṃ tatsainyaṃ punarapi mahāyuddhamakarot ||
2.5.d:
ततौ निष्कान्तोऽसौ विघसवदनाद्वीरकमुनि-र्गृहीत्वा तत्सर्वे स्वबलमतुलं विष्णुसहिताः ।
समुद्गीर्णाः सर्वे कमलजबलारीन्दुदिनपाः प्रहृष्टं तत्सैन्यं पुनरपि महायुद्धमकरोत् ॥
2.5.m: Then sage Vīraka came out of Vighasa’s mouth; / they, along with Viṣṇu, all seized their own incomparable army; / and the lotus-born [Brahmā], Balāri [Indra], the moon, and the sun were all vomited forth. / That delighted army again waged a great battle.

2.5.s:
jite tasmin śukrastadanu ditijānyuddhavihatān yadā vidyāvīryātpunarapi sajīvānprakurute |
tadā baddhvā''nītaḥ paśuriva gaṇairbhūtapataye nigīrṇastenāsau tripuraripuṇā dānavaguruḥ ||
2.5.d:
जिते तस्मिन् शुक्रस्तदनु दितिजान्युद्धविहतान् यदा विद्यावीर्यात्पुनरपि सजीवान्प्रकुरुते ।
तदा बद्ध्वा'ऽनीतः पशुरिव गणैर्भूतपतये निगीर्णस्तेनासौ त्रिपुररिपुणा दानवगुरुः ॥
2.5.m: When he was defeated, Śukra then restored to life / through the power of his lore the sons of Diti slain in the battle; / then, bound like a sacrificial animal by the attendants, he was brought to the lord of ghosts; / that preceptor of the Dānavas was swallowed by him, the enemy of Tripura.

2.5.s:
vinaṣṭe śukrākhye suraripunivāsastadakhilo jito dhvasto bhagno bhṛśamapi suraiścāpi dalitam |
prabhūtairbhūtaughairditijakuṇapagrāsarasikaiḥ saruṇḍairnṛtyadbhirniśitaśaraśaktyuddhṛtakaraiḥ ||
2.5.d:
विनष्टे शुक्राख्ये सुररिपुनिवासस्तदखिलो जितो ध्वस्तो भग्नो भृशमपि सुरैश्चापि दलितम् ।
प्रभूतैर्भूतौघैर्दितिजकुणपग्रासरसिकैः सरुण्डैर्नृत्यद्भिर्निशितशरशक्त्युद्धृतकरैः ॥
2.5.m: When the one named Śukra was destroyed, that entire dwelling of the gods' enemies / was conquered, devastated, broken, and also utterly shattered by the gods, / and by numerous hosts of ghosts relishers of devouring the corpses of Diti's sons, / dancing with headless trunks, their hands raised with sharp arrows and spears,

2.5.s:
pramattairvetālaiḥsudṛḍhakaratuṇḍairapi khagai-vṛkairnānābhedaiḥ śavakuṇapapūrṇāsyakavalaiḥ |
vikīrṇe saṅgrāme kanakakaśiporvaṃśajanaka ściraṃ yuddhaṃ kṛtvā hariharamahendraiśca vijitaḥ ||
2.5.d:
प्रमत्तैर्वेतालैःसुदृढकरतुण्डैरपि खगै-वृकैर्नानाभेदैः शवकुणपपूर्णास्यकवलैः ।
विकीर्णे सङ्ग्रामे कनककशिपोर्वंशजनक श्चिरं युद्धं कृत्वा हरिहरमहेन्द्रैश्च विजितः ॥
2.5.m: by intoxicated Vetālas, and by birds with very firm claws and beaks, / and by various kinds of wolves with mouths filled with morsels of dead bodies and corpses. / In that scattered battle, the progenitor of Hiraṇyakaśipu’s lineage, / after fighting for a long time, was conquered by Hari, Hara, and Mahendra.

2.5.s:
praviṣṭe pātāle girijaladhirandhrāṇyapi tathā tataḥ sainye kṣīṇe ditijavṛṣabhaścāndhakavaraḥ |
prakope devānāṃ kadanadavaro viśvadalano gadāghātairghorairvidalitamadaścāpi hariṇā ||
2.5.d:
प्रविष्टे पाताले गिरिजलधिरन्ध्राण्यपि तथा ततः सैन्ये क्षीणे दितिजवृषभश्चान्धकवरः ।
प्रकोपे देवानां कदनदवरो विश्वदलनो गदाघातैर्घोरैर्विदलितमदश्चापि हरिणा ॥
2.5.m: When [the Daityas] had entered the netherworld as well as the fissures of mountains and oceans, / and their army was thus diminished, the best of Diti’s sons, the excellent Andhaka, / a wild forest fire of destruction in the rage of the gods, the crusher of the universe, / had his arrogance crushed by Hari with dreadful blows of the mace.

2.5.s:
na vai yaḥ sagrāmaṃ tyajati varalabdhaḥ kila yataḥ tadā tāḍairghoraistridaśapatinā pīḍitatanuḥ |
tataḥ śastrāstraughaistarugirijalaiścāśu vibudhān jigāyoccairgarjanpramathapatimāhūya śanakaiḥ ||
2.5.d:
न वै यः सग्रामं त्यजति वरलब्धः किल यतः तदा ताडैर्घोरैस्त्रिदशपतिना पीडिततनुः ।
ततः शस्त्रास्त्रौघैस्तरुगिरिजलैश्चाशु विबुधान् जिगायोच्चैर्गर्जन्प्रमथपतिमाहूय शनकैः ॥
2.5.m: Indeed, having obtained a boon, he did not abandon the battle at all; / though his body was tormented by the lord of the gods with terrible blows, / roaring loudly, having challenged the lord of the Pramathas softly, / he swiftly overcame the gods with floods of weapons and missiles, trees, rocks, and water.

2.5.s:
sthito yuddhaṃ kurvan raṇapatitaśastrairbahuvidhaiḥ parikṣīṇaiḥ sarvaistadanu girijārudramatudat |
tathā vṛkṣaiḥ sarpairaśaninivahaiḥ śastrapaṭalai-rvirūpairmāyābhiḥ kapaṭaracanāśambaraśataiḥ ||
2.5.d:
स्थितो युद्धं कुर्वन् रणपतितशस्त्रैर्बहुविधैः परिक्षीणैः सर्वैस्तदनु गिरिजारुद्रमतुदत् ।
तथा वृक्षैः सर्पैरशनिनिवहैः शस्त्रपटलै-र्विरूपैर्मायाभिः कपटरचनाशम्बरशतैः ॥
2.5.m: Standing and fighting with the many kinds of weapons fallen on the battlefield / when all his own were exhausted, he then struck Girijā and Rudra / with trees, serpents, masses of thunderbolts, arrays of weapons, / and hundreds of vile illusions and deceptive devices of Śambara.

2.5.s:
vijetuṃ śaileśaṃ kuhakamaparaṃ tatra kṛtavān mahāsattvo vīrastripurariputulyaśca matimān |
na vadhyo devānāṃ varaśatamanonmādavivaśaḥ prabhūtaiḥ śastrāstraiḥ sapadi ditijo jarjaratanuḥ ||
2.5.d:
विजेतुं शैलेशं कुहकमपरं तत्र कृतवान् महासत्त्वो वीरस्त्रिपुररिपुतुल्यश्च मतिमान् ।
न वध्यो देवानां वरशतमनोन्मादविवशः प्रभूतैः शस्त्रास्त्रैः सपदि दितिजो जर्जरतनुः ॥
2.5.m: To conquer the lord of the mountain, that great-spirited, heroic, and wise [demon], / equal to the enemy of Tripura, employed another trick there; / being incapable of being killed by the gods, helpless through the arrogance born of a hundred boons, / the son of Diti quickly had his body lacerated by abundant weapons and missiles.

2.5.s:
tadīyādviṣyandātkṣititalagatairandhakagaṇai-rativyāptaṃ ghoraṃ vikṛtavadanaṃ svātmasadṛśam |
dadhatkalpāntāgnipratimavapuṣā bhūtapatinā triśūle nodbhinnastripuraripuṇā dāruṇataram ||
2.5.d:
तदीयाद्विष्यन्दात्क्षितितलगतैरन्धकगणै-रतिव्याप्तं घोरं विकृतवदनं स्वात्मसदृशम् ।
दधत्कल्पान्ताग्निप्रतिमवपुषा भूतपतिना त्रिशूले नोद्भिन्नस्त्रिपुररिपुणा दारुणतरम् ॥
2.5.m: From his trickling blood, the dreadful [earth] became excessively covered / with hosts of Andhakas of disfigured faces resembling himself, who had reached the surface of the earth; / assuming a body resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution, / the enemy of Tripura, the lord of ghosts, pierced him most dreadfully with his trident.

2.5.s:
yadā sainyātsainyaṃ paśupatihatādanyadabhavad-vraṇotthairatyuṣṇaiḥ piśitanisṛtairbindubhiralam |
tadā viṣṇuryogātpramathapatimāhūya matimān cakārograṃ rūpaṃ vikṛtavadanaṃ straiṇamajitam ||
2.5.d:
यदा सैन्यात्सैन्यं पशुपतिहतादन्यदभवद्-व्रणोत्थैरत्युष्णैः पिशितनिसृतैर्बिन्दुभिरलम् ।
तदा विष्णुर्योगात्प्रमथपतिमाहूय मतिमान् चकारोग्रं रूपं विकृतवदनं स्त्रैणमजितम् ॥
2.5.m: When from that army another army arose from the blood / shed from the flesh, intensely hot, falling in drops from the wounds of those slain by Paśupati, / then wise Viṣṇu, invoking the lord of the Pramathas by yoga, / created a fierce, unconquered feminine form with a disfigured face.

2.5.s: karālaṃ saṃśuṣkaṃ bahubhujalatākrāntakupito viniṣkrāntaḥ karṇādgaṇaśirasi śambhośca bhagavān ||
2.5.d: करालं संशुष्कं बहुभुजलताक्रान्तकुपितो विनिष्क्रान्तः कर्णाद्गणशिरसि शम्भोश्च भगवान् ॥
2.5.m: Terrifying, withered, angered, overcome with many creeper-like arms, / that divine [goddess] came forth from the ear upon the head of the attendant of Śambhu.

2.5.s:
raṇasthā sā devī caraṇayugalālaṅkṛtamahī stutā devaiḥ sarvaiḥ tadanu bhagavān preritamatiḥ |
kṣudhārtā tatsainyaṃ ditijanisṛtaṃ tacca rudhiraṃ papau sātyuṣṇaṃ tadraṇaśirasi sṛkkardamamalam ||
2.5.d:
रणस्था सा देवी चरणयुगलालङ्कृतमही स्तुता देवैः सर्वैः तदनु भगवान् प्रेरितमतिः ।
क्षुधार्ता तत्सैन्यं दितिजनिसृतं तच्च रुधिरं पपौ सात्युष्णं तद्रणशिरसि सृक्कर्दममलम् ॥
2.5.m: Standing in the battle, that goddess whose two feet adorned the earth / was praised by all the gods; thereupon the Lord impelled her mind; / afflicted with hunger, she completely drank the army of Diti’s sons, / and that very hot blood flowing from them into the mud on the corners of her mouth at the forefront of battle.

2.5.s:
tatastveko daityastadapi yuyudhe śuṣkarudhiraḥ talāghātairghorairaśanisadṛśairjānucaraṇaiḥ |
nakhairvajrākārairmukhabhujaśirobhiśca giriśaṃ smaran kṣātraṃ dharmaṃ svakulavihitaṃ śāśvatamajam ||
2.5.d:
ततस्त्वेको दैत्यस्तदपि युयुधे शुष्करुधिरः तलाघातैर्घोरैरशनिसदृशैर्जानुचरणैः ।
नखैर्वज्राकारैर्मुखभुजशिरोभिश्च गिरिशं स्मरन् क्षात्रं धर्मं स्वकुलविहितं शाश्वतमजम् ॥
2.5.m: Then one Daitya nevertheless fought on, his blood dried up, / with terrible blows of the palms resembling thunderbolts, with knees and feet, / with claws like vajras, with his mouth, arms, and head against Giriśa, / remembering the eternal, birthless duty of the warrior class ordained for his lineage.

2.5.s:
raṇe śāntaḥ paścātpramathapatinā bhinnahṛdaya-striśūle samproto nabhasi vidhṛtaḥ sthāṇusadṛśaḥ |
adhaḥkāyaḥ śuṣkastapanakiraṇairjīrṇatanumān jalāsārairmeghaiḥ pavanasahitaiḥ kleditavapuḥ ||
2.5.d:
रणे शान्तः पश्चात्प्रमथपतिना भिन्नहृदय-स्त्रिशूले सम्प्रोतो नभसि विधृतः स्थाणुसदृशः ।
अधःकायः शुष्कस्तपनकिरणैर्जीर्णतनुमान् जलासारैर्मेघैः पवनसहितैः क्लेदितवपुः ॥
2.5.m: At last exhausted in battle, with his heart pierced by the lord of the Pramathas, / he was transfixed on the trident and held in the sky, resembling a post (sthāṇu); / his lower body dried up, his worn body scorched by the rays of the sun, / his form drenched by clouds with torrents of water accompanied by the wind,

2.5.s:
viśīrṇastigmāṃśostuhinaśakalākāraśakala-stathābhūtaḥ prāṇāṃstadapi na jahau daityavṛṣabhaḥ |
tadā tuṣṭaḥ śambhuḥ paramakaruṇāvāridhirasau dadau tasmai prītyā gaṇapatipadaṃ tena vinutaḥ ||
2.5.d:
विशीर्णस्तिग्मांशोस्तुहिनशकलाकारशकल-स्तथाभूतः प्राणांस्तदपि न जहौ दैत्यवृषभः ।
तदा तुष्टः शम्भुः परमकरुणावारिधिरसौ ददौ तस्मै प्रीत्या गणपतिपदं तेन विनुतः ॥
2.5.m: shattered by the sun and broken into fragments resembling chunks of snow— / even though reduced to such a state, the bull among Daityas did not give up his life-breaths. / Then Śambhu, that ocean of supreme compassion, pleased and praised by him, / affectionately bestowed upon him the rank of lord of the attendants.

2.5.s:
tato yuddhasyānte bhuvanapatayaḥ sārtha ramaṇai-stavairnānābhedaiḥ pramathapatimabhyarcya vidhivat |
haribrahmādyāste paramanutibhiḥ tuṣṭuvuralaṃ nataskandhāḥ prītā jaya jaya giraṃ procya sukhitāḥ ||
2.5.d:
ततो युद्धस्यान्ते भुवनपतयः सार्थ रमणै-स्तवैर्नानाभेदैः प्रमथपतिमभ्यर्च्य विधिवत् ।
हरिब्रह्माद्यास्ते परमनुतिभिः तुष्टुवुरलं नतस्कन्धाः प्रीता जय जय गिरं प्रोच्य सुखिताः ॥
2.5.m: Then, at the end of the battle, the lords of the worlds, / having worshipped the lord of the Pramathas according to rule with various kinds of meaningful and delightful hymns of praise, / those [gods] headed by Hari and Brahmā extolled him amply with supreme praises; / bowing their shoulders, delighted and happy, they proclaimed: 'Victory! Victory!'

2.5.s:
harastaistaiḥ sārdhaṃ girivaraguhāyāṃ pramudito visṛjyaikānaṃśān vividhabalinā pūjyasunagān |
cakārājñāṃ krīḍāṃ girivarasutāṃ prāpya muditāṃ tathā putraṃ ghorādvighasavadanānmuktamanagham ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ pañcamo yuddhakhaṇḍe
2.5.d:
हरस्तैस्तैः सार्धं गिरिवरगुहायां प्रमुदितो विसृज्यैकानंशान् विविधबलिना पूज्यसुनगान् ।
चकाराज्ञां क्रीडां गिरिवरसुतां प्राप्य मुदितां तथा पुत्रं घोराद्विघसवदनान्मुक्तमनघम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां पञ्चमो युद्धखण्डे
2.5.m:
Delighted along with them in the cave of the best of mountains, sending away his portions to the worshipful great mountains by means of various offerings, / Hara, having regained the daughter of the best of mountains made joyful, as well as his sinless son freed from the dreadful mouth of destruction, engaged in amorous play.

Thus ends the forty-sixth chapter, named “The Description of the Battle with Andhaka” in the account of the slaying of Andhaka, in the fifth section, the Yuddhakhaṇḍa, of the second book, the Rudrasaṃhitā, in the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.5.s:
vyāsa uvāca |
tasminmahati saṅgrāme dāruṇe lomaharṣaṇe |
śukro daityapatirvidvān bhakṣitastripurāriṇā ||
2.5.d:
व्यास उवाच ।
तस्मिन्महति सङ्ग्रामे दारुणे लोमहर्षणे ।
शुक्रो दैत्यपतिर्विद्वान् भक्षितस्त्रिपुरारिणा ॥
2.5.m: Vyāsa said: / In that great, fierce, hair-raising battle, / the learned Śukra, lord of the Daityas, was devoured by the enemy of Tripura.

2.5.s:
iti śrutaṃ samāsānme tatpunarbrūhi vistarāt |
kiṃ cakāra mahāyogī jaṭharasthaḥ pinākinaḥ ||
2.5.d:
इति श्रुतं समासान्मे तत्पुनर्ब्रूहि विस्तरात् ।
किं चकार महायोगी जठरस्थः पिनाकिनः ॥
2.5.m: This was heard by me in brief; tell it again in detail: / What did that great yogin do while remaining in the belly of the wielder of Pināka?

2.5.s:
na dadāha kathaṃ śambhoḥ śukraṃ taṃ jaṭharānalaḥ |
kalpāntadahanaḥ kālo dīptatejāśca bhārgavaḥ ||
2.5.d:
न ददाह कथं शम्भोः शुक्रं तं जठरानलः ।
कल्पान्तदहनः कालो दीप्ततेजाश्च भार्गवः ॥
2.5.m: Why did the fire in the belly of Śambhu—that Bhārgava of radiant splendor— / not burn Śukra, when it is the death-fire that consumes at the end of an aeon?

2.5.s:
viniṣkrāntaḥ kathaṃ dhīmān śambhorjaṭharapañjarāt |
kathamārādhayāmāsa kiyatkālaṃ sa bhārgavaḥ ||
2.5.d:
विनिष्क्रान्तः कथं धीमान् शम्भोर्जठरपञ्जरात् ।
कथमाराधयामास कियत्कालं स भार्गवः ॥
2.5.m: How did that wise one emerge from the cage of Śambhu's belly? / How did that Bhārgava propitiate [him], and for how long?

2.5.s:
kathaṃ ca labdhavānvidyāṃ tāṃ mṛtyuśamanīṃ parām |
kā sā vidyā parā tāta yayā mṛtyurhi vāryate ||
2.5.d:
कथं च लब्धवान्विद्यां तां मृत्युशमनीं पराम् ।
का सा विद्या परा तात यया मृत्युर्हि वार्यते ॥
2.5.m: And how did he obtain that supreme lore that subdues death? / Dear father, what is that supreme lore by which death is averted?

2.5.s:
lebhe'ndhako gāṇapatyaṃ kathaṃ śūlādvinirgataḥ |
devadevasya vai śambhormunerlīlāvihāriṇaḥ ||
2.5.d:
लेभेऽन्धको गाणपत्यं कथं शूलाद्विनिर्गतः ।
देवदेवस्य वै शम्भोर्मुनेर्लीलाविहारिणः ॥
2.5.m: How did Andhaka, having come out from the trident, obtain the status of a lord of attendants / of the god of gods, Śambhu, the sage who sports at play?

2.5.s:
etatsarvamaśeṣeṇa mahādhīman kṛpāṃ kuru |
śivalīlāmṛtaṃ tāta śṛṇvataḥ kathayasva me ||
2.5.d:
एतत्सर्वमशेषेण महाधीमन् कृपां कुरु ।
शिवलीलामृतं तात शृण्वतः कथयस्व मे ॥
2.5.m: O greatly wise one, have compassion in full regarding all this; / dear father, narrate the nectar of Śiva's sports to me who am listening.

2.5.s:
brahmovāca |
iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā vyāsasyāmitatejasaḥ |
sanatkumāraḥ provāca smṛtvā śivapadāmbujam ||
2.5.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा व्यासस्यामिततेजसः ।
सनत्कुमारः प्रोवाच स्मृत्वा शिवपदाम्बुजम् ॥
2.5.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard these words of Vyāsa of immeasurable splendor, / Sanatkumāra, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, spoke.

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
śṛṇu vyāsa mahābuddhe śivalīlāmṛtaṃ param |
dhanyastvaṃ śaivamukhyo'si mamānandakaraḥ svataḥ ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
शृणु व्यास महाबुद्धे शिवलीलामृतं परम् ।
धन्यस्त्वं शैवमुख्योऽसि ममानन्दकरः स्वतः ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Listen, O Vyāsa of great intellect, to the supreme nectar of Śiva's sports. / Blessed are you, the foremost of Śaivas, who naturally bring joy to me.

2.5.s:
pravartamāne samare śaṅkarāndhakayostayoḥ |
anirbhedyapavivyūhagirivyūhādhināthayoḥ ||
2.5.d:
प्रवर्तमाने समरे शङ्करान्धकयोस्तयोः ।
अनिर्भेद्यपविव्यूहगिरिव्यूहाधिनाथयोः ॥
2.5.m: While the battle was proceeding between Śaṅkara and Andhaka, / the two supreme commanders of the impenetrable thunderbolt array and mountain array,

2.5.s:
purā jayo babhūvāpi daityānāṃ balaśālinām |
śivaprabhāvādabhavatpramathānāṃ mune jayaḥ ||
2.5.d:
पुरा जयो बभूवापि दैत्यानां बलशालिनाम् ।
शिवप्रभावादभवत्प्रमथानां मुने जयः ॥
2.5.m: formerly victory indeed belonged to the powerful Daityas; / but through the power of Śiva, O sage, victory came to the Pramathas.

2.5.s:
tacchrutvāsīdviṣaṇṇo hi mahādaityo'ndhakāsuraḥ |
kathaṃ syānme jaya iti vicāraṇaparo'bhavat ||
2.5.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वासीद्विषण्णो हि महादैत्योऽन्धकासुरः ।
कथं स्यान्मे जय इति विचारणपरोऽभवत् ॥
2.5.m: Hearing that, the great Daitya, the asura Andhaka, became despondent indeed; / he became engrossed in pondering: “How can victory be mine?”

2.5.s:
apasṛtya tato yuddhādandhakaḥ parabuddhimān |
drutamabhyagamadvīra ekalaḥ śukrasannidhim ||
2.5.d:
अपसृत्य ततो युद्धादन्धकः परबुद्धिमान् ।
द्रुतमभ्यगमद्वीर एकलः शुक्रसन्निधिम् ॥
2.5.m: Then, withdrawing from the battle, the exceedingly intelligent Andhaka, / that hero, went quickly and alone into the presence of Śukra.

2.5.s:
praṇamya svaguruṃ kāvyamavaruhya rathācca saḥ |
babhāṣedaṃ vicāryātha sāñjalirnītivittamaḥ ||
2.5.d:
प्रणम्य स्वगुरुं काव्यमवरुह्य रथाच्च सः ।
बभाषेदं विचार्याथ साञ्जलिर्नीतिवित्तमः ॥
2.5.m: Bowing to his guru Kāvya after descending from his chariot, / that foremost knower of statecraft, having reflected, spoke this with folded hands:

2.5.s:
andhaka uvāca |
bhagavaṃstvāmupāśritya gurorbhāvaṃ vahāmahe |
parājitā bhavāmo no sarvadā jayaśālinaḥ ||
2.5.d:
अन्धक उवाच ।
भगवंस्त्वामुपाश्रित्य गुरोर्भावं वहामहे ।
पराजिता भवामो नो सर्वदा जयशालिनः ॥
2.5.m: Andhaka said: / O venerable one, relying on you, we bear the status of [your disciples under] a guru; / we are never defeated, but are always victorious.

2.5.s:
tvatprabhāvātsadā devānsamastānsānugānvayam |
manyāmahe haropendramukhānapi hi kattṛṇān ||
2.5.d:
त्वत्प्रभावात्सदा देवान्समस्तान्सानुगान्वयम् ।
मन्यामहे हरोपेन्द्रमुखानपि हि कत्तृणान् ॥
2.5.m: Through your power, we always regard all the gods along with their followers— / even those headed by Hari and Upendra—as mere blades of grass.

2.5.s:
asmatto bibhyati surāḥ tadā bhavadanugrahāt |
gajā iva haribhyaśca tārkṣyebhya iva pannagāḥ ||
2.5.d:
अस्मत्तो बिभ्यति सुराः तदा भवदनुग्रहात् ।
गजा इव हरिभ्यश्च तार्क्ष्येभ्य इव पन्नगाः ॥
2.5.m: Because of your grace, the gods are as afraid of us / as elephants are of lions, or serpents of eagles.

2.5.s:
anirbhedyaṃ pavivyūhaṃ viviśurdaityadānavāḥ |
pramathānīkamakhilaṃ vidhūya tvadanugrahāt ||
2.5.d:
अनिर्भेद्यं पविव्यूहं विविशुर्दैत्यदानवाः ।
प्रमथानीकमखिलं विधूय त्वदनुग्रहात् ॥
2.5.m: The Daityas and Dānavas entered the impenetrable thunderbolt array, / dispersing the entire host of Pramathas by your grace.

2.5.s:
vayaṃ tvaccharaṇā bhūtvā sadā gā iva niścalāḥ |
sthitvā carāmo niḥśaṅkamājāvapi hi bhārgava ||
2.5.d:
वयं त्वच्छरणा भूत्वा सदा गा इव निश्चलाः ।
स्थित्वा चरामो निःशङ्कमाजावपि हि भार्गव ॥
2.5.m: Taking refuge in you, standing always firm like the earth, / we move without fear even in battle, O Bhārgava.

2.5.s:
rakṣarakṣābhito vipra pravrajya śaraṇāgatān |
asurān śatrubhirvīrairarditāṃśca mṛtānapi ||
2.5.d:
रक्षरक्षाभितो विप्र प्रव्रज्य शरणागतान् ।
असुरान् शत्रुभिर्वीरैरर्दितांश्च मृतानपि ॥
2.5.m: Protect, protect completely, O brahmin, having approached those who have come for refuge— / the asuras who have been crushed by heroic enemies and even those who are dead!

2.5.s:
prathamairbhīmavikrāntaiḥ krāntānmṛtyupramāthibhiḥ |
sūditānpatitānpaśya huṇḍādīnmadgaṇānvarān ||
2.5.d:
प्रथमैर्भीमविक्रान्तैः क्रान्तान्मृत्युप्रमाथिभिः ।
सूदितान्पतितान्पश्य हुण्डादीन्मद्गणान्वरान् ॥
2.5.m: Look upon my excellent hosts, Huṇḍa and others, / overcome by the foremost [warriors] of terrible valor who crush death, slain and fallen.

2.5.s:
yaḥ pītvā kaṇadhūmaṃ vai sahasraṃ śaradāṃ purā |
tvayā prāptā varā vidyā tasyāḥ kālo'yamāgataḥ ||
2.5.d:
यः पीत्वा कणधूमं वै सहस्रं शरदां पुरा ।
त्वया प्राप्ता वरा विद्या तस्याः कालोऽयमागतः ॥
2.5.m: The excellent lore that was obtained by you long ago, having inhaled the smoke of chaff / for a thousand autumns—the time for it has now arrived.

2.5.s:
adya vidyāphalaṃ tatte sarve paśyantu bhārgava |
pramathā asurānsarvān kṛpayā jīvayiṣyataḥ ||
2.5.d:
अद्य विद्याफलं तत्ते सर्वे पश्यन्तु भार्गव ।
प्रमथा असुरान्सर्वान् कृपया जीवयिष्यतः ॥
2.5.m: Today, let all the Pramathas behold that fruit of your lore, O Bhārgava, / as you graciously revive all the asuras!

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
itthamandhakavākyaṃ sa śrutvā dhīro hi bhārgavaḥ |
tadā vicārayāmāsa dūyamānena cetasā ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
इत्थमन्धकवाक्यं स श्रुत्वा धीरो हि भार्गवः ।
तदा विचारयामास दूयमानेन चेतसा ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Having heard these words of Andhaka, the steadfast Bhārgava / then deliberated with an aching heart:

2.5.s:
kiṃ kartavyaṃ mayādyāpi kṣemaṃ me syātkathaṃ tviti |
sannipātavidhirjīvaḥ sarvathānucito mama ||
2.5.d:
किं कर्तव्यं मयाद्यापि क्षेमं मे स्यात्कथं त्विति ।
सन्निपातविधिर्जीवः सर्वथानुचितो मम ॥
2.5.m: “What should be done by me now, so that there may be well-being for me? / A clash of vital forces is completely improper for me.

2.5.s:
vidyeyaṃ śaṅkarātprāptā tadguṇān prati yojaye |
tadraṇe marditānvīraiḥ pramathaiḥ śaṅkarānugaiḥ ||
2.5.d:
विद्येयं शङ्करात्प्राप्ता तद्गुणान् प्रति योजये ।
तद्रणे मर्दितान्वीरैः प्रमथैः शङ्करानुगैः ॥
2.5.m: This lore was obtained from Śaṅkara; shall I apply it against his own qualities, / in battle, against those crushed by the heroic Pramathas, the followers of Śaṅkara?”

2.5.s:
śaraṇāgatadharmo'tha pravaraḥ sarvato hṛdā |
vicārya śukreṇa dhiyā tadvāṇī svīkṛtā tadā ||
2.5.d:
शरणागतधर्मोऽथ प्रवरः सर्वतो हृदा ।
विचार्य शुक्रेण धिया तद्वाणी स्वीकृता तदा ॥
2.5.m: Reflecting in his heart that the duty toward one who has sought refuge is preeminent above all, / Śukra with his intellect then accepted his words.

2.5.s:
kiñcitsmitaṃ tadā kṛtvā so'bravīddānavādhipam |
bhārgavaḥ śivapādābjaṃ smṛtvā svasthena cetasā ||
2.5.d:
किञ्चित्स्मितं तदा कृत्वा सोऽब्रवीद्दानवाधिपम् ।
भार्गवः शिवपादाब्जं स्मृत्वा स्वस्थेन चेतसा ॥
2.5.m: Smiling slightly, Bhārgava then spoke to the lord of the Dānavas / with a composed mind, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva:

2.5.s:
śukra uvāca |
yattvayā bhāṣitaṃ tāta tatsarvaṃ tathyameva hi |
etadvidyopārjanaṃ hi dānavārthaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā ||
2.5.d:
शुक्र उवाच ।
यत्त्वया भाषितं तात तत्सर्वं तथ्यमेव हि ।
एतद्विद्योपार्जनं हि दानवार्थं कृतं मया ॥
2.5.m: Śukra said: / What has been spoken by you, dear one, is indeed completely true; / for the acquisition of this lore was undertaken by me for the sake of the Dānavas.

2.5.s:
duḥsahaṃ kaṇadhūmaṃ vai pītvā varṣasahasrakam |
vidyeyamīśvarātprāptā bandhūnāṃ sukhadā sadā ||
2.5.d:
दुःसहं कणधूमं वै पीत्वा वर्षसहस्रकम् ।
विद्येयमीश्वरात्प्राप्ता बन्धूनां सुखदा सदा ॥
2.5.m: Having inhaled unbearable smoke of chaff for a thousand years, / this lore was obtained from the Lord, bestowing happiness on my kinsmen forever.

2.5.s:
pramathairmathitāndaityān raṇe'haṃ vidyayānayā |
utthāpayiṣye mlānāni śasyāni jalabhugyathā ||
2.5.d:
प्रमथैर्मथितान्दैत्यान् रणेऽहं विद्ययानया ।
उत्थापयिष्ये म्लानानि शस्यानि जलभुग्यथा ॥
2.5.m: By means of this lore I will raise up in battle the Daityas crushed by the Pramathas, / just as a rain cloud revives withered crops.

2.5.s:
nirvraṇānnīrujaḥ svasthān suptveva punarutthitān |
muhūrte'smiṃśca draṣṭāsi daityāṃstānutthitānnijān ||
2.5.d:
निर्व्रणान्नीरुजः स्वस्थान् सुप्त्वेव पुनरुत्थितान् ।
मुहूर्तेऽस्मिंश्च द्रष्टासि दैत्यांस्तानुत्थितान्निजान् ॥
2.5.m: Free from wounds, healthy, restored, as if rising after having slept— / in this very moment you shall see those Daityas of yours risen.

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
ityuktvā so'dhakaṃ śukro vidyāmāvartayatkaviḥ |
ekaikaṃ daityamuddiśya smṛtvā vidyeśamādarāt ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा सोऽधकं शुक्रो विद्यामावर्तयत्कविः ।
एकैकं दैत्यमुद्दिश्य स्मृत्वा विद्येशमादरात् ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Having spoken thus to Andhaka, the poet Śukra recited the lore, / directing it toward each individual Daitya and respectfully remembering the Lord of Lore.

2.5.s:
vidyāvartanamātreṇa te sarve daityadānavāḥ |
uttasthuryugapadvīrāḥ suptā iva dhṛtāyudhāḥ ||
2.5.d:
विद्यावर्तनमात्रेण ते सर्वे दैत्यदानवाः ।
उत्तस्थुर्युगपद्वीराः सुप्ता इव धृतायुधाः ॥
2.5.m: Merely upon the recitation of the lore, all those heroic Daityas and Dānavas / stood up simultaneously with their weapons grasped, as though rising from sleep,

2.5.s:
sadābhyastā yathā vedāḥ samaye vā yathāmbudāḥ |
śraddhayārthāstathā dattā brāhmaṇebhyo yathāpadi ||
2.5.d:
सदाभ्यस्ता यथा वेदाः समये वा यथाम्बुदाः ।
श्रद्धयार्थास्तथा दत्ता ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यथापदि ॥
2.5.m: just like the Vedas when constantly practiced, or clouds in their season, / or wealth given with faith to brahmins in times of distress.

2.5.s:
ujjīvitāṃstu tāndṛṣṭvā huṇḍādīṃśca mahāsurān |
vinedurasurāḥ sarve jalapūrṇā ivāmbudāḥ ||
2.5.d:
उज्जीवितांस्तु तान्दृष्ट्वा हुण्डादींश्च महासुरान् ।
विनेदुरसुराः सर्वे जलपूर्णा इवाम्बुदाः ॥
2.5.m: Seeing those great asuras, Huṇḍa and others, revived, / all the asuras roared aloud like clouds full of water.

2.5.s:
raṇodyatāḥ punaścāsangarjanto vikaṭān ravān |
pramathaiḥ saha nirbhītā mahābalaparākramāḥ ||
2.5.d:
रणोद्यताः पुनश्चासन्गर्जन्तो विकटान् रवान् ।
प्रमथैः सह निर्भीता महाबलपराक्रमाः ॥
2.5.m: Endowed with great strength and valor, fearless, / and roaring with terrifying shouts, they once again prepared for battle against the Pramathas.

2.5.s:
śukreṇojjīvitāndṛṣṭvā pramathā daityadānavān |
visiṣmire tataḥ sarve nandyādyā yuddhadurmadāḥ ||
2.5.d:
शुक्रेणोज्जीवितान्दृष्ट्वा प्रमथा दैत्यदानवान् ।
विसिष्मिरे ततः सर्वे नन्द्याद्या युद्धदुर्मदाः ॥
2.5.m: Seeing the Daityas and Dānavas revived by Śukra, / all the Pramathas, Nandin and others, fierce in battle, were astonished.

2.5.s:
vijñāpyamevaṃ karmaitaddeveśe śaṅkare'khilam |
vicārya buddhimantaśca hyevaṃ te'nyonyamabruvan ||
2.5.d:
विज्ञाप्यमेवं कर्मैतद्देवेशे शङ्करेऽखिलम् ।
विचार्य बुद्धिमन्तश्च ह्येवं तेऽन्योन्यमब्रुवन् ॥
2.5.m: Considering that this whole matter should be reported to the lord of the gods, Śaṅkara, / those wise ones spoke thus to one another.

2.5.s:
āścaryarūpe pramatheśvarāṇāṃ tasmiṃstathā vartati yuddhayajñe |
amarṣito bhārgavakarma dṛṣṭvā śilādaputro'bhyagamanmaheśam ||
2.5.d:
आश्चर्यरूपे प्रमथेश्वराणां तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तति युद्धयज्ञे ।
अमर्षितो भार्गवकर्म दृष्ट्वा शिलादपुत्रोऽभ्यगमन्महेशम् ॥
2.5.m: While that sacrifice of battle of the lords of Pramathas, marvelous in form, was thus taking place, / the son of Śilāda, indignant upon seeing the deed of Bhārgava, went to Maheśa.

2.5.s:
jayeti coktvā jayayonimugra-muvāca nandī kanakāvadātam |
gaṇeśvarāṇāṃ raṇakarma deva devaiśca sendrairapi duṣkaraṃ yat ||
2.5.d:
जयेति चोक्त्वा जययोनिमुग्र-मुवाच नन्दी कनकावदातम् ।
गणेश्वराणां रणकर्म देव देवैश्च सेन्द्रैरपि दुष्करं यत् ॥
2.5.m: Having said, “Victory!”, Nandin spoke to the source of victory, the fierce one radiant like gold, / concerning that battle-work of the lords of attendants, O God, which is difficult even for the gods headed by Indra.

2.5.s:
tadbhārgaveṇādya kṛtaṃ vṛthā naḥ sañjīvitāṃstānhi mṛtānvipakṣān |
āvartya vidyāṃ mṛtajīvadātrī-mekaikamuddiśya sahelamīśa ||
2.5.d:
तद्भार्गवेणाद्य कृतं वृथा नः सञ्जीवितांस्तान्हि मृतान्विपक्षान् ।
आवर्त्य विद्यां मृतजीवदात्री-मेकैकमुद्दिश्य सहेलमीश ॥
2.5.m:
That has been rendered futile today by Bhārgava, O Īśa,
for having recited the lore that restores life to the dead, he effortlessly revived those dead enemies one by one.

2.5.s:
tuhuṇḍahuṇḍādikakumbhajambha-vipākapākādimahāsurendrāḥ |
yamālayādadya punarnivṛttā vidrāvayantaḥ pramathāṃścaranti ||
2.5.d:
तुहुण्डहुण्डादिककुम्भजम्भ-विपाकपाकादिमहासुरेन्द्राः ।
यमालयादद्य पुनर्निवृत्ता विद्रावयन्तः प्रमथांश्चरन्ति ॥
2.5.m:
The great lords of the asuras—Tuhuṇḍa, Huṇḍa, and the others, Kumbha, Jambha, Vipāka, Pāka, and the rest—
having returned today from Yama's abode, are roaming about, putting the pramathas to flight.

2.5.s:
yadi hyasau daityavarānnirastān sañjīvayedatra punaḥ punastān |
jayaḥ kuto no bhavitā maheśa gaṇeśvarāṇāṃ kuta eva śāntiḥ ||
2.5.d:
यदि ह्यसौ दैत्यवरान्निरस्तान् सञ्जीवयेदत्र पुनः पुनस्तान् ।
जयः कुतो नो भविता महेश गणेश्वराणां कुत एव शान्तिः ॥
2.5.m:
If he continues to revive those best of daityas time and again as they are struck down here,
whence shall come our victory, O Maheśa? Whence indeed shall come peace for the lords of the attendants?

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
ityevamuktaḥ pramatheśvareṇa sa nandinā vai pramatheśvareśaḥ |
uvāca devaḥ prahasaṃstadānīṃ taṃ nandinaṃ sarvagaṇeśarājam ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
इत्येवमुक्तः प्रमथेश्वरेण स नन्दिना वै प्रमथेश्वरेशः ।
उवाच देवः प्रहसंस्तदानीं तं नन्दिनं सर्वगणेशराजम् ॥
2.5.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Addressed thus by Nandin, lord of the pramathas, the god, the lord of the lords of the pramathas,
laughing at that moment, spoke to Nandin, the king of all lords of the attendants.

2.5.s:
śiva uvāca |
nandinprayāhi tvarito'ti mātraṃ dvijendravaryaṃ ditinandanānām |
madhyātsamuddhṛtya tathānayāśu śyeno yathā lāvakamaṇḍajātam ||
2.5.d:
शिव उवाच ।
नन्दिन्प्रयाहि त्वरितोऽति मात्रं द्विजेन्द्रवर्यं दितिनन्दनानाम् ।
मध्यात्समुद्धृत्य तथानयाशु श्येनो यथा लावकमण्डजातम् ॥
2.5.m:
Śiva said:
Go with utmost speed, Nandin! Seizing that foremost of the twice-born
from the midst of the sons of Diti, bring him swiftly, as a hawk carries off an egg-born quail.

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
sa evamukto vṛṣabhadhvajena nanāda nandī vṛṣasiṃhanādaḥ |
jagāma tūrṇaṃ ca vigāhya senāṃ yatrābhavadbhārgavavaṃśadīpaḥ ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
स एवमुक्तो वृषभध्वजेन ननाद नन्दी वृषसिंहनादः ।
जगाम तूर्णं च विगाह्य सेनां यत्राभवद्भार्गववंशदीपः ॥
2.5.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Addressed thus by Vṛṣabhadhvaja, Nandin roared with the roar of a bull and a lion,
and quickly penetrating the army, went to where the lamp of the Bhṛgu lineage was.

2.5.s:
taṃ rakṣyamāṇaṃ ditijaiḥ samastaiḥ pāśāsivṛkṣopalaśailahastaiḥ |
vikṣobhya daityān balavān jahāra kāvyaṃ sa nandī śarabho yathebham ||
2.5.d:
तं रक्ष्यमाणं दितिजैः समस्तैः पाशासिवृक्षोपलशैलहस्तैः ।
विक्षोभ्य दैत्यान् बलवान् जहार काव्यं स नन्दी शरभो यथेभम् ॥
2.5.m:
While he was guarded by all the sons of Diti, bearing nooses, swords, trees, stones, and mountains in their hands,
the mighty Nandin agitated the daityas and seized Kāvya, like a śarabha an elephant.

2.5.s:
srastāmbaraṃ vicyutabhūṣaṇaṃ ca vimuktakeśaṃ balinā gṛhītam |
vimocayiṣyanta ivānujagmuḥ surārayassiṃharavāṃstyajantaḥ ||
2.5.d:
स्रस्ताम्बरं विच्युतभूषणं च विमुक्तकेशं बलिना गृहीतम् ।
विमोचयिष्यन्त इवानुजग्मुः सुरारयस्सिंहरवांस्त्यजन्तः ॥
2.5.m:
With his garments slipping down, his ornaments fallen, his hair disheveled, and seized by that strong one,
the enemies of the gods followed, as if to release him, letting out lion-roars.

2.5.s:
dambholiśūlāsiparaśvadhānā-muddaṇḍacakropalakampanānām |
nandīśvarasyopari dānavendrā varṣaṃ vavarṣurjaladā ivogram ||
2.5.d:
दम्भोलिशूलासिपरश्वधाना-मुद्दण्डचक्रोपलकम्पनानाम् ।
नन्दीश्वरस्योपरि दानवेन्द्रा वर्षं ववर्षुर्जलदा इवोग्रम् ॥
2.5.m:
Upon Nandīśvara the lords of the dānavas showered a fierce shower
of thunderbolts, spears, swords, battle-axes, raised discs, stones, and missiles, like rain clouds.

2.5.s:
taṃ bhārgavaṃ prāpya gaṇādhirājo mukhāgninā śastraśatāni dagdhvā |
āyātpravṛddhe'suradevayuddhe bhavasya pārśve vyathitāripakṣaḥ ||
2.5.d:
तं भार्गवं प्राप्य गणाधिराजो मुखाग्निना शस्त्रशतानि दग्ध्वा ।
आयात्प्रवृद्धेऽसुरदेवयुद्धे भवस्य पार्श्वे व्यथितारिपक्षः ॥
2.5.m:
Having seized that Bhārgava, burning hundreds of weapons with the fire of his mouth,
the ruler of the attendants, tormenting the enemy host as the battle between asuras and gods intensified, came before Bhava.

2.5.s:
ayaṃ sa śukro bhagavannitīdaṃ nivedayāmāsa bhavāya śīghram |
jagrāha śukraṃ sa ca devadevo yathopahāraṃ śucinā pradattam ||
2.5.d:
अयं स शुक्रो भगवन्नितीदं निवेदयामास भवाय शीघ्रम् ।
जग्राह शुक्रं स च देवदेवो यथोपहारं शुचिना प्रदत्तम् ॥
2.5.m:
He swiftly presented him to Bhava, saying: 'This is that Śukra, O Lord!'
And the god of gods took Śukra, like an offering presented by a pure person.

2.5.s:
na kiñciduktvā sa hi bhūtagoptā cikṣepa vaktre phalavatkavīndram |
hāhāravastairasuraiḥsamastai-ruccairvimukto hahaheti bhūri ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ pañcamo yuddhakhaṇḍe
2.5.d:
न किञ्चिदुक्त्वा स हि भूतगोप्ता चिक्षेप वक्त्रे फलवत्कवीन्द्रम् ।
हाहारवस्तैरसुरैःसमस्तै-रुच्चैर्विमुक्तो हहहेति भूरि ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां पञ्चमो युद्धखण्डे

2.5.s:
vyāsa uvāca |
śukre nigīrṇe rudreṇa kimakārṣuśca dānavāḥ |
andhakeśā mahāvīrā vada tattvaṃ mahāmune ||
2.5.d:
व्यास उवाच ।
शुक्रे निगीर्णे रुद्रेण किमकार्षुश्च दानवाः ।
अन्धकेशा महावीरा वद तत्त्वं महामुने ॥
2.5.m:
Vyāsa said:
When Śukra was swallowed by Rudra, what did the dānavas do,
those great heroes headed by Andhaka? Tell the truth, O great sage!

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
kāvye nigīrṇe girijeśvareṇa daityā jayāśārahitā babhūvuḥ |
hastairvimuktā iva vāraṇendrāḥ śaṛṅgairvihīnā iva govṛṣāśca ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
काव्ये निगीर्णे गिरिजेश्वरेण दैत्या जयाशारहिता बभूवुः ।
हस्तैर्विमुक्ता इव वारणेन्द्राः शऋङ्गैर्विहीना इव गोवृषाश्च ॥
2.5.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
When Kāvya was swallowed by the lord of the Mountain's Daughter, the daityas were deprived of all hope of victory,
like lordly elephants deprived of their trunks, or bulls deprived of their horns,

2.5.s:
śiro vihīnā iva dehasaṅghā dvijā yathā cādhyayanena hīnāḥ |
nirudyamāḥ sattvagaṇā yathā vai yathodyamā bhāgyavivarjitāśca ||
2.5.d:
शिरो विहीना इव देहसङ्घा द्विजा यथा चाध्ययनेन हीनाः ।
निरुद्यमाः सत्त्वगणा यथा वै यथोद्यमा भाग्यविवर्जिताश्च ॥
2.5.m:
like hosts of bodies deprived of heads, or twice-born men deprived of Vedic study,
like groups of beings without effort, or like efforts deserted by fortune,

2.5.s:
patyā vihīnāśca yathaiva yoṣā yathā vipakṣāḥ khalu pakṣiṇaughāḥ |
āyūṃṣi hīnāni yathaiva puṇyai-rvratairvihīnāni yathā śrutāni ||
2.5.d:
पत्या विहीनाश्च यथैव योषा यथा विपक्षाः खलु पक्षिणौघाः ।
आयूंषि हीनानि यथैव पुण्यै-र्व्रतैर्विहीनानि यथा श्रुतानि ॥
2.5.m:
like women deprived of a husband, or flocks of birds deprived of wings,
like lifespans devoid of merits, or sacred traditions devoid of vows,

2.5.s:
vinā yathā vaibhavaśaktimekāṃ bhavanti hīnāḥsvaphalaiḥ kriyaughāḥ |
yathā viśūrāḥ khalu kṣatriyāśca satyaṃ vinā dharmagaṇo yathaiva ||
2.5.d:
विना यथा वैभवशक्तिमेकां भवन्ति हीनाःस्वफलैः क्रियौघाः ।
यथा विशूराः खलु क्षत्रियाश्च सत्यं विना धर्मगणो यथैव ॥
2.5.m:
like heaps of ritual actions lacking their results without the unique power of supreme majesty,
like kṣatriyas without valour, or a multitude of virtues without truth.

2.5.s:
nandinā ca hṛte śukre gilite ca viṣādinā |
viṣādamagamandaityā yatamānaraṇotsavāḥ ||
2.5.d:
नन्दिना च हृते शुक्रे गिलिते च विषादिना ।
विषादमगमन्दैत्या यतमानरणोत्सवाः ॥
2.5.m:
When Śukra was carried off by Nandin and swallowed by the consumer of poison,
the daityas, who had striven in the celebration of battle, fell into dejection.

2.5.s:
tān vīkṣya vigatotsāhānandhakaḥ pratyabhāṣata |
daityāṃstu huṇḍahuṇḍādīnmahādhīraparākramaḥ ||
2.5.d:
तान् वीक्ष्य विगतोत्साहानन्धकः प्रत्यभाषत ।
दैत्यांस्तु हुण्डहुण्डादीन्महाधीरपराक्रमः ॥
2.5.m:
Seeing them drained of enthusiasm, Andhaka, possessing great steadiness and valor,
spoke to the daityas, Tuhuṇḍa, Huṇḍa, and the others.

2.5.s:
andhaka uvāca |
kaviṃ vikramya nayatā nandinā vañcitā vayam |
tanūrvinā kṛtāḥ prāṇāḥ sarveṣāmadya no nanu ||
dhairyaṃ vīryaṃ gatiḥ kīrtiḥ sattvaṃ tejaḥ parākramaḥ |
yugapanno hṛtaṃ sarvamekasmin bhārgave hṛte ||
2.5.d:
अन्धक उवाच ।
कविं विक्रम्य नयता नन्दिना वञ्चिता वयम् ।
तनूर्विना कृताः प्राणाः सर्वेषामद्य नो ननु ॥
धैर्यं वीर्यं गतिः कीर्तिः सत्त्वं तेजः पराक्रमः ।
युगपन्नो हृतं सर्वमेकस्मिन् भार्गवे हृते ॥
2.5.m:
Andhaka said:
We have been deceived by Nandin, who carried off Kavi through valor!
Indeed, today the life-breaths of all of us have been left without bodies.

Firmness, strength, course of action, fame, courage, splendor, prowess—
all of ours has been taken away at once, when the single Bhārgava was taken away.

2.5.s:
dhigasmān kulapūjyo yaireko'pi kulasattamaḥ |
guruḥ sarvasamarthaśca trātā trāto na cāpadi ||
2.5.d:
धिगस्मान् कुलपूज्यो यैरेकोऽपि कुलसत्तमः ।
गुरुः सर्वसमर्थश्च त्राता त्रातो न चापदि ॥
2.5.m:
Shame on us! For even one guru, worshipped by the family, the best of the family,
all-capable and our protector, was not protected in calamity.

2.5.s:
tadyūyamavilambyeha yudhyadhvamaribhiḥ saha |
vīraistaiḥ pramathairvīrāḥ smṛtvā gurupadāmbujam ||
2.5.d:
तद्यूयमविलम्ब्येह युध्यध्वमरिभिः सह ।
वीरैस्तैः प्रमथैर्वीराः स्मृत्वा गुरुपदाम्बुजम् ॥
2.5.m:
Therefore, do not delay here, but fight with the enemies,
those heroic pramathas, O heroes, remembering the lotus feet of the guru!

2.5.s:
guroḥ kāvyasya sukhadau smṛtvā caraṇapaṅkajau |
sūdayiṣyāmyahaṃ sarvān pramathān saha nandinā ||
2.5.d:
गुरोः काव्यस्य सुखदौ स्मृत्वा चरणपङ्कजौ ।
सूदयिष्याम्यहं सर्वान् प्रमथान् सह नन्दिना ॥
2.5.m:
Remembering the lotus feet of our guru Kāvya, the bestower of joy,
I myself shall destroy all the pramathas along with Nandin.

2.5.s:
adyaitān vivaśān hatvā sahadevaiḥ savāsavaiḥ |
bhārgavaṃ mocayiṣyāmi jīvaṃ yogīva karmataḥ ||
2.5.d:
अद्यैतान् विवशान् हत्वा सहदेवैः सवासवैः ।
भार्गवं मोचयिष्यामि जीवं योगीव कर्मतः ॥
2.5.m:
Slaying these helpless ones today along with the gods and Indra,
I shall release Bhārgava, as a yogin releases the soul from action.

2.5.s:
sa cāpi yogī yogena yadi nāma svayaṃ prabhuḥ |
śarīrāttasya nirgacchedasmākaṃ śeṣapālakaḥ ||
2.5.d:
स चापि योगी योगेन यदि नाम स्वयं प्रभुः ।
शरीरात्तस्य निर्गच्छेदस्माकं शेषपालकः ॥
2.5.m:
Moreover, being a yogin himself through yoga, if that powerful one
were to emerge of his own accord from his body, he would protect what remains of us.

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
ityandhakavacaḥ śrutvā dānavā meghanissvanāḥ |
pramathān nirdayāḥ prāhurmartavye kṛtaniścayāḥ ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
इत्यन्धकवचः श्रुत्वा दानवा मेघनिस्स्वनाः ।
प्रमथान् निर्दयाः प्राहुर्मर्तव्ये कृतनिश्चयाः ॥
2.5.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Hearing the words of Andhaka, the dānavas, rumbling like clouds,
resolved upon dying and, showing no pity, said to the pramathas:

2.5.s:
satyāyuṣi na no jātu śaktāḥ syuḥ pramathā balāt |
asatyāyuṣi kiṃ gatvā tyaktvā svāminamāhave ||
2.5.d:
सत्यायुषि न नो जातु शक्ताः स्युः प्रमथा बलात् ।
असत्यायुषि किं गत्वा त्यक्त्वा स्वामिनमाहवे ॥
2.5.m:
'If our lifespan remains, the pramathas could never overcome us by force;
and if our lifespan has ended, what is the point of going away and abandoning our master in battle?

2.5.s:
ye svāminaṃ vihāyāto bahumānadhanā janāḥ |
yānti te yānti niyatamandhatāmisramālayam ||
2.5.d:
ये स्वामिनं विहायातो बहुमानधना जनाः ।
यान्ति ते यान्ति नियतमन्धतामिस्रमालयम् ॥
2.5.m:
Those men whose wealth is high honor, if they abandon their master and flee,
they certainly go to the abode of Blind Darkness.

2.5.s:
ayaśastamasā khyātiṃ malinīkṛtya bhūriśaḥ |
ihāmutrāpi sukhino na syurbhagnā raṇājire ||
2.5.d:
अयशस्तमसा ख्यातिं मलिनीकृत्य भूरिशः ।
इहामुत्रापि सुखिनो न स्युर्भग्ना रणाजिरे ॥
2.5.m:
Staining their fame deeply with the darkness of disgrace,
those broken on the battlefield could never be happy in this world or the next.

2.5.s:
kiṃ dānaiḥ kiṃ tapobhiśca kiṃ tīrthaparimajjanaiḥ |
dharātīrthe yadi snānaṃ punarbhavamalāpahe ||
2.5.d:
किं दानैः किं तपोभिश्च किं तीर्थपरिमज्जनैः ।
धरातीर्थे यदि स्नानं पुनर्भवमलापहे ॥
2.5.m:
What is the use of gifts, what of austerities, what of immersions in sacred fords,
if there is a bath in the ford of the earth that cleanses the impurity of rebirth?'

2.5.s:
sampradhāryeti tadvākyaṃ daityāste danujāstathā |
mamanthuḥ pramathānājau raṇabherīṃ ninādya ca ||
2.5.d:
सम्प्रधार्येति तद्वाक्यं दैत्यास्ते दनुजास्तथा ।
ममन्थुः प्रमथानाजौ रणभेरीं निनाद्य च ॥
2.5.m:
Resolving thus upon those words, those daityas and danujas
sounded the war drums and pounded the pramathas in battle.

2.5.s:
tatra bāṇāsivajraughaiḥ kaṭhinaiśca śilāmayaiḥ |
bhuśuṇḍibhindipālaiśca śakti bhallaparaśvadhaiḥ ||
2.5.d:
तत्र बाणासिवज्रौघैः कठिनैश्च शिलामयैः ।
भुशुण्डिभिन्दिपालैश्च शक्ति भल्लपरश्वधैः ॥
2.5.m:
There, with hosts of arrows, swords, and thunderbolts, and hard stones,
with bhuśuṇḍis, slings, lances, barbed darts, and axes,

2.5.s:
khaṭvāṅgaiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ śūlairlakuṭairmusalairalam |
parasparamabhighnantaḥ pracakruḥ kadanaṃ mahat ||
2.5.d:
खट्वाङ्गैः पट्टिशैः शूलैर्लकुटैर्मुसलैरलम् ।
परस्परमभिघ्नन्तः प्रचक्रुः कदनं महत् ॥
2.5.m:
with khaṭvāṅgas, paṭṭiśas, spears, clubs, and maces in abundance,
striking one another, they wrought great slaughter.

2.5.s:
kārmukāṇāṃ vikṛṣṭānāṃ patatāṃ ca patattriṇām |
bhindipālabhuśuṇḍīnāṃ kṣveḍitānāṃ ravo'bhavat ||
2.5.d:
कार्मुकाणां विकृष्टानां पततां च पतत्त्रिणाम् ।
भिन्दिपालभुशुण्डीनां क्ष्वेडितानां रवोऽभवत् ॥
2.5.m:
There was the sound of bows being drawn, of arrows falling,
of slings and bhuśuṇḍis, and of battle cries.

2.5.s:
raṇatūryyaninādaiśca gajānāṃ bahubṛṃhitaiḥ |
hreṣāravairhayānāṃśca mahānkolāhalo'bhavat ||
2.5.d:
रणतूर्य्यनिनादैश्च गजानां बहुबृंहितैः ।
ह्रेषारवैर्हयानांश्च महान्कोलाहलोऽभवत् ॥
2.5.m:
With the sounds of war trumpets, the numerous trumpetings of elephants,
and the neighing sounds of horses, a great uproar arose.

2.5.s:
atisvanairavāpūri dyāvābhūmyoryadantaram |
abhīrūṇāṃ ca bhīrūṇāṃ mahāromodgamo'bhavat ||
2.5.d:
अतिस्वनैरवापूरि द्यावाभूम्योर्यदन्तरम् ।
अभीरूणां च भीरूणां महारोमोद्गमोऽभवत् ॥
2.5.m:
The space between heaven and earth was filled with tremendous sounds,
and hair stood on end both for the fearless and for the fearful.

2.5.s:
gajavājimahārāvasphuṭaśabdagrahāṇi ca |
bhagnadhvajapatākāni kṣīṇapraharaṇāni ca ||
2.5.d:
गजवाजिमहारावस्फुटशब्दग्रहाणि च ।
भग्नध्वजपताकानि क्षीणप्रहरणानि च ॥
2.5.m:
There were clear catches of the loud sounds of elephants and horses,
banners and flags were broken, and weapons were shattered.

2.5.s:
rudhirodgāracitrāṇi vyaśvahastirathāni ca |
pipāsitāni sainyāni mumūrcchurubhayatra vai ||
2.5.d:
रुधिरोद्गारचित्राणि व्यश्वहस्तिरथानि च ।
पिपासितानि सैन्यानि मुमूर्च्छुरुभयत्र वै ॥
2.5.m: strewn with spewed blood, bereft of horses, elephants, and chariots, / the armies on both sides became parched with thirst and swooned.

2.5.s:
atha te pramathā vīrā nandiprabhṛtayastadā |
balena jaghnurasurānsarvānprāpurjayaṃ mune ||
2.5.d:
अथ ते प्रमथा वीरा नन्दिप्रभृतयस्तदा ।
बलेन जघ्नुरसुरान्सर्वान्प्रापुर्जयं मुने ॥
2.5.m: Then those heroic pramathas, led by Nandin, / struck down all the asuras by force and won victory, O sage.

2.5.s:
dṛṣṭvā sainyaṃ ca pramathairbhajyamānamitastataḥ |
dudrāva rathamāsthāya svayamevāndhako gaṇān ||
2.5.d:
दृष्ट्वा सैन्यं च प्रमथैर्भज्यमानमितस्ततः ।
दुद्राव रथमास्थाय स्वयमेवान्धको गणान् ॥
2.5.m: Seeing his army broken here and there by the pramathas, / Andhaka himself mounted his chariot and rushed against the attendants.

2.5.s:
śarāsāraprayuktaistairvajrapātairnagā iva |
pramathā neśire cāstrairnistoyā iva toyadāḥ ||
2.5.d:
शरासारप्रयुक्तैस्तैर्वज्रपातैर्नगा इव ।
प्रमथा नेशिरे चास्त्रैर्निस्तोया इव तोयदाः ॥
2.5.m: Struck by his torrents of arrows like mountains by thunderbolts, / the pramathas fell before his weapons like waterless clouds.

2.5.s:
yāntamāyāntamālokya dūrasthaṃ nikaṭasthitam |
pratyekaṃ romasaṅkhyābhirvivyādheṣubhirandhakaḥ ||
2.5.d:
यान्तमायान्तमालोक्य दूरस्थं निकटस्थितम् ।
प्रत्येकं रोमसङ्ख्याभिर्विव्याधेषुभिरन्धकः ॥
2.5.m: Looking at anyone advancing or retreating, standing far or standing near, / Andhaka pierced each one with arrows equal in number to the hairs [on their bodies].

2.5.s:
dṛṣṭvā sainyaṃ bhajyamānamandhakena balīyasā |
skando vināyako nandī somanandyādayaḥ pare ||
2.5.d:
दृष्ट्वा सैन्यं भज्यमानमन्धकेन बलीयसा ।
स्कन्दो विनायको नन्दी सोमनन्द्यादयः परे ॥
2.5.m: Seeing their army broken by the powerful Andhaka, / Skanda, Vināyaka, Nandin, Somanandin, and the rest,

2.5.s:
pramathā prabalā vīrāḥ śaṅkarasya gaṇā nijāḥ |
cukrudhuḥ samaraṃ cakrurvicitraṃ ca mahābalāḥ ||
2.5.d:
प्रमथा प्रबला वीराः शङ्करस्य गणा निजाः ।
चुक्रुधुः समरं चक्रुर्विचित्रं च महाबलाः ॥
2.5.m: the mighty, heroic pramathas, Śaṅkara's own attendants, / were enraged, and possessing great strength, waged an extraordinary battle.

2.5.s:
vināyakena skandena nandinā somanandinā |
vīreṇa naigameyena vaiśākhena balīyasā ||
2.5.d:
विनायकेन स्कन्देन नन्दिना सोमनन्दिना ।
वीरेण नैगमेयेन वैशाखेन बलीयसा ॥
2.5.m: By Vināyaka, Skanda, Nandin, Somanandin, / the heroic Naigameya, and the powerful Vaiśākha,

2.5.s:
ityādyaistu gaṇairugrairandhako'pyandhakīkṛtaḥ |
triśūlaśaktibāṇaughadhārāsampātapātibhiḥ ||
2.5.d:
इत्याद्यैस्तु गणैरुग्रैरन्धकोऽप्यन्धकीकृतः ।
त्रिशूलशक्तिबाणौघधारासम्पातपातिभिः ॥
2.5.m: and other fierce attendants, Andhaka was blinded [with weapons], / smitten down by showers and torrents of tridents, darts, and arrows.

2.5.s:
tataḥ kolāhalo jātaḥ pramathāsurasainyayoḥ |
tena śabdena mahatā śukraḥ śambhūdare sthitaḥ ||
2.5.d:
ततः कोलाहलो जातः प्रमथासुरसैन्ययोः ।
तेन शब्देन महता शुक्रः शम्भूदरे स्थितः ॥
2.5.m: Then an uproar arose between the armies of the pramathas and the asuras. / Hearing that great sound, Śukra, who was inside Śambhu's belly,

2.5.s:
chidrānveṣī bhramanso'tha viniketo yathānilaḥ |
saptalokānsapātālān rudradehe vyalokayat ||
2.5.d:
छिद्रान्वेषी भ्रमन्सोऽथ विनिकेतो यथानिलः ।
सप्तलोकान्सपातालान् रुद्रदेहे व्यलोकयत् ॥
2.5.m: wandered looking for an exit, homeless like the wind; / and he beheld the seven worlds along with the netherworlds in Rudra's body,

2.5.s:
brahmanārāyaṇendrāṇāṃ sādityāpsarasāṃ tathā |
bhuvanāni vicitrāṇi yuddhaṃ ca pramathāsuram ||
2.5.d:
ब्रह्मनारायणेन्द्राणां सादित्याप्सरसां तथा ।
भुवनानि विचित्राणि युद्धं च प्रमथासुरम् ॥
2.5.m: as well as the wondrous realms of Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, and Indra, / along with the Ādityas and Apsarases, and the battle between the pramathas and asuras.

2.5.s:
sa varṣāṇāṃ śataṃ kukṣau bhavasya parito bhraman |
na tasya dadṛśe randhraṃ śuce randhraṃ khalo yathā ||
2.5.d:
स वर्षाणां शतं कुक्षौ भवस्य परितो भ्रमन् ।
न तस्य ददृशे रन्ध्रं शुचे रन्ध्रं खलो यथा ॥
2.5.m: Wandering around for a hundred years within Bhava's belly, / he did not see any opening, just as a wicked man finds no flaw in a pure person.

2.5.s:
śāmbhavenātha yogena śukrarūpeṇa bhārgavaḥ |
imaṃ mantravaraṃ japtvā śambhorjaṭharapañjarāt ||
2.5.d:
शाम्भवेनाथ योगेन शुक्ररूपेण भार्गवः ।
इमं मन्त्रवरं जप्त्वा शम्भोर्जठरपञ्जरात् ॥
2.5.m: Then, by Śaiva yoga, in the form of semen, the Bhārgava, / having recited this supreme mantra, from the cage of Śambhu's belly,

2.5.s:
niṣkrānto liṅgamārgeṇa praṇanāma tataḥ śivam |
gauryyā gṛhītaḥ putrārthaṃ tadavighneśvarīkṛtaḥ ||
2.5.d:
निष्क्रान्तो लिङ्गमार्गेण प्रणनाम ततः शिवम् ।
गौर्य्या गृहीतः पुत्रार्थं तदविघ्नेश्वरीकृतः ॥
2.5.m: emerged through the channel of the liṅga and then bowed down to Śiva. / He was accepted by Gaurī as a son and made free of obstacles.

2.5.s:
atha kāvyaṃ viniṣkrāntaṃ śukramārgeṇa bhārgavam |
dṛṣṭvovāca maheśāno vihasya karuṇānidhiḥ ||
2.5.d:
अथ काव्यं विनिष्क्रान्तं शुक्रमार्गेण भार्गवम् ।
दृष्ट्वोवाच महेशानो विहस्य करुणानिधिः ॥
2.5.m: Seeing Kāvya Bhārgava having emerged through the channel of semen, / Maheśāna, the treasury of compassion, smiled and said:

2.5.s:
maheśvara uvāca |
śukravanniḥsṛto yasmālliṅgānme bhṛgunandana |
karmaṇā tena śukrastvaṃ mama putro'si gamyatām ||
2.5.d:
महेश्वर उवाच ।
शुक्रवन्निःसृतो यस्माल्लिङ्गान्मे भृगुनन्दन ।
कर्मणा तेन शुक्रस्त्वं मम पुत्रोऽसि गम्यताम् ॥
2.5.m: Maheśvara said: / 'Because you came out from my liṅga like semen (śukra), O descendant of Bhṛgu, / by that deed you are Śukra and my son; you may go.'

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
ityevamukto devena śukro'rkasadṛśadyutiḥ |
praṇanāma śivaṃ bhūyastuṣṭāva vihitāñjaliḥ ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
इत्येवमुक्तो देवेन शुक्रोऽर्कसदृशद्युतिः ।
प्रणनाम शिवं भूयस्तुष्टाव विहिताञ्जलिः ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Addressed thus by the god, Śukra, who shone like the sun, / bowed down to Śiva again and praised him with joined palms.

2.5.s:
śukra uvāca |
anantapādastvamanantamūrti-ranantamūrddhāntakaraḥ śivaśca |
anantabāhuḥ kathamīdṛśaṃ tvāṃ stoṣye ha nutyaṃ praṇipatya mūrdhnā ||
2.5.d:
शुक्र उवाच ।
अनन्तपादस्त्वमनन्तमूर्ति-रनन्तमूर्द्धान्तकरः शिवश्च ।
अनन्तबाहुः कथमीदृशं त्वां स्तोष्ये ह नुत्यं प्रणिपत्य मूर्ध्ना ॥
2.5.m: Śukra said: / 'You have endless feet, endless forms, endless heads; you are the destroyer and auspicious Śiva; / you have endless arms. How can I, bowing with my head, praise such a one worthy of praise?

2.5.s:
tvamaṣṭamūrtistvamanantamūrti-stvamiṣṭadaḥ sarvasurāsurāṇām |
aniṣṭadṛṣṭeśca vimardakaśca stoṣye ha nutyaṃ kathamīdṛśaṃ tvām ||
2.5.d:
त्वमष्टमूर्तिस्त्वमनन्तमूर्ति-स्त्वमिष्टदः सर्वसुरासुराणाम् ।
अनिष्टदृष्टेश्च विमर्दकश्च स्तोष्ये ह नुत्यं कथमीदृशं त्वाम् ॥
2.5.m: You have eight forms, you have endless forms, you grant desires to all gods and asuras, / and you crush all malevolent designs. How can I praise such a one worthy of praise?'

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
iti stutvā śivaṃ śukraḥ punarnatvā śivājñayā |
viveśa dānavānīkaṃ meghamālāṃ yathā śaśī ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
इति स्तुत्वा शिवं शुक्रः पुनर्नत्वा शिवाज्ञया ।
विवेश दानवानीकं मेघमालां यथा शशी ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Having thus praised Śiva, and bowing again at Śiva's command, / Śukra entered the army of the Dānavas like the moon entering a bank of clouds.

2.5.s:
nigīrṇanamiti proktaṃ śaṅkareṇa kave raṇe |
śṛṇu mantraṃ ca taṃ japto yaḥ śambhoḥ kavinodare ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ pañcamo yuddhakhaṇḍe
2.5.d:
निगीर्णनमिति प्रोक्तं शङ्करेण कवे रणे ।
शृणु मन्त्रं च तं जप्तो यः शम्भोः कविनोदरे ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां पञ्चमो युद्धखण्डे
2.5.m:
Thus has been recounted the swallowing of Kavi by Śaṅkara in battle. / Now hear that mantra which was recited by Kavi inside Śambhu's belly.

Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter, named 'The Swallowing of Śukra', in the fifth section, the Yuddhakhaṇḍa, of the second book, the Rudrasaṃhitā, in the venerable Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
oṃ namaste deveśāya surāsuranamaskṛtāya bhūtabhavyamahādevāya haritapiṅgalalocanāya balāya buddhirūpiṇe vaiyāghravasanacchadāyāraṇeyāya trailokyaprabhave īśvarāya harāya harinetrāya yugāntakaraṇāyānalāya gaṇeśāya lokapālāya mahābhujāya mahāhastāya śūline mahādaṃṣṭriṇe kālāya maheśvarāya avyayāya kālarūpiṇe nīlagrīvāya mahodarāya gaṇādhyakṣāya sarvātmane sarvabhāvanāya sarvagāya mṛtyuhantre pāriyātrasuvratāya brahmacāriṇe vedāntagāya tapontagāya paśupataye vyaṅgāya śūlapāṇaye vṛṣaketave haraye jaṭine śikhaṇḍine lakuṭine mahāyaśase bhūteśvarāya guhāvāsine vīṇāpaṇavatālavate amarāya darśanīyāya bālasūrya-nibhāya śmaśānavāsine bhagavate umāpataye arindamāya bhagasyākṣipātine pūṣṇordaśananāśanāya krurakartakāya pāśahastāya pralayakālāya ulkāmukhāyāgniketave munaye dīptāya viśāmpataye unnayate janakāya caturthakāya lokasattamāya vāmadevāya vāgdākṣiṇyāya vāmato bhikṣave bhikṣurūpiṇe jaṭine svayaṃ jaṭilāya śakrahastapratistambhakāya vasūnāṃ stambhakāya kratave kratukarāya kālāya medhāvine madhukarāya calāya vānaspatyāya vājasaneti samāśramapūjitāya jagaddhātre jagatkartre puruṣāya śāśvatāya dhruvāya dharmādhyakṣāya trivartmane bhūtabhāvanāya trinetrāya bahurūpāya sūryāyutasamaprabhāya devāya sarvatūryaninādine sarvabādhāvimocanāya bandhanāya sarvadhāriṇe dharmottamāya puṣpadantāyāvibhāgāya mukhāya sarvaharāya hiraṇyaśravase dvāriṇe bhīmāya bhīmaparākramāya oṃ namo namaḥ ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
ओं नमस्ते देवेशाय सुरासुरनमस्कृताय भूतभव्यमहादेवाय हरितपिङ्गललोचनाय बलाय बुद्धिरूपिणे वैयाघ्रवसनच्छदायारणेयाय त्रैलोक्यप्रभवे ईश्वराय हराय हरिनेत्राय युगान्तकरणायानलाय गणेशाय लोकपालाय महाभुजाय महाहस्ताय शूलिने महादंष्ट्रिणे कालाय महेश्वराय अव्ययाय कालरूपिणे नीलग्रीवाय महोदराय गणाध्यक्षाय सर्वात्मने सर्वभावनाय सर्वगाय मृत्युहन्त्रे पारियात्रसुव्रताय ब्रह्मचारिणे वेदान्तगाय तपोन्तगाय पशुपतये व्यङ्गाय शूलपाणये वृषकेतवे हरये जटिने शिखण्डिने लकुटिने महायशसे भूतेश्वराय गुहावासिने वीणापणवतालवते अमराय दर्शनीयाय बालसूर्य-निभाय श्मशानवासिने भगवते उमापतये अरिन्दमाय भगस्याक्षिपातिने पूष्णोर्दशननाशनाय क्रुरकर्तकाय पाशहस्ताय प्रलयकालाय उल्कामुखायाग्निकेतवे मुनये दीप्ताय विशाम्पतये उन्नयते जनकाय चतुर्थकाय लोकसत्तमाय वामदेवाय वाग्दाक्षिण्याय वामतो भिक्षवे भिक्षुरूपिणे जटिने स्वयं जटिलाय शक्रहस्तप्रतिस्तम्भकाय वसूनां स्तम्भकाय क्रतवे क्रतुकराय कालाय मेधाविने मधुकराय चलाय वानस्पत्याय वाजसनेति समाश्रमपूजिताय जगद्धात्रे जगत्कर्त्रे पुरुषाय शाश्वताय ध्रुवाय धर्माध्यक्षाय त्रिवर्त्मने भूतभावनाय त्रिनेत्राय बहुरूपाय सूर्यायुतसमप्रभाय देवाय सर्वतूर्यनिनादिने सर्वबाधाविमोचनाय बन्धनाय सर्वधारिणे धर्मोत्तमाय पुष्पदन्तायाविभागाय मुखाय सर्वहराय हिरण्यश्रवसे द्वारिणे भीमाय भीमपराक्रमाय ओं नमो नमः ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / 'Oṃ, salutation to you, Lord of the Gods, revered by gods and asuras, Great God of the past and future, having greenish-yellow eyes, embodiment of strength and intelligence, wrapped in a tigerskin garment, fire born of friction, sovereign of the three worlds, Īśvara, Hara, whose eyes are green, maker of the dissolution of the world, fire, Gaṇeśa, guardian of the worlds, mighty-armed, great-handed, bearer of the trident, large-fanged, Death, Maheśvara, imperishable, form of Time, blue-necked, large-bellied, overseer of the attendants, soul of all, creator of all, omnipresent, destroyer of death, keeper of the vows of the Pāriyātra, celibate, student of the Vedānta, who has reached the end of austerity, Paśupati, bodiless, trident in hand, having the bull for an emblem, Hari, matted-haired, having a topknot, bearer of the staff, of great renown, lord of spirits, dweller in caves, possessing the lute, the paṇava drum, and rhythm, immortal, handsome to behold, resembling the morning sun, dweller in the cremation ground, blessed lord, husband of Umā, conqueror of enemies, tearer of the eyes of Bhaga, destroyer of the teeth of Pūṣan, cruel cutter, noose in hand, the time of cosmic dissolution, having a mouth of meteoric flame, fire-crested, sage, luminous, lord of the subjects, the uplifter, father, the fourth, best of the world, Vāmadeva, courteous in speech, mendicant on the left, having the form of a mendicant, matted-haired, himself having tangled locks, paralyser of Indra's arm, paralyzer of the Vasus, sacrifice, performer of sacrifice, Time, intelligent, maker of honey, restless, plant-like, revered in the ashram known as Vājasaneya, bearer of the universe, creator of the universe, Puruṣa, eternal, constant, presiding deity of righteousness, having three paths, creator of living beings, three-eyed, multiformed, radiant as ten thousand suns, god, making all musical instruments sound, deliverer from all affliction, bondage, bearer of all, supreme righteousness, Puṣpadanta, indivisible, face, taker of all, with golden ears, gatekeeper, terrible, of terrible prowess, Oṃ, salutation, salutation!'

2.5.s:
imaṃ mantravaraṃ japtvā śukro jaṭharapañjarāt |
niṣkrānto liṅgamārgeṇa śambhoḥ śukramivotkaṭam ||
2.5.d:
इमं मन्त्रवरं जप्त्वा शुक्रो जठरपञ्जरात् ।
निष्क्रान्तो लिङ्गमार्गेण शम्भोः शुक्रमिवोत्कटम् ॥
2.5.m: Reciting this supreme mantra, Śukra emerged from the cage of Śambhu's belly / through the channel of the liṅga, like vigorous semen.

2.5.s:
gauryā gṛhītaḥ putrārthaṃ viśveśena tataḥ kṛtaḥ |
ajaraścāmaraḥ śrīmāndvitīya iva śaṅkaraḥ ||
2.5.d:
गौर्या गृहीतः पुत्रार्थं विश्वेशेन ततः कृतः ।
अजरश्चामरः श्रीमान्द्वितीय इव शङ्करः ॥
2.5.m: He was accepted by Gaurī as a son and then made by the Lord of the Universe / ageless, immortal, glorious, like a second Śaṅkara.

2.5.s:
tribhirvarṣasahasraistu samatītairmahītale |
maheśvarātpunarjātaḥ śukro vedanidhirmuniḥ ||
2.5.d:
त्रिभिर्वर्षसहस्रैस्तु समतीतैर्महीतले ।
महेश्वरात्पुनर्जातः शुक्रो वेदनिधिर्मुनिः ॥
2.5.m: When three thousand years had passed on the surface of the earth, / the sage Śukra, treasury of the Vedas, was born again from Maheśvara.

2.5.s:
dadarśa śūle saṃśuṣkaṃ dhyāyantaṃ parameśvaram |
andhakaṃ dhairyasampannaṃ dānaveśaṃ tapasvinam ||
2.5.d:
ददर्श शूले संशुष्कं ध्यायन्तं परमेश्वरम् ।
अन्धकं धैर्यसम्पन्नं दानवेशं तपस्विनम् ॥
2.5.m: He saw Andhaka, dried up upon the trident, meditating on Parameśvara, / endowed with fortitude, lord of the Dānavas, practicing asceticism;

2.5.s:
mahādevaṃ virūpākṣaṃ candrārddhakṛtaśekharam |
amṛtaṃ śāśvataṃ sthāṇuṃ nīlakaṇṭhaṃ pinākinam ||
2.5.d:
महादेवं विरूपाक्षं चन्द्रार्द्धकृतशेखरम् ।
अमृतं शाश्वतं स्थाणुं नीलकण्ठं पिनाकिनम् ॥
2.5.m: and [he saw] Mahādeva, the odd-eyed, who wears the crescent moon on his crest, / immortal, eternal, motionless, blue-throated, bearer of the Pināka,

2.5.s:
vṛṣabhākṣaṃ mahājñeyaṃ puruṣaṃ sarvakāmadam |
kāmāriṃ kāmadahanaṃ kāmarūpaṃ kapardinam ||
2.5.d:
वृषभाक्षं महाज्ञेयं पुरुषं सर्वकामदम् ।
कामारिं कामदहनं कामरूपं कपर्दिनम् ॥
2.5.m: with eyes like a bull's, the great object of knowledge, the Puruṣa, giver of all desires, / enemy of Kāma, burner of Kāma, who assumes any form at will, with matted hair,

2.5.s:
virūpaṃ giriśaṃ bhīmaṃ sragviṇaṃ raktavāsasam |
yoginaṃ kāladahanaṃ tripuraghnaṃ kapālinam ||
2.5.d:
विरूपं गिरिशं भीमं स्रग्विणं रक्तवाससम् ।
योगिनं कालदहनं त्रिपुरघ्नं कपालिनम् ॥
2.5.m: monstrous, dweller in the mountains, formidable, garlanded, clad in red garments, / the yogin, burner of Time, slayer of Tripura, bearer of the skull.

2.5.s:
gūḍhavrataṃ guptamantraṃ gambhīraṃ bhāvagocaram |
aṇimādiguṇādhāraṃ trilokaiśvaryadāyakam ||
2.5.d:
गूढव्रतं गुप्तमन्त्रं गम्भीरं भावगोचरम् ।
अणिमादिगुणाधारं त्रिलोकैश्वर्यदायकम् ॥
2.5.m: [Meditating on him as] the one of secret observances, of concealed mantras, profound, accessible through devotion, / the receptacle of virtues such as anima, the giver of sovereignty over the three worlds,

2.5.s:
vīraṃ vīrahaṇaṃ ghoraṃ virūpaṃ māṃsalaṃ paṭum |
mahāmāṃsādamunmattaṃ bhairavaṃ vai maheśvaram ||
2.5.d:
वीरं वीरहणं घोरं विरूपं मांसलं पटुम् ।
महामांसादमुन्मत्तं भैरवं वै महेश्वरम् ॥
2.5.m: the heroic one, the slayer of heroes, fierce, grotesque, muscular, skillful, / the eater of great flesh, the ecstatic, Bhairava indeed, the great lord,

2.5.s:
trailokyadrāvaṇaṃ lubdhaṃ lubdhakaṃ yajñasūdanam |
kṛttikānāṃ sutairyuktamunmattaṃ kṛttivāsasam ||
2.5.d:
त्रैलोक्यद्रावणं लुब्धं लुब्धकं यज्ञसूदनम् ।
कृत्तिकानां सुतैर्युक्तमुन्मत्तं कृत्तिवाससम् ॥
2.5.m: the agitator of the three worlds, the covetous, the hunter, the destroyer of sacrifice, / accompanied by the sons of the Kṛttikās, the ecstatic one, clothed in animal skins,

2.5.s:
gajakṛttiparīdhānaṃ kṣubdhaṃ bhujagabhūṣaṇam |
dattālambaṃ ca vetālaṃ ghoraṃ śākinipūjitam ||
2.5.d:
गजकृत्तिपरीधानं क्षुब्धं भुजगभूषणम् ।
दत्तालम्बं च वेतालं घोरं शाकिनिपूजितम् ॥
2.5.m: attired in elephant skin, agitated, adorned with serpents, / providing support, the Vetāla, fierce, worshipped by Śākinīs,

2.5.s:
aghoraṃ ghoradaityaghnaṃ ghoraghoṣaṃ vanaspatim |
bhasmāṅgaṃ jaṭilaṃ śuddhaṃ bheruṇḍaśatasevitam ||
2.5.d:
अघोरं घोरदैत्यघ्नं घोरघोषं वनस्पतिम् ।
भस्माङ्गं जटिलं शुद्धं भेरुण्डशतसेवितम् ॥
2.5.m: the un-terrible, the slayer of formidable daityas, of terrifying roar, the lord of the forest, / whose limbs are smeared with ashes, matted-haired, pure, attended by hundreds of Bheruṇḍas,

2.5.s:
bhūteśvaraṃ bhūtanāthaṃ pañcabhūtāśritaṃ khagam |
krodhitaṃ niṣṭhuraṃ caṇḍaṃ caṇḍīśaṃ caṇḍikāpriyam ||
2.5.d:
भूतेश्वरं भूतनाथं पञ्चभूताश्रितं खगम् ।
क्रोधितं निष्ठुरं चण्डं चण्डीशं चण्डिकाप्रियम् ॥
2.5.m: the lord of spirits, the master of beings, dwelling in the five elements, moving through the sky, / angered, cruel, fierce, the lord of Caṇḍī, beloved of Caṇḍikā,

2.5.s:
caṇḍaṃ tuṅgaṃ garutmantaṃ nityamāsavabhojanam |
lelihānaṃ mahāraudraṃ mṛtyuṃ mṛtyoragocaram ||
2.5.d:
चण्डं तुङ्गं गरुत्मन्तं नित्यमासवभोजनम् ।
लेलिहानं महारौद्रं मृत्युं मृत्योरगोचरम् ॥
2.5.m: fierce, exalted, winged, ever enjoying liquor, / licking with his tongue, exceedingly terrible, death itself, inaccessible to death,

2.5.s:
mṛtyormṛtyuṃ mahāsenaṃ śmaśānāraṇyavāsinam |
rāgaṃ virāgaṃ rāgāndhaṃ vītarāgaśatārcitam ||
2.5.d:
मृत्योर्मृत्युं महासेनं श्मशानारण्यवासिनम् ।
रागं विरागं रागान्धं वीतरागशतार्चितम् ॥
2.5.m: the death of death, of vast armies, dwelling in cremation grounds and forests, / passion, dispassion, blinded by passion, worshipped by hundreds of the passionless,

2.5.s:
sattvaṃ rajastamodharmamadharmaṃ vāsavānujam |
satyaṃ tvasatyaṃ sadrūpamasadrūpamahetukam ||
2.5.d:
सत्त्वं रजस्तमोधर्ममधर्मं वासवानुजम् ।
सत्यं त्वसत्यं सद्रूपमसद्रूपमहेतुकम् ॥
2.5.m: sattva, rajas, tamas, righteousness, unrighteousness, the younger brother of Indra, / truth and untruth, real form, unreal form, causeless,

2.5.s:
arddhanārīśvaraṃ bhānuṃ bhānukoṭiśataprabham |
yajñaṃ yajñapatiṃ rudramīśānaṃ varadaṃ śivam ||
2.5.d:
अर्द्धनारीश्वरं भानुं भानुकोटिशतप्रभम् ।
यज्ञं यज्ञपतिं रुद्रमीशानं वरदं शिवम् ॥
2.5.m: the Lord who is half woman, the sun, radiant as hundreds of millions of suns, / the sacrifice, the lord of sacrifice, Rudra, Īśāna, the boon-giver, Śiva.

2.5.s:
aṣṭottaraśataṃ hyetanmūrtīnāṃ paramātmanaḥ |
śivasya dānavo dhyāyan muktastasmānmahābhayāt ||
2.5.d:
अष्टोत्तरशतं ह्येतन्मूर्तीनां परमात्मनः ।
शिवस्य दानवो ध्यायन् मुक्तस्तस्मान्महाभयात् ॥
2.5.m: Meditating thus on these one hundred and eight forms of the supreme soul, / Śiva, the dānava was freed from that great terror.

2.5.s:
divyenāmṛtavarṣeṇa so'bhiṣiktaḥ kaparddinā |
tuṣṭena mocitaṃ tasmācchūlāgrādavaropitaḥ ||
2.5.d:
दिव्येनामृतवर्षेण सोऽभिषिक्तः कपर्द्दिना ।
तुष्टेन मोचितं तस्माच्छूलाग्रादवरोपितः ॥
2.5.m: Sprinkled by the matted-haired god with a heavenly shower of nectar, / he was released by the pleased [deity] and taken down from the tip of the trident.

2.5.s:
uktaścātha mahādaityo maheśānena so'ndhakaḥ |
asuraḥ sāntvapūrvaṃ yatkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ mahātmanā ||
2.5.d:
उक्तश्चाथ महादैत्यो महेशानेन सोऽन्धकः ।
असुरः सान्त्वपूर्वं यत्कृतं सर्वं महात्मना ॥
2.5.m: Then that great daitya Andhaka, the asura, / was addressed by the great lord with soothing words, having performed all [this], the great-souled one.

2.5.s:
īśvara uvāca |
bho bho daityendra tuṣṭo'smi yamena niyamena ca |
śauryeṇa tava dhairyeṇa varaṃ varaya suvrata ||
2.5.d:
ईश्वर उवाच ।
भो भो दैत्येन्द्र तुष्टोऽस्मि यमेन नियमेन च ।
शौर्येण तव धैर्येण वरं वरय सुव्रत ॥
2.5.m: The Lord said: / 'O chief of daityas, I am pleased with your restraint and discipline, / with your valor and your fortitude. Choose a boon, O one of noble vows!

2.5.s:
ārādhitastvayā nityaṃ sarvanirdhūtakalmaṣaḥ |
varado'haṃ varārhastvaṃ mahādaityendrasattama ||
2.5.d:
आराधितस्त्वया नित्यं सर्वनिर्धूतकल्मषः ।
वरदोऽहं वरार्हस्त्वं महादैत्येन्द्रसत्तम ॥
2.5.m: I, whose impurities are all washed away, have been constantly worshipped by you; / I am the giver of boons, and you are worthy of a boon, O best of great daitya chiefs!

2.5.s:
prāṇasandhāraṇādasti yacca puṇyaphalaṃ tava |
tribhirvarṣasahasraistu tenāstu tava nirvṛtiḥ ||
2.5.d:
प्राणसन्धारणादस्ति यच्च पुण्यफलं तव ।
त्रिभिर्वर्षसहस्रैस्तु तेनास्तु तव निर्वृतिः ॥
2.5.m: Whatever fruit of merit has accrued from your preservation of life / for three thousand years—by that let bliss be yours!'

2.5.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca |
etacchrutvāndhakaḥ prāha vepamānaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ |
bhūmau jānudvayaṃ kṛtvā bhagavantamumāpatim ||
2.5.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच ।
एतच्छ्रुत्वान्धकः प्राह वेपमानः कृताञ्जलिः ।
भूमौ जानुद्वयं कृत्वा भगवन्तमुमापतिम् ॥
2.5.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Hearing this, Andhaka, trembling, with folded hands, / placing both knees upon the ground, spoke to the blessed lord, the husband of Umā.

2.5.s:
andhaka uvāca |
bhagavanyanmayokto'si dīno hīnaḥ parātparaḥ |
harṣagadgadayā vācā mayā pūrvaṃ raṇājire ||
2.5.d:
अन्धक उवाच ।
भगवन्यन्मयोक्तोऽसि दीनो हीनः परात्परः ।
हर्षगद्गदया वाचा मया पूर्वं रणाजिरे ॥
2.5.m: Andhaka said: / 'O Blessed Lord, regarding that which was spoken by me—wretched, base, [yet addressing you as] the highest of the high— / with a voice choked with joy earlier upon the battlefield,

2.5.s:
yadyatkṛtaṃ vimūḍhatvātkarma lokeṣu garhitam |
ajānatā tvāṃ tatsarvaṃ prabho manasi mā kṛthāḥ ||
2.5.d:
यद्यत्कृतं विमूढत्वात्कर्म लोकेषु गर्हितम् ।
अजानता त्वां तत्सर्वं प्रभो मनसि मा कृथाः ॥
2.5.m: and whatever act, censured among the worlds, was committed out of bewilderment / by me not knowing you—O Lord, do not hold all that in your mind!

2.5.s:
